Novel Molecular Descriptors for ADME Prediction in Beyond Rule of Five Chemical Space
works.abstract: Abstract Beyond Rule of Five (bRo5) molecules, including proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs), macrocycles, and cyclic peptides, present challenges for conventional ADME prediction because their size, flexibility, polarity, and potential for intramolecular hydrogen bonding (IMHB) can influence solubility, membrane permeability, and downstream pharmacokinetics (PK). Here, we introduce molecular descriptors designed to encode structural features relevant to bRo5 chemical space, including long-range IMHB potential and macrocyclic topology. We also developed predictive models for three experimentally derived physicochemical properties relevant to bRo5 behavior: EPSA, ChromLogD, and ChameLogK. These descriptors and predicted properties were incorporated into machine-learning models for multiple ADME endpoints, including solubility, permeability, plasma protein binding, and intrinsic clearance. Models incorporating expanded bRo5 chemical space showed improved performance for bRo5 compounds relative to previous models. The effects of the updated ADME models were evaluated in high-throughput physiologically based pharmacokinetic (HTPK) simulations. For two PROTAC case studies not included in model training, use of the updated models produced PK predictions that were generally closer to reported experimental observations. Together, these results demonstrate the utility of computationally efficient descriptors of long-range IMHB potential and related structural features for extending ADME modeling into bRo5 chemical space and illustrate how improved representation of these properties can propagate to predictions of in vivo PK.

works.title: Optimization of the Arg8−Arg9 Cleavage Site in 68Ga-Labeled Neurotensin(6−13) Analogs for NTSR1-Targeted PET Imaging of Cancer
works.abstract: Abstract Neurotensin receptor 1 (NTSR1) is overexpressed in many cancers and represents a promising target for PET imaging. Neurotensin (NT)-derived radiopharmaceuticals targeting NTSR1 have been widely investigated; however, their clinical translation is limited in part by rapid proteolytic degradation, particularly at the Arg8−Arg9, Pro10−Tyr11, and Tyr11−Ile12 peptide bonds. In this study, we focused on optimizing the Arg8−Arg9 cleavage site through the incorporation of non-canonical amino acids to improve metabolic stability while maintaining high receptor affinity. A series of 16 DOTA-conjugated NT(6−13) analogs containing modifications at Arg8 and/or Arg9 were synthesized by solid-phase peptide synthesis. The natGa-labeled analogs were evaluated in PC-3 cells using a competition binding assay with [125I-Tyr3]Neurotensin, and compounds with Ki values < 5 nM were selected for 68Ga-radiolabeling, PET imaging, biodistribution, and in vivo stability studies. Ga-SK01033 (Phe(3-guanidine) at Arg8) and Ga-SK02040 (NMe-Orn(Me)3 at Arg8) demonstrated Ki values of 3.35 ± 0.32 and 4.34 ± 1.16 nM, respectively. Both peptides were labeled with 68Ga in 35.0−60.9% decay-corrected radiochemical yields, >108 GBq/μmol molar activity, and >97% radiochemical purity. Despite good binding affinity, [68Ga]Ga-SK01033 exhibited poor in vivo stability and negligible tumor uptake (<1 % ID/g at 1 h p.i., no intact tracer detected at 15 min p.i.). In contrast, [68Ga]Ga-SK02040 displayed improved metabolic stability, with 70.3 ± 5.11% intact tracer at 15 min p.i., resulting in tumor uptake of 11.1 ± 2.64 % ID/g at 1 h p.i. and 9.39 ± 2.64 % ID/g at 3 h p.i. Co-injection of excess natGa-SK02040 reduced tumor uptake by 91.2%, confirming NTSR1-mediated targeting. Overall, these findings demonstrate that while Phe(3-guanidine) substitution improves binding affinity without enhancing stability, incorporation of NMe-Orn(Me)3 at Arg8 simultaneously enhances affinity and metabolic stability, resulting in higher tumor uptake and tumor-to-non-target contrast than previously reported [68Ga]Ga-DOTA-NT-20.3. The present study establishes NMe-Orn(Me)3 as a favorable Arg8 modification that enables the development of NT(6−13)-based PET tracers with improved in vivo performance for targeting NTSR1.

works.title: Post-Packaging pH-Responsive Peptide Conjugation Enhances Productive Transduction by Antibody-Guided Adeno-Associated Viral Vectors
works.abstract: Abstract Adeno-associated virus vectors are widely used for gene delivery, yet their functional efficiency is limited by multiple intracellular bottlenecks. Here, we develop a modular vector engineering strategy that combines antibody-guided cellular entry with site-specific capsid modification to enhance post-entry processes. By systematically introducing surface-exposed cysteine residues into a heparan sulfate-binding-deficient capsid, we identify a permissive position that enables efficient chemical conjugation without compromising capsid assembly while revealing strong serotype-dependent constraints on capsid engineering. Using this optimized backbone, we implement antibody-guided delivery and conjugate a membrane-inserting peptide through polyethylene glycol linkers to enhance the post-entry efficiency. Peptide conjugation significantly increases transgene expression across multiple cell types without increasing viral uptake, indicating improved intracellular processing. Dose−response analyses further reveal a threshold-dependent behavior, in which functional enhancement becomes evident only above a critical vector input, a phenomenon consistently observed across distinct antigen−antibody pairs and extended to therapeutic transgenes. Together, these findings define a flexible and generalizable capsid modification strategy that improves productive transduction independently of intrinsic capsid tropism and provides a practical framework for next-generation gene delivery vectors.

works.title: Glucose-Responsive Promoter Engineering for Dynamic Regulation of Insulin Transgene Expression Delivered by Non-Viral Gene Therapy
works.abstract: Abstract Diabetes mellitus treatment currently relies on externally administered insulin, which lacks the precise glucose-responsive regulation of pancreatic β-cells. This study develops a synthetic glucose-responsive gene expression system using repeated glucose-responsive elements (R3G) to regulate insulin production in non-pancreatic cells. The R3G element, derived from carbohydrate response elements (ChoREs) of the liver pyruvate kinase promoter, was incorporated upstream of minimal promoters to create glucose-inducible constructs with low basal activity. Plasmid (pDNA) constructs were generated using the pGM206 backbone containing either reporter genes or a furin-cleavable human insulin cDNA (hsoINSfur). pDNA was delivered into HepG2 cells using the non-viral Glycosaminoglycan-binding Enhanced Transduction (GET) nanoparticle system. Glucose responsiveness was evaluated using Gaussia luciferase (GLuc) assays and a dual secreted reporter system incorporating secreted embryonic alkaline phosphatase (SEAP) as an internal normalisation control. Among the promoters tested, R3G-miniCMV and R3G-SCP1 demonstrated strong glucose-dependent activation while maintaining low basal expression. R3G-miniCMV produced the greatest dynamic range, showing up to ∼24-fold induction under hyperglycaemic conditions (25 mM glucose) relative to hypoglycaemic/glucose-free conditions. Dual-reporter assays confirmed that increased GLuc activity was due to glucose-responsive transcription rather than variations in transfection efficiency or cell viability/metabolism. Replacement of reporter genes with hsoINSfur demonstrated functional insulin secretion, with R3G-containing constructs producing significantly higher C-peptide levels under elevated glucose conditions compared with non-R3G controls. Overall, this study demonstrates that synthetic R3G promoters can confer robust glucose-responsive insulin expression in non-pancreatic cells using a safe non-viral delivery platform, providing a proof-of-concept system for future glucose-regulated insulin gene therapy applications.

works.title: A Portable N-Terminal Biphenyl Motif in LL-37 Enhances the Activity of Short Human Cathelicidin Derivatives
works.abstract: Abstract Issues such as potency and stability limit our ability to realize the potential of host defense peptides to serve as new antibiotics. Informed by our prior structure−activity work, we demonstrate that transposition of an N-terminal biphenyl motif from full-length LL-37 onto the previously-described central activity region (residues 18−29) improves activity against Gram-negative bacteria by >16-fold. We further improve upon this lead derivative, termed FF-14, using stabilizing modifications such as d-amino acids and C-terminal amidation as well as selected N-lipidation moieties and demonstrate the transferability of biphenyl motif activity to longer cathelicidin scaffolds. Mechanistic interrogation reveals that the biphenyl pharmacophore increases both inner and outer membrane permeabilization while promoting a helical structure in the 14-mer without directly impacting peptide stability. Inclusion of the LL-37 biphenyl motif is thus a portable strategy for augmenting short cathelicidin activity and better approximating the activity profile of LL-37 itself in short sequences.

works.title: Combinatorial Synthesis and Direct-to-Biology Antibacterial Evaluation of Ruthenium(II) and Iridium(III) N^O -Schiff−Base Complexes
works.abstract: Abstract Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) represents a major global health challenge, compounded by a limited antibiotic discovery pipeline and restricted chemical diversity among clinically used antibiotics. Metal-based complexes offer promising antimicrobial agents owing to their structural diversity and unique modes of action. Here, we report the synthesis and biological evaluation of two combinatorial libraries comprising 176 novel ruthenium(II) p-cymene (RuCy) and iridium(III) Cp* (IrCp) N^O-Schiff-base complexes. Syntheses used a robust three-step, room-temperature methodology, with automated LC−MS characterization enabling Direct-to-Biology screening. Against Staphylococcus aureus, 50−80% of compounds inhibited growth, whereas no significant activity was observed against Escherichia coli. Three leads exhibited MICs of 1.56−12.5 μM against Gram-positive pathogens, therapeutic indices exceeding 15, and negligible haemolysis. Mechanistic studies suggest that IrCp-B5, incorporating the ligand (E)-2-bromo-4-chloro-6-(((naphthalen-2-ylmethyl)imino)methyl)phenol, disrupts membrane associated processes, while RuCy-J3, incorporating (E)-1-((cyclohexylimino)methyl)naphthalen-2-ol, targets intracellular DNA-related pathways. This work demonstrates the utility of Direct-to-Biology approaches for accelerated antimicrobial lead identification and prioritization.

works.title: Design, Synthesis, and Evaluation of 99mTc-Labeled PSMA-Targeting Dimeric Tracers: Comparison of Glutamate−Urea−Lysine (EuK) and Aminoadipic Acid−Urea−Lysine (AuK) Targeting Groups
works.abstract: Abstract In clinical practice of prostate cancer (PCa) management, the high renal uptake of prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA)-targeted radiotracers remains a significant concern. To address this challenge, the study systematically evaluated molecular modification strategiestargeting moieties, linker types, and coligand compositionsfor their effects on tracer pharmacokinetics. Among candidates, [99mTc]Tc-EuK2-LPRO-HYNIC-EDDA was the most promising for single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) imaging. It binds PSMA stably with nanomolar affinity (Kd = 16.28 nM), and the high blocking efficiency in vitro and in vivo subsequently confirmed excellent targeting specificity. The tracer cleared rapidly from nontarget organs, effectively mitigating renal accumulation and giving high target-to-background ratios. Crucially, high-contrast SPECT/CT images obtained 2−6 h post-injection indicate clinical promise for routine and delayed PCa imaging. Additionally, density functional theory (DFT) and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations provided critical theoretical insights into coordination structure, ligand−protein interaction mechanisms, and correlations between conformational differences and biological activity.

works.title: Development and Preclinical Evaluation of 68Ga-Labeled BCMA-Targeting Nanobodies for PET Imaging of Multiple Myeloma
works.abstract: Abstract B-cell maturation antigen (BCMA) is a critical biomarker for multiple myeloma (MM). In this study, three 68Ga-labeled BCMA-targeting nanobodies (C02, C06, and C07) were developed and evaluated. Protein-based binding assays showed apparent nanomolar affinities, with dissociation constants of 58 ± 7 nM, 87 ± 9 nM, and 33 ± 3 nM, respectively. Their BCMA specificities were confirmed by the high BCMA-positive H929 cell uptakes (6.08 ± 0.73%, 4.59 ± 0.45%, and 4.05 ± 0.29% at 0.5 h, respectively) and significant inhibition (82%, 88%, and 66%, respectively) by the unlabeled nanobodies. [68Ga]Ga-NOTA-BCMA-C07 exhibited the most favorable profile in microPET/CT imaging, with tumor uptake of 3.26 ± 0.19% ID/g, renal uptake of 13.61 ± 1.90% ID/g, and tumor-to-muscle ratio of 7.46 ± 2.82 at 0.5 h post-injection (p.i.). These findings support [68Ga]Ga-NOTA-BCMA-C07 as a promising BCMA-targeted PET radiotracer with potential for further clinical translation.

A Dual SIRT6/Classical HDAC Inhibitor with Integrated Antiproliferative, Antimigratory, and Pharmacokinetic Advantages Against Pancreatic Cancer
works.abstract: Abstract Pancreatic cancer (PC) is highly malignant, with a poor prognosis and high metastatic potential. Given the synergy between sirtuin 6 (SIRT6) and classical histone deacetylase (HDAC) in regulating epithelial−mesenchymal transition (EMT), dual-target inhibitors may offer improved antimetastatic therapy. The lead compound 11e suffers from poor metabolic stability, weak antiproliferative activity, and insufficient antimigratory capacity. Through pharmacophore merging and structural optimization, we obtained S20, which potently inhibits SIRT6 (IC50 = 3.903 μM) and classical HDACs (IC50 = 0.217 μM). In vitro, S20 was superior to 11e in antiproliferative activity and showed stronger antimigratory activity than SAHA, 11e, or their combination. Mechanistically, S20 modulated EMT-associated marker expression, increasing E-cadherin while decreasing N-cadherin, vimentin, and ZEB1. Its intravenous half-life (4.11 h) was 14.7-fold longer than 11e (0.28 h). In vivo, S20 dose-dependently suppressed liver metastasis with favorable safety. In summary, S20 exhibits comprehensive advantages in antiproliferative, antimigratory, and metabolic stability, providing a new strategy for antimetastatic drug development.

works.title: Don’t Take It at Face Value: What Medicinal Chemists Should Ask of an X-ray Crystal Structure
Design, Synthesis and Evaluation of QuAOCOM-Linked Halogenated Phenazines as Potent Antibacterial and Biofilm-Killing Agents
works.abstract: Abstract Bacterial biofilms are surface-attached communities with enriched populations of non-replicating persister cells. As such, biofilms are credited as the underlying cause of chronic and recurring bacterial infections. Unlike free-floating, replicating planktonic bacteria that can acquire resistance to conventional antibiotic treatments, metabolically-dormant biofilm communities exhibit intrinsic tolerance to all classes of antibiotics. To address challenges associated with bacterial biofilms, our lab has identified halogenated phenazine (HP) small molecules that demonstrate outstanding antibacterial and biofilm-killing activities via iron starvation. Here, we report the design, chemical synthesis, and evaluation of a focused series of quinone alkyloxycarbonyloxymethyl(QuAOCOM)-linked HP prodrugs. During these studies, we found QuAOCOM-linked HPs 22 and 27 to demonstrate very good linker stability, rapid processing of the quinone trigger, improved water solubilities, potent antibacterial and biofilm eradication activities, and favorable cytotoxicity profiles. These studies highlight important features related to the design of HP prodrug conjugates which could have a significant impact addressing problems associated with antibiotic-tolerant biofilms.

Identification of Novel RORγt Inverse Agonist YW-089 as a Preclinical Candidate for the Treatment of Autoimmune Diseases
works.abstract: Abstract Retinoic acid receptor-related orphan receptor γt (RORγt) is a key regulator of IL-17-producing T helper 17 (Th17) cell differentiation and an attractive target for autoimmune diseases. Although RORγt inverse agonists have shown clinical promise, identifying candidates with both high potency and favorable drug-like properties remain challenging. We previously reported the carboxyl-containing biaryl urea compound 3i, which reduced psoriasis severity in mice but exhibited poor microsomal stability and suboptimal pharmacokinetics (38% oral bioavailability in mice). Herein, optimization of sulfone-containing biaryl ureas led to the discovery of compound 4 (YW-089), a potent and selective RORγt inverse agonist (RORγ FRET IC50 = 27 nM; mTh17 IC50 = 140 nM). YW-089 demonstrated markedly improved metabolic stability across species (t1/2 > 145 min), favorable pharmacokinetics in mice, rats, and dogs (oral bioavailability 66%, 65%, and 73%, respectively), and robust efficacy in imiquimod- and IL-23-induced psoriasis mouse models, supporting its further preclinical development for autoimmune diseases.

works.title: AI-Augmented Medicinal Chemist: Skillsets for Resolving Uncertainty in the AI-Assisted Drug Discovery Era
Beyond AlphaFold 3: a standardised benchmark of open-source co-folding models for antibody–antigen complexes, from docking accuracy to interaction specificity
works.abstract: Hs) from SAbDab2-Bench, a newly curated dataset, and a reconstructed antibody-antigen subset of FoldBench, Ab-FoldBench. Using standardized inputs, sampling, and interface metrics that isolate the antibody-antigen interface, we compare docking accuracy, inference-time scaling, confidence-based candidate structure selection and sensitivity to interaction perturbations. OpenDDE achieved the highest median DockQ and docking pass rate, followed by Protenix-v2, although their difference was not statistically significant. Both models outperformed AlphaFold 3 on these measures, alongside offering fewer licensing restrictions on model and prediction use. We further find that model confidence was generally effective at identifying accurate predictions but showed model-dependent variations. To probe interaction specificity, which is essential for antibody design, we generated decoys through non-conservative interface mutations, and non-cognate antigen shuffling. Confidence decreased for both perturbations, but more consistently for non-cognate antigens than for interface mutations, with OpenDDE retaining comparatively high confidence for many decoys. Overall, Protenix-v2 combined high docking accuracy with strong rejection of perturbed interfaces, OpenDDE achieved the highest docking accuracy, albeit at the longest runtime, while ESMFold2-fast offered the fastest inference for large-scale triage. These results provide an up-to-date guidance framework for selecting and configuring co-folding models in antibody discovery, design, and engineering.

Normalized membrane ratio of TROP2 as a predictor of clinical outcomes with datopotamab deruxtecan in non-small-cell lung cancer
works.abstract: Datopotamab deruxtecan (Dato-DXd)-a trophoblast cell surface antigen 2 (TROP2)-directed antibody-drug conjugate-has demonstrated efficacy in patients with advanced nonsquamous non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) ± actionable genomic alterations. However, TROP2 expression by pathologist assessment using conventional immunohistochemistry with visual scoring does not predict response to TROP2-directed antibody-drug conjugates in NSCLC. We developed TROP2 quantitative continuous scoring (QCS)-a fully supervised computational pathology approach that quantifies TROP2 expression in individual NSCLC cells and subcellular components from immunohistochemistry-stained slides. Using QCS to determine TROP2 expression at the tumor cell membrane and cytoplasm, normalized membrane ratio (NMR) was developed (ratio of membrane relative to membrane + cytoplasmic TROP2) in the biomarker-evaluable population of patients with advanced NSCLC in the TROPION-PanTumor01 study (n = 115). The TROP2 NMR cut-point was optimized and validated in patients with nonsquamous NSCLC without actionable genomic alterations (primary intended-use population, n = 221) in the biomarker-evaluable population (n = 352) of the TROPION-Lung01 trial. Association with clinical outcomes was assessed. Progression-free survival was longer in Dato-DXd-treated (median 7.2 versus 4.0 months; hazard ratio 0.40, 95% confidence interval 0.25-0.64) but not docetaxel-treated (median 4.1 versus 4.4 months; hazard ratio 0.94, 95% confidence interval 0.59-1.49) patients with TROP2 NMR-positive versus TROP2 NMR-negative samples (treatment by biomarker status interaction P = 0.0098), indicating that TROP2 NMR may be a predictive biomarker for Dato-DXd.

works.title: Lessons from recent investigator-initiated trials of gene-editing therapies in China
Frequency of pharmacogenomic variation and medication exposures among participants in the All of Us Research Program
works.abstract: Pharmacogenomics promises improved outcomes through individualized prescribing. However, the lack of diversity in pharmacogenomics studies impedes clinical translation and the application of precision medicine across populations. We evaluated the frequencies of variants in 16 pharmacogenes ( ABCG2 , CACNA1S , CYP2D6 , CYP2C Cluster , CYP2C19 , CYP2C9 , CYP3A5 , CYP4F2 , DPYD , G6PD , NUDT15 , RYR1 , SLCO1B1 , TPMT , UGT1A1 , and VKORC1 ) and predicted phenotypes and medication exposures using whole-genome sequencing and electronic health record data from nearly 100,000 All of Us Research Program participants. We report that 100% of participants carried at least one pharmacogenomic variant and nearly all (99.5%) had a predicted phenotype with prescribing recommendations. Clinical impact was high with 24.4% of participants having both an actionable phenotype for these pharmacogenes and a prior exposure to an impacted medication with pharmacogenomic prescribing guidance. Importantly, we report thousands of previously unrecognized pharmacogene variants and hundreds of alleles and predicted phenotypes that deviate from known frequencies across populations or were previously unreported, especially in the Americas and African ancestry groups.

works.title: Sleep-like slow waves during wakefulness are associated with hallucinations and poorer cognition in Parkinson’s disease
works.abstract: Slow waves during sleep are fundamental for neural homeostasis, metabolic regulation, and waste clearance and are known to be altered in neurodegenerative diseases. Sleep-like slow waves (SLSWs) have been observed in awake, healthy individuals, where they are linked to fluctuations in vigilance and mind-wandering. Whether SLSWs are altered in Parkinson's disease (PD), and whether such alterations contribute to psychiatric or cognitive complications, remains unknown. In a cohort of 84 nondemented patients with PD and 30 healthy older adults, we found that SLSWs occurred more frequently in patients with PD. Hallucinatory traits in patients with PD were associated with higher SLSW amplitude, especially over frontocentral regions. Moreover, more prominent SLSWs were associated with poorer cognitive functions. We conclude that, whereas slow waves during sleep have positive physiological functions, exacerbated diurnal SLSWs may reflect responses related to PD neuropathology, at the cost of hallucinations and reduced cognitive function.

works.title: Erratum for the Research Article “Preclinical and clinical evaluation of systemic danegaptide for the treatment of nonproliferative diabetic retinopathy”
Albumin-bound paclitaxel–induced stromal reprogramming drives resistance to neoadjuvant chemotherapy in patients with pancreatic cancer
works.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is a highly lethal malignancy for which neoadjuvant chemotherapy with albumin-bound paclitaxel combined with gemcitabine (AG) is a standard first-line approach for borderline resectable and locally advanced disease. However, secondary resistance to this regimen is common, and its underlying mechanisms remain poorly defined. In this study, we investigated how neoadjuvant AG therapy shapes the tumor stroma in PDAC. Single-cell transcriptomics of patient tumors revealed that AG treatment induces a phenotypic switch of cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) from myofibroblastic (myCAF) to inflammatory (iCAF) states and identified a previously unrecognized TMEM100 + CAF subset enriched in nonresponders. Mechanistic studies showed that albumin-bound paclitaxel activates IL-2–STAT5 signaling to drive TMEM100 expression and that TMEM100 + CAFs promote chemoresistance through paracrine secretion of amphiregulin (AREG) and activation of tumor EGFR signaling. Genetic ablation of TMEM100 + CAFs in mouse models reversed CAF switching and enhanced the antitumor efficacy of AG therapy. These findings map chemotherapy-induced CAF plasticity, reveal a TMEM100-AREG axis of resistance, and highlight TMEM100 + CAFs as a promising target to sensitize PDAC to neoadjuvant treatment.

works.title: Dual inhibition of TNF-α and IL-1β signaling through BIG2 ameliorates osteoarthritis in mouse and primate models
works.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA), a leading cause of disability, is characterized by chronic low-grade inflammation and metabolic dysregulation in chondrocytes. TNF-α and IL-1β are key inflammatory drivers in OA pathogenesis, but clinical trials targeting them individually have been unsuccessful, highlighting the potential need for dual-targeting strategies. By screening a US Food and Drug Administration-approved drug library, we identified dabigatran, a thrombin inhibitor, as a potent dual suppressor of TNF-α and IL-1β signaling that restored chondrocyte metabolism. In preclinical OA models, including both mice and cynomolgus macaques, dabigatran attenuated cartilage degeneration, alleviated pain, and improved joint function. To elucidate the molecular mechanisms, we performed biochemical copurification coupled with mass spectrometry, identifying brefeldin A-inhibited guanine nucleotide-exchange protein 2 (BIG2) as a previously unknown dabigatran-binding target. Mechanistically, dabigatran binds to BIG2, promoting BIG2-dependent TNFR1 release to dampen TNF-α signaling while enhancing BIG2-mediated IL-1R1 degradation through the autophagy-lysosome pathway to limit IL-1β effects. These findings establish BIG2-mediated receptor trafficking and membrane dynamics as a regulatory node that concurrently inhibits TNF-α and IL-1β signaling, suggesting this pathway as a potential therapeutic strategy for OA.

works.title: Human antibody combinations determined by epitope mapping of orthopoxvirus A33/A35 confer therapeutic protection in mice
works.abstract: Human infections with mpox virus (MPXV) since 2022 have resulted in more than 188,000 cases reported globally as of June 2026, highlighting the urgent need for effective therapeutics. Here, we recruited smallpox vaccinees and donors with incidental vaccinia virus (VACV) exposure and isolated a panel of human anti-A33/A35 monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) from the latter using recombinant MPXV A35 as a cross-reactive bait. These mAbs recognized four distinct nonoverlapping epitopes (epitopes 1 to 4) and one composite epitope (epitope 3 + 4) on MPXV A35 and exhibited cross-reactivity against multiple orthopoxviruses (OPXVs). Cryo-electron microscopy structural analysis revealed that the high-affinity epitope 3 + 4 mAb HD15 engages an epitope at the A35 dimer interface that is conserved across OPXVs. Combinations of mAbs targeting nonoverlapping epitopes mediated synergistic, Fc-dependent neutralization in vitro; conferred therapeutic protection against lethal VACV challenge; and reduced viral burden and disease severity after MPXV challenge in mice. Together, these findings establish a single-antigen, multiepitope strategy for the development of broadly protective therapeutics against OPXVs.

works.title: Osimertinib, platinum, and etoposide for patients with metastatic EGFR / TP53 / RB1 -mutant lung cancers at risk for histological transformation
works.abstract: Although EGFR inhibitors are highly effective for treating EGFR- mutant lung adenocarcinomas ( EGFR + LUADs), resistance inevitably emerges, with histologic transformation to small cell lung cancer (SCLC) representing a particularly aggressive mechanism. Our prospective trial enrolled patients with EGFR + LUAD at high risk of transformation ( TP53 / RB1 -deficient) and treated them with first-line osimertinib combined with platinum and etoposide. Despite the addition of SCLC-directed chemotherapy, nearly half of patients (5 of 11) underwent SCLC transformation, with median progression-free survival of 11 months and overall survival of 33 months. Genomic and single-cell transcriptomic profiling of patient samples revealed clinical and subclinical plasticity associated with TP53 / RB1 comutations, including histological transformation to SCLC, as well as mesenchymal and squamous histologies. These changes in plasticity were linked to progressive disruption of the RB pathway, leading to altered chromatin accessibility and induction of neuronal differentiation and epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition transcriptional programs, further intensified by osimertinib treatment. These findings provide insights into the role of plasticity in mediating drug tolerance.

works.title: Editorial Board
RiboGreen-Based Encapsulation Efficiency Measurement for Lipid Nanoparticles: Evaluation of Total RNA Assay and Surrogate-Matrix Correction of Free RNA Fluorescence Bias
works.abstract: Abstract The RiboGreen fluorescence assay is widely utilized to determine mRNA encapsulation efficiency (EE %) in lipid nanoparticle (LNP) formulations by separately quantifying free and total mRNA, but both measurements often exhibit high variability and inconsistent performance, compromising accurate EE % measurement. We evaluated each assay using both LNP and targeted lipid nanoparticles (tLNP) formulations to identify root causes of poor performance. The total RNA assay performed acceptably, with %CV below 13% and inter-run recovery of 92−113% as assessed using nanoparticles with known mRNA concentration and different ionizable lipids, confirming complete RNA−lipid dissociation under Triton X-100 lysis. Progressive fluorescent signal decay was observed in the free RNA assay during prolonged incubation, highlighting the importance of an optimal time window for plate reading. More strikingly, the free assay yielded a systematic underestimation of over 30% when calibrated in conventional Trizma-EDTA (TE) buffer, inflating apparent EE % irrespective of dilution factor. Parallelism testing revealed that the calibration curve in TE buffer failed to match the responses in the sample matrix, attributable to nanoparticle-mediated fluorescence attenuation. Substituting the TE calibration buffer with empty nanoparticles (LNPs without mRNA) as a surrogate matrix restored inter-day spike-in recovery to 84−102% across 1−10% spike levels with %CV ≤ 18% at the lower limit of quantitation (LOQ), enabling accurate EE % reporting up to 99%. Matrix-matched calibration is therefore essential for reliable EE % determination and represents a broadly applicable solution for method qualification.

works.title: Novel CXCR4-Targeted Radioligands with Improved Tumor Uptake and Therapeutic Efficacy
works.abstract: Abstract Radioligands targeting the C-X-C Chemokine Receptor 4 (CXCR4) are promising for the diagnosis and therapy of multiple tumor types. The therapeutic efficacy of radiopharmaceutical therapy can be enhanced by albumin binders, which modulate the plasma half-life of radioligands and can increase tumor uptake. We report a novel class of CXCR4-targeting radioligands conjugated to non-covalent albumin binders with improved tumor uptake and prolonged tumor retention in a lymphoma model. Four 4-phenylbutyric acid (4-PBA) derivatives with p-MeO, p-Cl, p-Br, or p-I substituents were selected as albumin-binding motifs and coupled to a novel CXCR4-binding cyclic peptide. All non-radioactive standards were obtained with high purity (>95%) and showed high specific binding to CXCR4 as measured by the radioligand competition assay. Four peptides were labeled with [177Lu]LuCl3, with >94% radiochemical purity. Biodistribution and longitudinal SPECT imaging studies showed that variations in albumin binder substituents modulated the plasma half-life of CXCR4-targeting radioligands and improved tumor uptake. [177Lu]Lu-6, a peptide coupled to a 4-BrPBA albumin binder, showed high tumor uptake and tumor-to-organ ratios optimal for therapeutic studies. [177Lu]Lu-6 tumor uptake reached 23.6 ± 4.57% injected activity per gram (% IA/g) at 24 h post-injection, with persistent uptake (12.3 ± 2.04 % IA/g) after 120 h. Blood and kidney uptake were 0.28 ± 0.03 and 1.14 ± 0.08 % IA/g at 24 h, respectively. In a therapy study, [177Lu]Lu-6 (15, 30, and 60 MBq) resulted in potent tumor growth inhibition and increased overall survival in a Z138 xenograft model in comparison to the control and [177Lu]Lu-Pentixather groups (p < 0.05). Novel CXCR4 radioligands coupled to albumin binders demonstrated high and prolonged tumor uptake in a CXCR4-expressing tumor model. [177Lu]Lu-6 achieved an excellent balance between maximizing tumor uptake while keeping the blood residence time sufficiently short to avoid excessive exposure to normal organs.

works.title: The Human ADME Score: Quantifying the ADME Performance of Oral Therapeutics
works.abstract: Abstract Quantifying ADME-related drug-likeness is challenging as drug discovery expands into larger, more complex molecules. We developed the human ADME Score to assess oral drug-likeness through functional ADME properties, positioned between molecular descriptors and clinical pharmacokinetic outcomes. The continuous score (0−1) integrates experimental or machine-learning-predicted solubility, passive permeability, free hepatocyte intrinsic clearance, P-gp efflux, and plasma fraction unbound using Softmin-5, balancing minimum and average values. Datasets of 32,307 nonclinical and 588 clinical compounds with over 123 thousand ADME measurements were used for the construction and evaluation. Scores were higher in clinical than nonclinical compounds and varied across projects, target classes, and chemotypes. The score achieved the highest observed correlation and discrimination among evaluated comparators, supporting compound comparison and prioritization. Endpoint scores highlight potential ADME liabilities. Current application is best supported for molecules ≤1000 Da, reflecting chemical representation and assay validity.

works.title: Why Breakthrough Drug Discovery Platforms Need Decades to Mature: Lessons from FBDD, DEL, Aptamers, and PROTACs
works.abstract: Abstract Breakthrough hit-finding platforms rarely become routine after the first novel proof-of-concept and realistically take 20−30 years to develop fully. Across FBDD, DEL, Aptamer, and PROTAC drug discovery technologies, the persistent rate-limiting issue in platform development is not the founding concept alone (e.g., chemistry) rather, it is often more likely due to organizations underestimating the time to develop a robust technique in-house and the significant supporting infrastructure and talent required to transform novel technologies into routine hit-finding drug discovery platforms. A consequence for not being “all in” on its development can be a dilution of effort across programs that may lead to fewer clinical candidates and a decrease in ROI. As a result, it can take decades not years to develop a platform. Using lessons learned from these four platforms, this Perspective identifies key (and often unappreciated) hurdles that each new technology needs to resolve before becoming a mainstream hit-finding drug discovery platform driving FDA approvals.

works.title: Generative AI-Driven Interpolation of Cross-Family Kinase Space: Discovery of Dual-Targeting Degraders of IRAK4 and TYK2
works.abstract: Abstract Bridging structural discontinuities between disparate protein families is a fundamental challenge in multi-target design. We present a generative artificial intelligence (AI) platform for the non-linear interpolation of cross-family kinase space to simultaneously modulate innate (interleukin-1 receptor-associated kinase 4, IRAK4) and adaptive (tyrosine kinase 2, TYK2) immunity. Utilizing a variational autoencoder−recurrent neural network (VAE−RNN) model within the POLYGON framework, we successfully navigated high-dimensional latent space through an iterative “sampling−scoring−refocusing” strategy. This approach bypassed the geometric limitations of traditional pharmacophore merging, leading to the rational discovery of a novel spirocyclic scaffold with significant structural novelty (Tanimoto similarity <0.45). Integration of WaterMap-based optimization and proteolysis-targeting chimera (PROTAC) conjugation yielded C-8-014, a potent dual-target degrader achieving nanomolar potency and efficient degradation of both kinases. This study demonstrates a validated closed-loop methodology for navigating “unreachable” regions of the kinome, providing a paradigm-shifting approach for cross-family chemical design and a powerful molecular tool for chemical biology.

works.title: Design of High-Affinity Mini-Protein Drug Conjugates Targeting TROP2
works.abstract: Abstract Accurate and effective treatment of solid tumors has long been a core issue in cancer therapy. Antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) represent a crucial breakthrough in precision oncology. Traditional ADCs rely on monoclonal antibodies generated through animal immunization, followed by screening, sequencing, and recombinant expressiona process that is experimentally complex and costly. In this study, we employed deep learning-based computational design methods to design mini-protein binders targeting the tumor-associated antigen TROP2. The designed TROP2 mini-protein binder exhibited high specificity and thermal stability. The binding affinity was optimized from 40.4 nM to 628 pM through partial diffusion. On this basis, we engineered the mini-protein binder by conjugating it with the microtubule inhibitor VcMMAE, thereby constructing mini-protein drug conjugates (MPDCs) that can specifically target and kill TROP2-positive tumor cells. A comprehensive assessment of the anti-tumor efficacy of these MPDCs was performed using cancer cell lines, organoid models, and mouse xenograft models.

works.title: Design and Synthesis of Novel Mitochondria-Targeted HDAC3 Inhibitors for the Treatment of Obesity
works.abstract: Abstract Obesity is closely associated with mitochondrial dysfunction, which impairs fatty acid oxidation and energy metabolism, yet currently available HDAC3 inhibitors have not been optimized to address these metabolic abnormalities. Herein, we developed a series of mitochondria-targeted HDAC3 inhibitors by incorporating a TPP moiety into the classical HDAC pharmacophore. Structure-based optimization identified H18 (IC50 = 45.4 nM) as the most promising candidate, exhibiting potent HDAC3 inhibitory activity together with preferential mitochondrial localization. H18 effectively suppressed lipid accumulation during 3T3-L1 adipocyte differentiation while restoring intracellular ATP levels and reducing oxidative stress. In diet-induced obese mice, H18 produced dose-dependent reductions in body weight gain, improved glucose tolerance, and insulin sensitivity and exhibited superior efficacy to BG45. Collectively, these findings identify H18 as a promising antiobesity lead compound and support the integration of mitochondrial targeting capability into HDAC3 inhibitor design as a promising strategy for obesity intervention.

works.title: Narrow-Spectrum Oxadiazole Antibacterials that Target Cell−Wall Septation in Clostridioides difficile and Spare the Gut Microbiota
works.abstract: Abstract Recurrence of infection is a challenge in treatment of Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI), observed in 25% of patients. The first-line antibiotics disturb the gut microbiota, exacerbating the already disrupted commensal gut homeostasis and allow for C. difficile colonization. Narrow-spectrum antibiotics are critical for selective targeting of C. difficile while preserving beneficial gut flora, thereby mitigating recurrence. Our study investigates a novel class of highly selective, nitroimidazole-based oxadiazole antibacterials. We detail the chemical basis for their exceptional selectivity against C. difficile over commensal bacteria and elucidate their mechanism of action. Oxadiazole 2 inhibits penicillin-binding proteins 1 and 3 involved in septal peptidoglycan biosynthesis during vegetative cell division. We further demonstrate by whole-genome sequencing that treatment of mice with oxadiazole 2 does not disrupt the gut microflora and confers an impediment to colonization by C. difficile. This work is foundational for development of a new generation of narrow-spectrum therapeutics to combat CDI.

works.abstract: M olecular Pharmaceutics is excited to announce a Call for Papers for a Special Issue titled "Vaccine Adjuvant Process, Formulation, and Characterization."This Special Issue is dedicated to highlighting cutting-edge pharmaceutical science that translates complex immunological concepts into stable, manufacturable, and safe vaccine products.Vaccines remain one of the most profound achievements in global public health.However, as the field shifts toward highly purified subunit, recombinant, and synthetic antigens to improve safety profiles, these antigens often suffer from reduced immunogenicity.This necessitates the use of advanced adjuvant systems.The landscape of adjuvants has rapidly expanded beyond traditional aluminum salts to include complex, multiphase systems such as lipid-based nanoparticles, liposomes, and emulsions incorporating specialized immunostimulants of various modalities.While these complex adjuvant systems represent the frontier of preventative and therapeutic vaccines, they introduce profound physicochemical and engineering challenges.Navigating component interactions, maintaining critical quality attributes during manufacturing, and ensuring long-term stability require rigorous innovation.This Special Issue seeks to capture advances across the entire continuum of adjuvant developmentfrom early-stage adjuvant formulation design optimization to continuous manufacturing technologies and occupational safety.We invite original research articles, communications, perspectives, and comprehensive reviews (by invitation or proposal only) that fit within the scope of Molecular Pharmaceutics and highlight exciting developments in adjuvant science.Submissions are encouraged in the following thematic areas, but not limited to:Formulation Science & Design

works.title: Monoclonal Antibody-Based Near-Infrared Cancer Phototheranostics: Emerging Strategies and Translational Perspectives
works.abstract: Abstract Monoclonal Antibody-Based Near-Infrared Cancer Phototheranostics have emerged as a versatile platform for cancer phototheranostics by integrating antigen-specific targeting with spatiotemporally controlled imaging and therapy. Conjugation of monoclonal antibodies (mAb) with NIR-responsive photosensitizers enables selective tumor localization and light-triggered cytotoxicity, thereby minimizing off-target toxicity while enhancing therapeutic precision. Despite promising preclinical outcomes, clinical translation remains constrained by limited intratumoral penetration of macromolecular constructs, heterogeneous antigen expression, and restricted light delivery to deep-seated tumors. Additional challenges, large-scale manufacturing, and regulatory complexity further hinder widespread clinical adoption. This review provides a critical analysis of recent advances in NIR-based antibody phototheranostics, with emphasis on rational design parameters such as antibody selection, photosensitizer engineering, and conjugation strategies. Emerging approaches, including nanocarrier-assisted delivery, tumor microenvironment modulation, and immune checkpoint-directed combination therapies, are discussed in the context of enhancing therapeutic and translational potential. Finally, future directions focusing on activatable and tumor microenvironment-responsive probes, exploration of the NIR-II window, and optimized irradiation strategies are highlighted as key avenues to bridge the gap between preclinical promise and clinical translation.

works.title: From Site-Specific Conjugation to Linker−Payload Presentation: Lessons from AJICAP and Exo-Linker for Antibody−Drug Conjugate Pharmaceutical Design
works.abstract: Abstract The therapeutic activity and pharmacokinetics of antibody−drug conjugates (ADCs) depend on antibody specificity, payload potency, and the attachment and surface presentation of the linker−payload. Linker−payload presentation denotes the spatial arrangement and local chemical environment of the linker−payload on the antibody. Conjugation site, drug-to-antibody ratio (DAR), release chemistry, and manufacturability are therefore interdependent design variables. This perspective examines AJICAP second-generation site-specific conjugation and Exo-Linker chemistry as approaches to controlling linker−payload presentation. AJICAP enables control of the conjugation site on native immunoglobulin G (IgG) antibodies without antibody sequence engineering, whereas Exo-Linker chemistry illustrates how linker−payload reconfiguration can alter hydrophobic exposure and off-target enzymatic processing. The central argument is that the conjugation site and linker−payload presentation should be evaluated together using orthogonal analytical, pharmacokinetic, stability, and manufacturability readouts. We propose matched site-by-linker comparisons to distinguish these contributions and guide the balance between systemic stability, intracellular release, and manufacturability.

works.title: Glycosylation Shapes Isoform-Selective Recognition of Flavonoids by Human Glucose Transporters
works.abstract: Abstract Human glucose transporters (GLUTs) are pharmacologically relevant membrane proteins interacting with diverse flavonoids, yet previous studies focused largely on individual isoforms and limited ligand sets. Here, we docked 207 flavonoids against all 14 human GLUT isoforms, complemented by microscale thermophoresis (MST) and membrane-embedded molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. Docking revealed heterogeneous interaction profiles associated with differential glycosyl accommodation, distinguishing broad glycosylated flavonoid−preferring (gly-flav−preferring; e.g., GLUT1) and aglycone-biased (agly-flav−biased; e.g., GLUT3) groups. Glycosyl size generally outweighed attachment position, with gly-flav−preferring GLUTs tending to favor larger glycosides and agly-flav−biased GLUTs showing weaker or less favorable responses to glycosyl enlargement. Consistently, MST revealed enhanced GLUT1 binding for selected diglycosides relative to monoglycosides. MD further showed more favorable calculated binding energies for GLUT1 than GLUT3, with size predominating in GLUT1 and position contributing more prominently in GLUT3. Together, these findings highlight glycosylation as a context-dependent determinant of GLUT−flavonoid recognition.

works.title: Unbiased, Target-Agnostic Platform for the Synthesis and Screening of PROTAC Libraries
works.abstract: Abstract Most approaches to PROTAC discovery require prior knowledge of the protein target, limiting the scope of targetable biology. Here we report an unbiased, direct-to-biology platform for the high-throughput synthesis and phenotypic screening of PROTAC libraries. The platform employs the Ugi multicomponent reaction to couple diverse carboxylic acid-containing ligands with VHL-recruiting E3 ligase ligand−linker conjugates in a single well plate step, followed by solid-phase extraction and cell-based phenotypic screening without predetermined target selection. A pilot library derived from seven structurally diverse protein ligands was screened in a cell viability assay against six cancer cell lines, yielding potent and selective hits. Global proteomics identified BRD4 as the primary target of lead compound B5, a BI2536-derived VHL-recruiting degrader that exhibited single-digit nanomolar degradation potency (DC50 = 4.9 nM, Dmax = 96%) and complete selectivity for BRD4 over PLK1. Target engagement and ternary complex formation were confirmed by NanoBRET, Western blot, and Boltz-2 computational modeling. The modularity of the Ugi reaction further enabled direct synthesis of two photoaffinity labeling probes, PALTAC-1 and PALTAC-2, which confirmed BRD4 as a direct binding target via photocrosslinking and pull-down experiments. This platform enables the unbiased discovery of degrader drugs and their targets from phenotypic screens and provides a generalizable framework for converting existing compound libraries into functional PROTAC collections.

works.title: Interpretable multimodal network analysis of lipid‐lowering therapies
works.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Multimodal integration of clinical and omics data could clarify the hepatic mechanisms of lipid-lowering therapies, but interpretable methods for heterogeneous data remain limited. The objective was to apply interpretable multimodal networks (IMNs), a topology-aware framework that condenses heterogeneous omics and clinical data into compact, cross-modal modules, to characterize treatment-specific hepatic responses to simvastatin and ezetimibe. EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: In the Stockholm Study, patients scheduled for cholecystectomy were randomized for 4 weeks to simvastatin, ezetimibe, their combination or placebo. We integrated liver transcriptomics and DNA methylation with plasma/bile biochemistry, including lipoprotein functionality, on the human protein-protein interactome to build treatment-specific IMNs and evaluated selected network-derived predictions in a human hepatocyte-like model (SOAT2-only-HepG2). KEY RESULTS: IMNs reduced dimensionality while preserving network topology, producing distinct molecular signatures for simvastatin, ezetimibe and combination therapy that mapped to different biological processes; the placebo network was less multimodal and more fragmented. IMNs highlighted apolipoprotein-centred modules and predicted drug effects on APOA2, PPARA and PTPRS, linked to plasma C-peptide. In SOAT2-only-HepG2 cells, selected predictions were supported experimentally, including APOA2 induction and ezetimibe-associated PTPRS upregulation. CONCLUSIONS AND IMPLICATIONS: IMNs provide a practical, interactome-based route from multimodal patient data to focused, testable hypotheses about lipid-lowering therapies, yielding compact features suitable for downstream predictive modelling while retaining biological interpretability.

Resistance exercise to attenuate lean mass loss during tirzepatide therapy for obesity: a randomized controlled trial
works.abstract: Incretin mimetics as obesity therapy induce substantial weight and fat loss but also decrease lean soft tissue mass, possibly impairing skeletal muscle function. Here, in this two-arm randomized controlled trial of adding resistance exercise (REx) to tirzepatide (T), 120 adults with overweight or obesity were treated with tirzepatide and randomized to thrice-weekly resistance exercise training or usual activities for 40 weeks. Tirzepatide was safe, and most participants tolerated up-titration to 15 mg weekly. Adherence to resistance exercise was 91%. Weight loss achieved was similar (T = -22.61 kg, T+REx = -22.28 kg, P = 0.694). For primary outcomes, loss of total fat mass was similar (T = -17.19 kg, T+REx = -17.98 kg, P = 0.700; between-group difference = -0.77 kg, 95% confidence interval (CI): -2.14 kg to 0.60 kg), but resistance exercise reduced loss of total lean soft tissue mass (T = -4.67 kg, T+REx = -3.57 kg, P < 0.001; between-group difference = 1.09 kg, 95% CI: 0.43-1.75 kg). For related endpoints, resistance exercise reduced loss of appendicular lean soft tissue mass (T = -3.55 kg, T+REx = -2.92 kg, P < 0.001). Upper and lower body muscle strength decreased with tirzepatide (bench press -4.09 kg, lat pulldown -4.42 kg, knee extension -4.42 kg) but increased with T+REx (+4.68 kg, +8.58 kg, +5.88 kg, respectively, all P < 0.001 versus tirzepatide). In conclusion, resistance exercise training attenuated loss of total lean soft tissue mass, representing an effective adjunct to tirzepatide anti-obesity therapy. Australian New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry identifier: ACTRN12623001236684 .

works.title: An ulcerative colitis taxonomy defined by individual patient-reported response trajectories
works.abstract: Abstract A barrier to precision medicine for ulcerative colitis (UC) is the inability to predict and mechanistically explain treatment responses. Using patient-reported outcomes (PROs) from a phase 3b comparative trial of 768 participants, we identified four distinct patient response-trajectory groups for vedolizumab (anti-integrin) and adalimumab (antitumor necrosis factor). Validation in a second phase 3 trial of 576 participants linked PRO-defined vedolizumab trajectories to long-term disease complications. Bulk, single cell, and spatial transcriptomics and proteomics identified vascular inflammation as associated with vedolizumab nonresponse through interactions between SPP1 + macrophages and endothelial cells. In two separate real-world cohorts of 4,981 and 3,854 patients with UC, concomitant use of renin–angiotensin system inhibitors (modulators of vascular inflammation) was associated with reduced long-term complications for vedolizumab but not anticytokine therapies. These findings define a response-trajectory-based taxonomy that requires prospective validation for clinical utility and applications for selecting vedolizumab combination therapy in UC.

works.title: Oxidation Mechanisms and Control Strategies in Peptide and Protein Formulations
works.abstract: Abstract Oxidation represents an important chemical degradation process in formulations of therapeutic peptides and proteins. Potential consequences of peptide and protein oxidation are loss of efficacy, aggregation and/or immunogenicity. Depending on the oxidant(s) present or generated in pharmaceutical formulations, oxidation can target any amino acid, though preferred oxidation targets are the aromatic and sulfur-containing amino acids. The rational development of stable peptide and protein formulations would be greatly assisted by a detailed mechanistic understanding of protein oxidation processes in these formulations. This review will provide an overview about oxidation mechanisms relevant for pharmaceutical peptide and protein formulations. It will cover oxidation mechanisms of peptide and protein amino acids as well as processes which may lead to the formation of oxidants in pharmaceutical formulations, together with a mechanistic analysis of potential mitigation strategies.

works.title: ABCB1, ABCG2, and CES1 are Key Determinants of the Pharmacokinetics of KRASG12C Inhibitor Divarasib
works.abstract: Abstract Divarasib is a selective KRASG12C inhibitor currently in phase 3 trials for treatment of NSCLC. Drug transporters and metabolic enzymes can markedly influence oral drug disposition. We therefore examined whether the efflux transporters ABCB1 and ABCG2, the influx transporter OATP1, and the enzymes CYP3A and CES1 affect the plasma and tissue distribution of divarasib. Using genetically modified cell lines and mouse models, we assessed transporter- and enzyme-mediated effects on divarasib pharmacokinetics. Transepithelial transport assays, oral pharmacokinetic studies, and ex vivo esterase assays were performed to evaluate divarasib transport, plasma exposure, tissue distribution, metabolism, and protein binding. Divarasib was efficiently transported by hABCB1, mAbcb1a, hABCG2 and mAbcg2 in vitro. Abcb1a/b−/− and Abcb1a/b;Abcg2−/− mice displayed a >4-fold increase in plasma exposure and 7.1- to 16-fold higher brain-to-plasma ratios compared to wild-type mice. Small intestinal content-to-plasma ratios were significantly reduced in Abcb1a/b−/− and Abcb1a/b;Abcg2−/− mice. Coadministration of the dual ABCB1/ABCG2 inhibitor elacridar in wild-type mice increased divarasib plasma exposure to the level seen in Abcb1a/b;Abcg2−/− mice, but only modestly enhanced brain penetration. Oatp1a/b deficiency did not alter divarasib pharmacokinetics, and neither mCyp3a nor hCYP3A4 affected its oral availability. Ces1 ablation strongly decreased divarasib plasma exposure, suggesting binding to plasma Ces1c. Accordingly, divarasib inhibited plasma Ces1c-mediated hydrolysis of 4-nitrophenyl acetate. Increased tissue concentrations in Ces1−/− mice further suggested decreased hydrolysis of divarasib by (non-Ces1c) Ces1 enzymes, or compensatory downregulation of other divarasib clearance process(es). The obtained pharmacokinetic insights may support optimization of divarasib clinical application, efficacy and safety, and highlight potential drug−drug interaction risks.

Lipid-Modified CGRP Receptor Antagonists: Balancing Pharmacokinetic Improvement and Potency Loss
works.abstract: Abstract Lipidation is a promising strategy for enhancing peptide stability by reducing proteolytic degradation and prolonging systemic exposure. In this study, we systematically evaluated lipid motifs varying in lipid chain length and PEG spacer composition, combined with peptide N-terminal modifications, using a 10-mer calcitonin gene-related peptide receptor antagonist to optimize a candidate for migraine treatment. Incorporation of a C18 diacid lipid motif increased the in vivo (mouse) half-life to 3.5 h. Although lipidation improved serum stability in a size-dependent manner, it was accompanied by a reduction in receptor antagonism, highlighting the balance between pharmacokinetic enhancement and biological activity. These findings improve our understanding of the trade-offs involved in lipidated peptide design and support future optimization strategies. In addition, we developed a rapid, inexpensive, and HPLC-compatible assay for quantifying peptide binding to human serum albumin, overcoming limitations of conventional equilibrium dialysis methods, including non-specific membrane binding, lengthy equilibration times, and peptide degradation.

works.title: Discovery of F73, a New Generation RET Inhibitor Overcoming RET Gatekeeper (V804M) and Solvent-Front (G810C/R) Mutations
works.abstract: Abstract Pharmacological invention of RET offers a compelling strategy to treat patients harboring RET fusions or mutations. Selective RET inhibitors, including pralsetinib and selpercatinib, have demonstrated substantial clinical benefits. However, this efficacy is often compromised by the occurrence of resistance, particularly RET solvent front mutations G810C/R. To address this problem, we performed a systematic structure−activity optimization based on our reported RET inhibitors. Our efforts yielded F73, a next generation RET inhibitor with potent activity against RET mutations including V804M and G810C/R. F73 effectively suppressed RET phosphorylation and downstream SHC activation in Ba/Fa3 cells harboring various RET resistance mutations. Furthermore, it induced apoptosis and cell-cycle arrest in a dose-dependent manner in CCDC6-RET and CCDC6-RET-G810R Ba/F3 cells. Notably, F73 exhibited robust antitumor efficacy in Ba/F3-RET-G810R xenograft models, outperforming selpercatinib, thus supporting its potential to overcome resistance mediated by RET gatekeeper (V804M) and solvent-front (G810C/R) mutations.

works.title: Broad-Spectrum Antimicrobial Peptide Designed from the Mycobacterium tuberculosis Adenylate Kinase Structure, Inspired by Its LPS/LTA Dual Recognition
works.abstract: Abstract Broad-spectrum therapeutics targeting multidrug-resistant (MDR) Gram-negative and Gram-positive pathogens remain limited. Utilizing structural insights from Mycobacterium tuberculosis adenylate kinase (MtAdk), which uniquely recognizes both lipopolysaccharide (LPS) and lipoteichoic acid (LTA), we designed broad-spectrum antimicrobial peptides. Through incorporation of non-natural amino acids, terminal acylation, and arginine extension, we developed a lead candidate, YK-mAK-17, with remarkable stability, minimal resistance development, and broad-spectrum activity, particularly against carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (CRAB) and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA). Mechanistic studies revealed an amphipathic α-helix with N-terminal C6 acylation that enhances membrane engagement, driving rapid bactericidal activity via multimodal disruption of membrane integrity and virulence pathways. In septic shock mouse models induced by CRAB and MRSA, YK-mAK-17 significantly improved survival and reduced organ damage. By combining MtAdk-inspired dual LPS/LTA recognition with targeted chemical modifications, YK-mAK-17 represents a promising antimicrobial candidate possessing broad-spectrum antibacterial and anti-inflammatory properties, highlighting the potential of structure-guided peptide design for addressing MDR infections.

works.title: Autonomous Drug Design via Workflow Agents: Integrating Chemical Semantics and Tool-Oriented Automation
works.abstract: Abstract Large language model (LLM)-based agents have shown promise in automating scientific tasks, yet existing systems for drug discovery often lack strategic, cross-step planning, and multi-objective coordination. Here, we present drugflow-skills, an LLM-driven agent framework that abstracts key drug design operations, including virtual screening, de novo molecule generation, molecular optimization, and multi-target design, into composable and reusable skills. The agent operates under a ReAct paradigm, executing iterative “Thought → Action → Observation” loops while interfacing with the DrugFlow backend. Across five representative tasks targeting ALK, ROS1, and IGF-1R, the agent demonstrates autonomous decision-making, cross-step planning, and multi-objective trade-offs, achieving improved predicted binding scores while reducing predicted toxicity and off-target liabilities. It also provides interpretable rationales and adapts strategies based on human feedback, enabling a human-agent co-optimization loop. These results support dynamic reasoning-driven drug design.

α‐tocopherol (Vitamin E) inhibits second mitochondria‐derived activator of caspases (SMAC) mimetic‐induced cell death by directly targeting cIAP1 degradation
works.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Tocopherols (vitamin E) are well characterized as essential lipophilic antioxidant agents. However, recent evidence suggests that tocopherols may also regulate cellular signalling through direct interactions with specific protein targets. This study aimed to investigate the molecular mechanism by which α-tocopherol regulates programmed cell death and to identify its direct molecular target. EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: A high-throughput screen identified α-tocopherol as an inhibitor of TNF-α/SMAC-mimetic-induced cell death. The mechanism(s) underlying this action of α-tocopherol was investigated using western blotting, immunoprecipitation, ubiquitination assays, drug affinity responsive target stability, cellular thermal shift assay, isothermal titration calorimetry and molecular docking. Its efficacy, in vivo, was evaluated in a murine model of ulcerative colitis, induced by dextran sulphate sodium (DSS). KEY RESULTS: α-Tocopherol selectively inhibited TNF-α/SMAC-mimetic-induced cell death by directly and competitively binding to the BIR3 domain of the inhibitor of apoptosis protein-1 (cIAP1). This interaction stabilized cIAP1, prevented the formation of RIPK1-dependent death complexes and suppressed apoptosis and necroptosis. In a murine model of DSS-induced colitis, α-tocopherol significantly alleviated disease severity while preserving cIAP1 protein expression. CONCLUSION AND IMPLICATIONS: Our findings identified cIAP1 as a previously unrecognized molecular target of α-tocopherol and demonstrated that cIAP1 stabilization contributed to the suppression of RIPK1-dependent cell death. These findings expand the current understanding of the biological functions of tocopherols and provide a mechanistic basis for their potential therapeutic application in inflammatory diseases associated with aberrant cIAP1 degradation.

works.title: Design and Development of Lipid-Based In Situ Forming Long-Acting Injectables for Delivering a Highly Water-Soluble Drug at High Loading
works.abstract: Abstract Long-acting injectables (LAIs) have emerged as a pivotal modality for managing chronic diseases, driven by the need to improve patient adherence and overall quality of life. Most clinically established LAI products rely on either simple suspensions/solutions or polymer-based depot technologies designed for low-dose, hydrophobic active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs). In contrast, achieving long-acting delivery for high drug loading of hydrophilic drugs remains a significant challenge and represents a clear technological gap in the field. The present work focused on the design and development of lipid-based in situ-forming LAIs as a promising approach for the controlled release of a model hydrophilic API, paracetamol. The key formulation parameters including lipid composition, solvent selection and content, and drug loading were systematically studied to understand their influence on the microstructure of the depot formed, injectability, and the release kinetics of paracetamol. The formulations demonstrated good injectability and immediate formation of the highly viscous depot upon contact with aqueous fluids. A comprehensive physicochemical characterization of the blank and compound-loaded formulations pre- and post-injection was conducted using a range of analytical techniques including powder X-ray diffraction, small-angle X-ray scattering, proton nuclear magnetic resonance, rheological analyzer, and texture analyzer as well as imaging techniques cryogenic field emission scanning electron microscopy and cross-polarized light microscopy. The characterization data demonstrated the complex structures of the gels, due to the various lyotropic liquid crystalline phases formed in situ post-injection. In vitro drug release studies revealed the long-acting effect, and the best-performing formulation showed 96.6% paracetamol released after 77 days. Preliminary in vivo results in rats after subcutaneous administration of an ethanol/benzyl benzoate (1:4, w/w) formulation showed that paracetamol plasma concentrations peaked after nine days, while drug release remained incomplete at day 24. Histopathological assessment suggested minimal to mild injection-site findings two months after administration. The compound release rates were significantly affected by both drug loading and the ratios between water-miscible and water-immiscible solvents used in the formulation. The findings of this study present new insights into optimizing the use of lipid-based materials with ordered structures as LAIs for the delivery of hydrophilic compounds.

works.title: Lipid Nanoparticles for RNA Delivery to the Central Nervous System: Biological Barriers, Engineering Strategies, and Therapeutic Applications
works.abstract: Abstract Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) have emerged as an adaptable platform for the delivery of therapeutic RNA, as demonstrated by the clinical success of mRNA vaccines and RNA interference therapies. Despite this progress, translation of RNA LNPs to diseases of the central nervous system (CNS) remains challenging due to multiple biological barriers that restrict access to neural tissue and target cells. Beyond crossing the blood-brain barrier and related CNS interfaces, further obstacles include efficient tissue distribution, cell-specific uptake, and intracellular RNA delivery. This review summarizes CNS-relevant delivery routes, key anatomical and cellular barriers limiting therapeutic access to neural tissues, major therapeutic RNA modalities, and the chemical composition and design principles of LNPs. We further discuss engineering strategies developed to overcome these obstacles and highlight emerging therapeutic applications across neuro-oncology, acute CNS injury, and neurodegenerative disorders. Collectively, RNA LNPs demonstrate potential as a versatile carrier system for neurological disease. However, further advances in delivery strategies will likely be needed to improve brain access, distribution, cell-specific targeting, and intracellular RNA delivery across diverse CNS applications.

works.title: Correction to “Two-Step Design of Triazole-Stapled Opioid Agonists Exhibiting Potent and Prolonged Peripheral Analgesic Activity”
Small-Molecule Drugs for Glaucoma: IOP-Lowering, Neuroprotective and Multi-Target Strategies
works.abstract: Abstract Glaucoma, a leading cause of irreversible blindness worldwide, is primarily driven by elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) and retinal ganglion cell (RGC) apoptosis. Small-molecule agents, owing to their high target specificity and excellent ocular tissue penetration, remain the cornerstone of clinical management. This perspective evaluates recent advances in small-molecule glaucoma therapeutics and their pharmacological targets. We first outline the medicinal chemistry, structure−activity relationships (SAR), and clinical status of agents modulating aqueous humor (AH) dynamics, detailing targeted therapies. Given that disease commonly progresses to optic nerve degeneration despite well-controlled IOP, we further summarize developmental trends in neuroprotective molecules designed to directly slow disease progression. We also discuss the rationale, design strategies, clinical translational potential and limitations of dual/multi-target drugs and combination therapies. Collectively, this perspective provides a systematic reference and future outlook for developing next-generation, mechanism-informed therapies for precision glaucoma treatment.

works.title: Design, Synthesis, and Biological Evaluation of Indolin-2-one Derivatives as Novel Covalent Pan-FGFR Inhibitors for Overcoming Clinical Resistance
works.abstract: Abstract Oncogenic FGFR alterations drive the development of multiple cancers. However, acquired resistance to clinically approved inhibitors mediated by gatekeeper and molecular brake mutations poses a major therapeutic challenge. Herein, we describe the structure-based discovery of (Z)-3-(amino(phenyl)methylene)indolin-2-one derivatives as potent covalent pan-FGFR inhibitors. The representative compound, 9v, displayed high potency against FGFR1/2/3/4 (IC50 = 8.6, 5.4, 4.4, and 6.9 nM, respectively) and potent antiproliferative effects across a panel of FGFR-driven cancer cell lines (IC50 = 0.3−6.1 nM). Notably, 9v retained high efficacy against common resistance mutations, including the gatekeeper (FGFR1 V561M, FGFR2 V564F, and FGFR3 V555M) and “molecular brake” (FGFR2 N549K) variants, with IC50 values of <0.1 nM. Covalent modification of FGFR3 by 9v was confirmed through MALDI-TOF-MS and LC−MS/MS-based site mapping. Furthermore, 9v exhibited significant antitumor efficacy in an RT112/84 bladder cancer xenograft model, providing a promising strategy to overcome resistance in FGFR-targeted therapy.

works.title: Potent and Selective Caspase-2 Inhibitors: Biological Profiling, Structural Characterization, and Challenges of Molecular Instability
works.abstract: Abstract Caspase-2 (Casp2) has emerged as a promising therapeutic target for neurodegenerative diseases due to its role in pathological tau processing. Here, we designed and synthesized a series of 48 novel peptidomimetic Casp2 inhibitors organized into distinct structural classes. Compounds were evaluated for Casp2 inhibition and selectivity against Casp1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, and 10. Inhibitors Idc(hE)G(Dab)D-CHO (32) and Idc(hE)G((S)-Me-THIQ)D-CHO (33) exhibited low nanomolar potency and ≥537-fold selectivity over Casp3. These unprecedented scaffold modifications are consistent with preferred steric arrangements between the P2 and P3 positions. Biochemical assays demonstrated the blockade of tau truncation and impaired the formation of toxic Δtau314. High-resolution crystal structures of compounds 2 and 33 bound to Casp2 revealed binding interactions consistent with the observed SAR. Although Idc(hE)V((S)-Me-THIQ)D-CHO (3, MUR-65) showed favorable ADME and pharmacokinetic properties, limited membrane permeability, insufficient blood−brain barrier penetration, and P5 indoline instability remain key challenges for further development.

works.title: Enthalpy-Informed Design of Dasatinib-Derived Small-Molecule Inhibitors of Transthyretin Amyloidogenesis
works.abstract: Abstract Transthyretin (TTR) amyloidosis is driven by dissociation of the native tetramer into aggregation-prone monomers, making kinetic stabilization of the tetramer an established therapeutic strategy. Here, we demonstrate that binding enthalpy-guided optimization provides an effective strategy for developing selective TTR stabilizers. Starting from a kinase inhibitor-derived scaffold, stepwise optimization comprising scaffold simplification, terminal phenyl modification, and halogen substitution yielded compound 29, which exhibits aggregation inhibitory activity comparable to tafamidis and close to that of acoramidis. Isothermal titration calorimetry revealed that optimization predominantly improved binding enthalpy, while changes in binding free energy were modest. Combined X-ray and neutron crystallographic analyses suggested that the favorable enthalpy originates from enhanced shape complementarity and weak interactions rather than conventional hydrogen bonds. Importantly, compound 29 maintains robust binding to TTR in human plasma. These findings demonstrate that binding enthalpy can serve as a practical parameter for optimizing TTR amyloid inhibitors.

works.title: Design, Synthesis, and Evaluation of a Potent NLRP3 Inflammasome Inhibitor with Favorable Pharmacokinetic and Safety Profiles for Chronic Inflammatory Diseases
works.abstract: Abstract Persistent NLRP3 activation drives chronic inflammatory diseases, necessitating inhibitors with sustained exposure and tolerability. Rational optimization of the hydrophobic and solvent-exposed regions of MCC950 yielded sulfonylurea F34, which inhibited NLRP3-dependent IL-1β release (IC50 = 38.81 nM), with nanomolar potency similar to MCC950, without apparent NLRC4 or AIM2 inhibition. Docking predicted that F34 binds within the MCC950 pocket, where it generally remained during a 200 ns MD simulation. SPR confirmed direct NLRP3 binding (KD = 2.12 μM). In mice, F34 exhibited an oral half-life of 11.89 h and oral bioavailability of 91.36%, potentially contributing to greater efficacy than MCC950 in MSU-induced gouty arthritis and chronic DSS-induced colitis. F34 also showed better tolerability than MCC950 in acute high-dose and 14 day repeated-dose studies, together with weak hERG-channel inhibition (IC50 > 40 μM) and limited CYP inhibition. Thus, optimization preserved nanomolar cellular potency while improving oral exposure, in vivo efficacy, and preliminary tolerability.

works.title: Diverse Computational Strategies Enable the Discovery of p38α−MK2 Molecular Glues
works.abstract: Abstract Mitogen-activated protein kinase-activated protein kinase 2 (MK2) phosphorylates AU-rich element-binding proteins (AUBPs) that modulate the stability of cytokine mRNA. An emerging class of inhibitors creates a ternary complex between upstream kinase p38α and MK2. These molecular glues demonstrate sustained efficacy relative to orthosteric inhibitors of either p38α or MK2; however, their mechanism of action presents challenges to computationally driven design. Herein we describe in silico hit identification strategies leveraging free energy perturbation coupled with machine learning to triage and prioritize ligands from diverse chemical sources and identify multiple structurally diverse, potent, and highly selective p38α−MK2 molecular glues. Lead compounds 14 and 28 demonstrated an attractive PK profile with sufficient coverage of human whole blood EC50 and displayed pronounced reduction of TNFα levels after PO dosing in lipopolysaccharide mouse models, illustrating the value of our in silico hit identification strategies and optimization of non-degrading molecular glues.
