Rational Design and Preclinical Evaluation of LRP1-Targeted 68Ga-Labeled Angiopep-2 Peptides for PET Imaging of Hepatocellular Carcinoma
works.abstract: Abstract Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a heterogeneous malignancy lacking effective strategies for subtype-specific molecular imaging. Low-density lipoprotein receptor-related protein 1 (LRP1) is a multifunctional receptor implicated in HCC progression. Herein, we report the rational design and systematic comparison of three Angiopep-2-derived 68Ga-labeled radiotracers with distinct DOTA conjugation positions, aiming to elucidate how chelator placement modulates targeting specificity and in vivo imaging contrast for LRP1-positive HCC. Immunohistochemical analysis of an HCC tissue microarray confirmed LRP1 overexpression in 19.3% of clinical specimens, which correlated with poorer overall survival and defined a high-risk subgroup. All tracers exhibited high radiochemical purity, excellent stability, and favorable pharmacokinetic profiles. In vitro, 68Ga-DOTA-ANG-2 and 68Ga-DOTA-ANG-3 showed robust uptake in LRP1-high Huh-7 cells. Although 68Ga-DOTA-ANG-2 achieved the highest absolute tumor uptake, 68Ga-DOTA-ANG-3 demonstrated markedly reduced nonspecific hepatic accumulation, yielding a superior tumor-to-liver contrast (5.61 ± 1.33 at 120 min). MicroPET/CT imaging in subcutaneous and orthotopic HCC models verified that 68Ga-DOTA-ANG-3 enables sensitive and high-contrast detection of intrahepatic lesions. Collectively, 68Ga-DOTA-ANG-3 is a promising positron emission tomography (PET) agent for subtype-specific HCC imaging, supporting further evaluation of LRP1-targeted PET imaging in a biomarker-defined subset of HCC.

works.title: Hierarchical Bond Programming Enables Triphasic Chemotherapy from an Injectable Tumor-Responsive Hydrogel
works.abstract: Abstract Localized chemotherapy requires sustained yet dynamically regulated drug exposure to match the evolving therapeutic demands within solid tumors. However, existing hydrogel depots are predominantly governed by passive diffusion or single-trigger activation, limiting their ability to achieve spatiotemporally programmed drug release. Here, we report a hierarchically programmed injectable hydrogel platform that enables triphasic chemotherapy through orthogonal bond dissociation pathways. The system integrates physically encapsulated 6-mercaptopurine (6 MP) together with two polymeric prodrugs containing redox-responsive and hydrolytically labile linkages, thereby establishing sequential release processes governed by diffusion, glutathione-triggered cleavage, and bond hydrolysis. This multilevel release architecture enables immediate therapeutic intervention, tumor-microenvironment-activated intracellular drug liberation, and sustained intratumoral maintenance. The hydrogel exhibits excellent injectability, prolonged local retention, and sustained release behavior under tumor-associated conditions (>90% over 200 h). In colorectal tumor models, the hierarchically programmed system significantly enhanced intratumoral drug exposure, achieved 71% tumor inhibition, and reduced systemic toxicity compared with free-drug administration. By coupling orthogonal chemical activation with localized hydrogel delivery, this work establishes a generalizable strategy for spatiotemporally regulated chemotherapy through hierarchical bond programming.

works.title: Exploring Structure−Activity Relationships by Engineering Modified Thrombin Inhibitors from the Flea Xenopsylla cheopis
works.abstract: Abstract Engineering of post-translationally sulfated polypeptides from hematophagous organisms has shown promise for the development of novel anticoagulants with improved therapeutic potential. Here, we describe the development of a high-throughput peptide engineering workflow to facilitate rapid assembly of libraries of modified peptide analogues. Library members were designed from the privileged chimeric anticoagulant sulfo-XC43-Hiru, comprised of a peptide fragment of XC43 (from the rat flea Xenopsylla cheopis) and a sulfopeptide fragment of hirudin (from the medicinal leech, Hirudo medicinalis). Focus was placed on exploring the influence of non-native structural motifs through the incorporation of non-canonical amino acids at a number of strategic sites. The thrombin inhibitory activity and cleavage resistance of each analogue is profiled and provides valuable insight into the relationship between the sequence and biological activity of these molecules.

works.title: Discovery of Ebselen Analogs as Novel Inhibitors of Polyphosphate Metabolism to Attenuate Virulence and Show Combination Benefit with Meropenem in Pseudomonas aeruginosa
works.abstract: Abstract Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a major opportunistic pathogen responsible for severe hospital-acquired infections. The challenge in treating these infections is exacerbated by increasing antibiotic resistance. Polyphosphate kinases (PPKs), specifically PPK1 and PPK2, play a critical role in the virulence, stress response, and antibiotic tolerance of P. aeruginosa, making it a compelling target for therapeutic intervention. In this study, we describe the discovery and development of ebselen analogs as novel inhibitors against PPK1Pa and PPK2Pa. Biochemical and cellular assays revealed that ebselens interfere with the polyphosphate homeostasis within the bacterium. EB-1 and EB-18 treatment significantly reduced intracellular polyP levels, mirroring the phenotypic effects observed in Δppk strains, including impaired biofilm formation, reduced motility, and attenuated production of pyoverdine and pyocyanin. Notably, EB-1 and EB-18 showed combination benefit with meropenem against P. aeruginosa in the Galleria model, supporting their potential as an adjunctive agent to improve the antibacterial efficacy of meropenem. Most representative compounds, including EB-1 and EB-18, showed no detectable cytotoxicity in the tested mammalian cells. These findings underscore ebselen analogs as promising dual-specific PPK inhibitors, establishing a valuable strategy for the development of adjunct therapies via the PPK-mediated anti-virulence pathways.

works.title: Design, Synthesis, and Preclinical Evaluation of [18F]FPON, a First-In-Class PET Tracer Targeting Proliferating Cell Nuclear Antigen for Glioblastoma Imaging
works.abstract: Abstract Proliferating cell nuclear antigen (PCNA) is a central regulator of glioma stem cell maintenance and therapy resistance, yet no noninvasive method exists to visualize its expression in vivo. We developed [18F]FPON, a first-in-class small-molecule PET tracer targeting PCNA, derived from the clinical inhibitor AOH1996. FPON binds recombinant PCNA with a Kd of 900.8 ± 131.2 nM, comparable to AOH1996. [18F]FPON is synthesized in one step with a decay-corrected radiochemical yield of 11.43 ± 4.03% (n = 6) and >95% radiochemical purity, readily crosses the blood−brain barrier, and remains >87% intact in brain at 60 min post-injection. In orthotopic U87 glioma xenografts, [18F]FPON exhibits specific tumor uptake (SUVr = 2.58 ± 0.38 vs contralateral brain), which is significantly reduced by AOH1996 (SUVr = 1.62 ± 0.24, p < 0.01). These results establish [18F]FPON as a promising PET tracer for noninvasive imaging of PCNA and support its potential use as a companion diagnostic for PCNA-targeted therapies.

works.title: Precision/Locus-Selective G-Quadruplex Stabilization as the Next Medicinal Chemistry Challenge
works.abstract: Abstract G-quadruplexes (G4s) are druggable nucleic acid structures implicated in gene regulation and disease, but translating G4 ligands into medicines remains difficult because affinity for shared G-tetrad features can produce broad target engagement and obscure locus-specific mechanisms. This Perspective distinguishes topology selectivity from true genomic or transcriptomic selectivity and examines emerging strategies that add sequence addressability or induced proximity to G4 pharmacology. We discuss CRISPR-guided G4 modulation, G4-ligand-oligonucleotide conjugates, and RNA-targeting chimeras, together with earlier sequence-directed polyamide approaches and selective small-molecule precedents. We also consider medicinal chemistry parameters including ligand exit vector, linker architecture, charge, subcellular access, residence time, and off-target burden, and propose a staged validation workflow from biophysical profiling to locus-specific perturbation. We argue that programmable approaches are valuable complements to, rather than replacements for, optimized small-molecule G4 ligands.

works.title: Highlight on Pronidesivir (GS-441524): The First Approved Drug for the Treatment of Feline Infectious Peritonitis (FIP)
Synthesis of Amino-Functionalized Abasic Monomers as Versatile Building Blocks for siRNA Modification
works.abstract: Abstract Chemical modification plays a central role in optimizing siRNA therapeutics. Here, we designed and synthesized four amino-functionalized abasic phosphoramidite monomers (Ab1−Ab4) based on tetrahydropyrrole and aminocyclopentane scaffolds. Incorporation of these units destabilized siRNA duplexes in a position-dependent manner, and enhanced silencing activity at central or terminal positions on the sense strand, with the (S)-aminocyclopentane abasic (Ab4) exhibiting the strongest potency. Seed-region incorporation, particularly of the (R)-aminocyclopentane abasic (Ab3), mitigated miRNA-like off-target effects while retaining on-target activity in vitro. Following subcutaneous administration in mice, an Ab4-modified siRNA induced more potent hepatic mRNA knockdown than the parent siRNA at a single dose of 0.1 mg/kg, and Ab3 incorporation significantly reduced the number of off-target transcripts. In addition, 3′-terminal Ab4 incorporation improved nuclease resistance, leading to enhanced hepatic exposure in vivo, and served as a practical linker for conjugation. These findings establish amino-functionalized abasic units as a versatile platform for siRNA modification.

works.title: An inhibitor of the mitochondrial respiratory chain exerts synergistic anti‐tumour effects when combined with alkylating agents
works.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Cancer cells exhibit the Warburg effect, but oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) is also important for cancer cell proliferation. Metabolic reprogramming from glycolysis to OXPHOS is one mechanism of resistance to anti-tumour drugs. Here, we have synthesized and characterized OPB-111077, a novel, first-in-class orally available small-molecule compound, and investigated its anti-tumour activity and therapeutic potential in combination with alkylating agents. EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: Inhibition of mitochondrial function by OPB-111077 were assessed by measuring the oxygen consumption rate, ATP production and Complex I enzymatic activity. anti-tumour effects were evaluated in human haematological and solid tumour cell lines and in cell line-derived xenograft and lymphoma patient-derived xenograft models. Mechanistic studies included CRISPR screening, metabolomic analyses, and measurements of the oxygen consumption and extracellular acidification rates. Effects of OPB-111077 combined with alkylating agents were also assessed in mice. KEY RESULTS: OPB-111077 inhibited mitochondrial respiratory chain Complex I, suppressed OXPHOS, and exerted anti-tumour effects in several models. OPB-111077 demonstrated synergism with the alkylating agent bendamustine, with simultaneous inhibition of both OXPHOS and glycolysis. Bendamustine reprogrammed cancer cells into an OXPHOS-dominant state, thereby enhancing the efficacy of OPB-111077. CONCLUSION AND IMPLICATIONS: Based on these findings, we propose a novel anticancer therapeutic strategy of combining OXPHOS inhibitors with alkylating agents. OPB-111077 has demonstrated potential in combination therapy and was recently evaluated with bendamustine and rituximab in a Phase 1 clinical trial for patients with relapsed/refractory diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (NCT04049825).

works.title: Resolving melanoma heterogeneity at single‐cell resolution: implications for target discovery and therapy resistance
works.abstract: Melanoma is characterized by profound intra-tumoural heterogeneity and a complex tumour microenvironment (TME), which are primary drivers of therapy resistance. Conventional bulk sequencing lacks the resolution to capture these cellular nuances. Single-cell technologies, particularly single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and spatial multiomics, have fundamentally advanced our understanding of melanoma by enabling high-resolution characterization of malignant cell states, immune ecosystems and tumour microenvironment interactions. In this review, we summarize recent advances in single-cell multiomics studies of melanoma heterogeneity and therapy resistance, focusing on the identification of drug-tolerant persister states, immune escape mechanisms and resistance-associated cellular transitions. We further discuss how single-cell approaches facilitate target discovery, biomarker development and the rational design of combination therapies. By integrating multiomics profiling, computational modelling and pharmacological validation, these technologies provide a framework for translating cellular-level insights into precision therapeutic strategies. Finally, we highlight current challenges and future opportunities for clinical implementation of single-cell-guided approaches in refractory melanoma.

works.title: Triptonide alleviates sepsis‐associated acute lung injury by suppressing the STAT3/HIF‐1α‐mediated aerobic glycolysis in macrophages
works.abstract: Background and Purpose Sepsis‐associated acute lung injury (SA‐ALI), represents a major contributor to mortality among septic patients during the early hyperinflammatory phase. Triptonide, a diterpenoids extract from Tripterygium wilfordii Hook f has anticancer and contraceptive effects. However, its potential and mechanism in SA‐ALI are largely unknown. This study aims to evaluate the therapeutic efficacy and elucidate underlying mechanisms of triptonide in SA‐ALI to identify new clinical strategies. Experimental Approach Lipopolysaccharide (LPS)‐induced endotoxemia model or caecal ligation and puncture (CLP) model was used to induce SA‐ALI in mice, accompanied by treatment with triptonide, triptolide and 2‐methoxyestradiol. Parallel in vitro experiments involved LPS‐treated mouse primary macrophages cultured with or without triptonide. Transcriptomic sequencing of macrophages was performed to explore the anti‐inflammatory mechanisms of triptonide, which were further substantiated using specific activators, inhibitors and adeno‐associated virus (AAV)‐mediated gene targeting. Key Results Our data shows that triptonide effectively inhibits macrophage pro‐inflammatory activation, reduces pulmonary inflammation and alleviates SA‐ALI pathology (i.e. inflammatory cell infiltration, oedema and cell apoptosis), thereby improving the survival of septic mice. Transcriptomic sequencing combined with metabolic analysis shows that triptonide suppresses aerobic glycolysis in pro‐inflammatory macrophages by inhibiting the Signal Transducer and Activator of Transcription 3 (STAT3)/Hypoxia inducible factor‐1α (HIF‐1α) axis. Notably, the therapeutic efficacy of triptonide against SA‐ALI was abolished in myeloid cell‐specific HIF‐1α overexpressed mice (LyzM‐Cre DIO‐ hif1a mice). Conclusions and Implications Triptonide protects against SA‐ALI by suppressing the STAT3/HIF‐1α signalling axis, thereby inhibiting aerobic glycolysis‐mediated pro‐inflammatory macrophage activation, which suggests that triptonide is a promising therapeutic strategy for SA‐ALI.

works.title: Direct infusion intact mass spectrometry for rapid and sensitive characterization of antibody therapeutics in complex matrices
works.abstract: Native intact mass spectrometry (MS) is essential for resolving the structural heterogeneity of complex biotherapeutics. Traditionally, intact MS combines online chromatography (e.g. ion-exchange chromatography or size-exclusion chromatography). Here, we report an MS-centric, column-free direct infusion MS workflow that combines high-throughput off-line 96-well affinity purification with rapid and sensitive direct infusion MS. This approach achieves a sampling rate of ~1 min/sample with minimal sample consumption (<1 µL) and high sensitivity (detection of antibody drugs in the low µg/mL range). The method demonstrates excellent linearity (R2 ≥ 0.99) in the 1.953–500 µg/mL range, enabling relative quantitation and relative quality ranking across samples based on the deconvoluted MS signal. The utility of this direct infusion MS workflow is demonstrated through two case studies: 1) analysis of antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) stability and biotransformation in mouse serum, where direct infusion MS successfully tracked changes in drug-load distribution and average drug-to-antibody ratio; and 2) sensitive, high-throughput MS screening during early-stage bispecific antibody clone development. The workflow allows early detection of high-quality bsAb clones, providing results that show potential as an early indicator of drug quality in expanded fed-batch cultures. The serum stability study illustrates how this direct infusion MS workflow – despite being column free – can reveal critical product changes in highly complex sample matrices using a robust, rapid, and sensitive workflow. The established workflow uses commercially available instrumentation, reagents, and software, enabling easy implementation in biopharmaceutical analytical development and quality control laboratories.

Digital readiness for cardiovascular care in high-burden US communities with cardiology workforce constraints
Opposing microbiome-mediated axes link modifiable lifestyles to health and chronic diseases
works.abstract: Analyses disentangling the role of the gut microbiome in linking lifestyle factors to health outcomes remain limited. Here, using fecal shotgun metagenomics from 6,803 adults in the Japanese 4D cohort, we identified two opposing microbiome-mediated axes linking lifestyle to health and 15 diseases. A health-associated axis enriched in microbial metabolism of dietary components was linked to plant-based, soy and dairy intake. In contrast, a disease-associated axis, enriched in oral-derived bacteria and pathobionts, was linked to refined carbohydrates and sedentary behavior. Starter culture microorganisms used to ferment foods did not show statistically significant mediation of the observed health effects. Alcohol was associated with both health- and disease-oriented mediation patterns involving microbial host-glycan utilization. Microbiome-defined health- and disease-oriented mediator axes were supported by fecal short-chain fatty acids and plasma cytokines from >1,700 individuals, revealing butyrate-associated anti-inflammatory and pro-inflammatory host profiles, respectively. Microbiome-based prediction (MADE) scores captured lifestyle-microbiome-disease mediation patterns and distinguished individual diseases across 13 independent external cohorts from the United States, China, Sweden, Russia and Australia. We identify the gut microbiome as a key mediator linking lifestyle to health and disease, providing a framework for microbiome-based assessment to guide lifestyle interventions for health promotion and disease prevention.

works.title: Design and Synthesis of Metabolically Stable Tricyclic-SpiroLactams Inhibitors of Mycobacterium tuberculosis Type-II NADH Dehydrogenase: Structure−Activity and Structure−Property Relationship Studies
works.abstract: Abstract Tuberculosis (TB) remains a major global health threat, intensified by rising drug resistance. Tricyclic spirolactam (TriSLa) inhibitors targeting mycobacterial type II NADH dehydrogenases (Ndh/NdhA) represent a promising antibiotic class but previously suffered from poor metabolic stability. Through extensive structure−activity and structure−property optimization, we identified BDM91465, a potent and metabolically stable TriSLa analog. Cryo-EM analysis revealed its binding mode within the menaquinone pocket of Ndh, consistent with observed SAR trends. BDM91465 displayed favorable pharmacokinetics, including good bioavailability and low clearance, resulting in sustained exposure above its MIC. In vivo, BDM91465 significantly reduced Mycobacterium tuberculosis burden in mice, mirroring the phenotype of Ndh-2 genetic inactivation. These findings provide the first demonstration of Ndh-2 inhibition efficacy in a murine model, validating Ndh-2 as a druggable target and supporting further development of TriSLa-based regimen.

works.title: Refinement of Peptidomimetics toward MUR-2425: A Brain-Penetrant and Selective Caspase-2 Inhibitor with Enhanced Pharmacokinetics
works.abstract: Abstract Caspase-2 (Casp2) has emerged as a promising target for tau-associated neurodegenerative diseases, yet the development of potent, selective, and drug-like inhibitors remains challenging. Here, we report a systematic structure–activity relationship study of 80 novel covalent-reversible peptidomimetic Casp2 inhibitors, revealing key structural features of the Casp2 S2–S3 binding site and discovering (S)-2-methylindoline-2-carboxylic acid (2-Me-Idc) and quinaldic acid (Quin) as versatile and stable P5 scaffolds. One-step conversion of the aldehyde warhead into a nitrile remarkably enhanced selectivity while maintaning potency. The results culminate in MUR-2425 (87, (2-Me-Idc)(hE)VP*D-CN), a nanomolar Casp2 inhibitor (pKi (cpCasp2) = 7.75) with ≥525-fold selectivity over Casp1/3/4/5/6/7/9/10 and 24-fold over Casp8. MUR-2425 prevents the formation of neurotoxic Δtau314 in vitro, exhibits stable ADMET properties across human, rat, and mouse species and proves brain penetrance after subcutaneous injection in CD-1 mice. MUR-2425 is confirmed to engage Casp2 covalently by cocrystallization, supporting its further development for Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias.

works.title: Discovery of Quinoline-Based Highly Potent and Selective THRβ Agonists for MASLD Treatment
works.abstract: Abstract Metabolic-dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) is a progressive metabolic liver disease lacking sufficient clinical therapies. Thyroid hormone receptor β (THRβ), a liver-enriched nuclear receptor, is an attractive therapeutic target. Resmetirom, the first FDA-approved THRβ agonist for MASH, achieves clinical efficacy yet suffers from suboptimal THRβ/THRα selectivity restricting its therapeutic window. We used a scaffold-hopping strategy to design and synthesize a novel series of quinoline-based THRβ agonists. Systematic SAR optimization identified compound 24 as a potent, selective THRβ agonist, with an EC50 of 46.07 nM and 34.3-fold THRβ/THRα selectivity. It displayed favorable oral bioavailability (F = 54.1%) and approximately 2-fold higher hepatic exposure than Resmetirom. In animal models, compound 24 ameliorated metabolic dysfunction, reduced hepatic lipid accumulation, and suppressed liver inflammation and fibrosis. No obvious thyroid axis disruption or THRα-mediated cardiotoxicity was observed, and mice tolerated compound 24 up to 100 mg/kg. Overall, compound 24 represents a promising THRβ-selective therapeutic candidate for MASH.

works.title: Development of Potent METTL1 Inhibitors Using a Nanoscale Direct-To-Biology Strategy
works.abstract: Abstract The RNA methyltransferase METTL1/WDR4, which catalyzes N7-methylguanosine (m7G) modification in tRNA, has emerged as a key regulator of mRNA translation, and its dysregulation is associated with cancer development. Here, we report the development of a potent series of METTL1 inhibitors by combining conventional structure−activity relationship (SAR) studies with a tandem direct-to-biology (D2B) approach. Lead compound VK238 inhibited METTL1 enzymatic activity at nanomolar concentrations and exhibited selectivity across a panel of methyltransferases and kinases. In a cellular context, pharmacological METTL1 inhibition reduced m7G levels in tRNAs, leading to apoptosis-mediated cell death in several acute myeloid leukemia (AML) cell lines. Mechanistic studies combining biophysical experiments, photoaffinity labeling (PAL), and molecular docking suggested that this inhibitor series occupies the (S)-adenosylmethionine (SAM) binding pocket of METTL1. Collectively, these findings highlight METTL1 as a tractable and pharmacologically relevant target for therapeutic intervention in AML.

works.title: Correction to “Design, Synthesis, and Biological Evaluation of Indole Derivatives Targeting LsrK as AI-2 Quorum Sensing Inhibitors”
Correction to “Design, Synthesis, and Biological Evaluation of β-Trifluoroethoxydimethyl Selenides as Potent Antiosteoporosis Agents”
Compact Sulfonyl-γ-AApeptide Foldamers for Targeting Translation Initiation Machinery Assembly
works.abstract: Abstract Dysregulated cap-dependent translation is a hallmark of malignant transformation and progression, yet direct inhibition of the dynamic eIF4E−eIF4G protein−protein interaction remains challenging. Herein, we report the rational design of short helical sulfonyl-γ-AApeptide foldamers mimicking the eIF4G1 α-helical binding motif and directly engaging eIF4E. Structure-guided optimization, including stereochemical remodeling, afforded a compact, right-handed foldamer with remarkable proteolytic stability, submicromolar affinity for eIF4E, and potent inhibition of cap-dependent translation. Recognizing that cancer cells exploit enhanced lysosome-centered signaling and trafficking programs to sustain cap-dependent translation, we repurposed this oncogenic dependency as an intracellular delivery route to release the translation inhibitor. The optimized conjugate suppresses ferritin translation, triggers lipid peroxidation and ferroptosis, and exhibits antitumor activity in vivo. Together, these findings establish short sulfonyl-γ-AApeptides as an effective chemical modality for targeting eIF4E−eIF4G interface and demonstrate that dynamic assembly events within the translation initiation machinery can be manipulated through rational foldamer design.

works.title: Correction to “A ROS-Responsive Dual-Functional H2S Donor for Synergistic Cardioprotection”
Beyond CRBN and VHL: DCAF16-Recruiting Degraders from Rational Design to Clinical Translation
works.abstract: Abstract Targeted protein degradation (TPD) has revolutionized modern drug discovery. However, the current clinical landscape remains predominantly reliant on CRBN and VHL, restricting the targetable proteome and increasing the risk of acquired resistance. Expanding the TPD toolbox with therapeutically tractable E3 ligases is imperative. Recently, DCAF16 has emerged as a frontrunner in this effort, underscored by the advancement of DCAF16-based monovalent degraders such as PLX-61639 and AMX-883 toward clinical evaluation. Unlike the historically serendipitous discovery of CRBN-based molecular glues, DCAF16 offers a versatile platform for the rational design of both bifunctional and monovalent degraders. In this timely perspective, we present the first comprehensive medicinal chemistry analysis of the DCAF16-mediated degradation landscape, focusing on delineating the expanding diversity of recruiting motifs and elucidating the design principles, structural basis, and SAR of representative degraders. Finally, we outline current challenges and offer insights into future design strategies and clinical translation of DCAF16-based degraders.

works.title: Correction to “C-Branched Iminosugars as Selective Pharmacological Chaperones of Lysosomal Alpha-Glucosidase for the Treatment of Pompe Disease”
Identification and Optimization of Novel Dual PARP/Tubulin Colchicine-Binding Site Inhibitors for Cancer Therapy
works.abstract: Abstract Dual targeting of poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP) and the colchicine-binding site (CBS) of tubulin represents a promising strategy to overcome tumor heterogeneity and acquired resistance. Herein, a series of benzofused heterocyclic carboxamide derivatives were designed and synthesized as novel dual PARP/CBS inhibitors. Structure−activity relationship studies identified D13 as the most potent lead, demonstrating low-nanomolar antiproliferative activities (IC50 = 2−15 nM) across multiple cancer cell lines with high selectivity over normal cells. D13 inhibited PARP1/2 enzymatic activity and suppressed tubulin polymerization via CBS binding. D13 also induced G2/M arrest, DNA damage, and apoptosis, while blocking cell migration and tube formation. In an MDA-MB-231 xenograft model, D13 at 20 mg/kg achieved 72.3% tumor growth inhibition with dose-dependent efficacy and good tolerability, outperforming veliparib, phenstatin, and their combination. These findings validate dual PARP/CBS inhibition as a viable therapeutic strategy and support further development of D13 as an anticancer lead.

works.title: The H 2 S‐releasing metformin hybrid Met‐ITC protects against diabetes‐associated vascular dysfunction preserving glycaemic control
works.abstract: Background and Purpose Patients undergoing metformin (Met) therapy for the treatment of type 2 diabetes remain at high cardiovascular risk. Hydrogen sulphide (H 2 S)‐releasing molecules offer antioxidant, anti‐senescence and vasoactive properties that may complement Met activity. This study investigated whether metformin–isothiocyanate (Met‐ITC), a H 2 S‐releasing metformin hybrid, preserves the antidiabetic activity of Met while providing H 2 S‐derived vascular protection. Experimental Approach The predicted Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism and Excretion (ADME) properties of Met and Met‐ITC were evaluated in silico. Maintenance of Met antidiabetic properties was assessed in vitro by evaluating glucose uptake in HepG2 cells and in vivo through oral glucose tolerance tests in db/db mice. The ability of Met‐ITC to release H 2 S and its ability to preserve cell viability and contrast ROS formation and cellular senescence were evaluated in human aortic endothelial cells (HAECs) and smooth muscle cells (HASMCs) exposed to hydrogen peroxide, homocysteine or high‐glucose concentrations. The hyperpolarizing effect of Met‐ITC was tested on HASMCs and its direct vasorelaxing effect as well as its ability to inhibit noradrenaline‐induced vasoconstriction were tested on endothelium‐intact or ‐denuded rat aortic rings. Key Results Met‐ITC showed a more favourable permeability profile than Met and maintained its antidiabetic profile. It provided better protection against oxidative stress, loss of cell viability and senescence compared with Met. Moreover, Met‐ITC produced a concentration‐dependent hyperpolarization of HASMCs, restricted noradrenaline‐induced contraction and induced vasodilatation in endothelium‐denuded and ‐intact rat aortic rings. Conclusion and Implications These findings identify Met‐ITC as a potential candidate for the treatment of diabetes‐associated vascular dysfunction.

works.title: Pharmacological targeting of phosphodiesterase‐5 halts pulmonary fibrosis by suppressing epithelial‐mesenchymal transition via cGMP/PKG/Smad/HDAC2 pathway
works.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Pulmonary fibrosis (PF) is a progressive and incurable disease with activation of epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) as a crucial pathological step. Despite advances in elucidating its pathogenesis, therapeutic options for PF remain very limited. Although raising intracellular levels of cGMP mitigated fibrosis in animal models, the mechanism(s) underlying this action, particularly concerning EMT, remain unclear. PDE5, a key cGMP-hydrolyzing enzyme, is a promising therapeutic target, as some PDE5 inhibitors are in clinical use. EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: Two well-established rat models of PF, induced by bleomycin or paraquat were used to elucidate the therapeutic potential and mechanisms underpinning effects of the PDE5 inhibitor tadalafil on pulmonary fibrogenesis. KEY RESULTS: Daily administration of tadalafil attenuated PF development and lung injury. even when administered at an advanced stage of PF, tadalafil significantly attenuated fibrotic progression and improved lung histopathology. Mechanistically, tadalafil exerted its therapeutic effect by suppressing the canonical TGF-β/Smad signaling pathway and EMT through a cGMP/PKG pathway. Immunohistochemical and immunofluorescence analyses corroborated the in‑vivo antifibrotic activity of tadalafil. Preliminary results indicated PKG‑dependent down-regulation of histone deacetylase 2 (HDAC2) expression and elevated acetylated histones. Knockdown and pharmacological inhibition of HDAC2 mimicked effects of tadalafil, whereas over-expression of HDAC2 negated tadalafil's effects on EMT, implying a key mechanistic role for HDAC2. CONCLUSIONS AND IMPLICATIONS: Tadalafil halted progression of PF by inhibiting EMT, most likely through a PKG-mediated pathway counteracting TGF-β-induced HDAC2 expression. Our findings, together with the well-tolerated safety profile. warrant immediate clinical assessment of repurposing tadalafil for the treatment of pulmonary fibrosis.

works.title: Angiotensin receptor blockers and nontraditional health outcomes: an umbrella review of meta‐analyses of randomised controlled trials
works.abstract: AIM: Angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs) are prescribed for cardiovascular and renal protection, but their effects on nontraditional health outcomes remain unclear. With the increasing use of ARBs in diverse populations, clarifying their broader impact has important clinical implications. METHODS: We conducted an umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses of randomised controlled trials (RCTs) that assessed ARBs and nontraditional health outcomes. PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were searched from inception to April 2026. Methodological quality was appraised using AMSTAR 2, and certainty of evidence was assessed using GRADE. Where trial-level data were available, we re-analysed outcomes using random-effects models and evaluated heterogeneity, 95% prediction intervals, and small-study effects. RESULTS: Fifteen systematic reviews and meta-analyses of RCTs were included, covering 35 unique nontraditional outcomes. Nine outcomes reached nominal statistical significance, but only a few met more stringent credibility criteria. The most credible associations were lower risks of headache and new-onset diabetes, and lower fasting plasma insulin levels with ARB therapy. Associations with migraine severity, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, and insulin resistance were suggestive or exploratory because of prediction intervals crossing the null, sparse data, heterogeneity, or limited certainty. No convincing evidence supported associations with oncological, infectious, or transplant-related outcomes. Most included reviews were rated as low or critically low-quality using AMSTAR 2, warranting cautious interpretation. CONCLUSION: ARBs appear to provide therapeutic benefits beyond traditional indications, particularly in metabolic and neurological domains, without evidence of excess harm. These findings may inform clinical decision-making in patients at risk of diabetes or with comorbid pain conditions.

Perioperative ivonescimab with or without chemotherapy in resectable non-small cell lung cancer: a phase 2 trial
works.abstract: Resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) carries a high risk of postoperative recurrence, underscoring the need for effective perioperative therapies. This nonrandomized, noncomparative phase 2 trial evaluated neoadjuvant ivonescimab monotherapy (cohort 1) or in combination with chemotherapy (cohort 2), followed by surgery and adjuvant ivonescimab. In cohort 2, the major pathological response (MPR) rate was 70.1% (47/67; 95% confidence interval (CI) = 57.7-80.7); the lower bound of the 80% two-sided CI exceeded the historical control rate of 41% and the primary endpoint was met. The MPR rate in cohort 1 was 60.0% (6/10; 95% CI = 26.2-87.8). Among patients who achieved MPR, 83.3% (5/6) in cohort 1 and 97.9% (46/47) in cohort 2 had residual viable tumor (RVT) of ≤5%, respectively. Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events (AEs) occurred in 36.4% (4/11) patients in cohort 1 and 30.4% (24/79) of those in cohort 2, with no grade 3 or higher hemorrhage or treatment-related death. Treatment-related surgery delay occurred in one (1.3%) patient. Surgery-related AEs related to ivonescimab occurred in 10.0% (1/10) and 10.4% (7/67) patients in the two cohorts, respectively, with no grade 3 or higher events reported. These data support perioperative ivonescimab with or without chemotherapy as a promising strategy for resectable NSCLC. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05247684 .

works.title: A tumor transcriptomic atlas across eight decades of life reveals distinct features of early-onset colorectal cancer
Distinct tau PET dynamics in early versus late age-of-onset Alzheimer’s disease
works.abstract: Early-onset Alzheimer’s disease (EOAD) and late-onset AD (LOAD) differ in clinical presentations and rates of progression. We aimed to compare baseline and longitudinal tau positron emission tomography (PET) burden measured with 18 F-flortaucipir and its relationship with clinical variables in amyloid PET–positive, cognitively impaired participants from the Longitudinal Early-Onset Alzheimer’s Disease Study (EOAD; n = 390) and Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (LOAD; n = 211). Participants with EOAD showed higher baseline tau PET burden, broader neuroanatomical involvement, and stronger associations of tau PET with amyloid PET and global cognition. Higher baseline tau PET burden in EOAD was independently validated in participants with EOAD from ADNI. Longitudinally, tau PET increased more rapidly in EOAD than in LOAD, independent of amyloid PET and clinical stage. We conclude that earlier age of onset in AD is linked to a more aggressive tauopathy, which in turn is a primary driver of clinical decline.

works.title: Extended in vivo activity of VRC01 HIV-1 prophylaxis entails initial protective efficacy and subsequent breakthrough infections
works.abstract: The two parallel antibody-mediated prevention (AMP) efficacy trials evaluated whether intravenous infusion of the anti-CD4 binding site broadly neutralizing antibody VRC01 prevents HIV-1 acquisition. Here, we analyzed HIV-1 acquisition in AMP through the week 104 final study visit. Against viruses considered highly sensitive to VRC01 [80% inhibitory concentration (IC 80 ) < 1 microgram/milliliter], VRC01 prophylaxis maintained cumulative prevention efficacy of 66.3% (95% confidence interval: 32.4, 83.2%), suggesting that the antibody successfully blocked or cleared these infections. In the post–week 80 period (after the final dose at week 72), HIV diagnosis and resistance to VRC01 were more frequent and greater in the VRC01 groups versus placebo. For instance, more HIV diagnoses with viruses considered moderately sensitive or resistant to VRC01 (IC 80 ≥ 5 microgram/milliliter) were made in the VRC01 groups compared with placebo groups (11 versus 1). Plausibly, as in vivo VRC01 concentration waned, suppressed viruses—often evolving greater resistance because of selective pressure—emerged as detectable infections. Our findings suggest that, whereas single antibodies can block sensitive strains, multiple antibodies are likely required to prevent both viral escape and breakthrough infections.

works.title: Erratum for the Research Article “CRISPR-engineered human brown-like adipocytes prevent diet-induced obesity and ameliorate metabolic syndrome in mice”
TWEAK signaling drives the transition from psoriasis to atopic dermatitis–like inflammation in paradoxical eczema
works.abstract: Targeted biologics have transformed the treatment of inflammatory skin diseases such as plaque psoriasis. However, some patients with psoriasis paradoxically develop eczematous skin reactions after therapy targeting tumor necrosis factor (TNF), interleukin-17 (IL-17), or IL-23. Although paradoxical eczema (PE) resembles atopic dermatitis (AD) clinically and histologically, the molecular mechanisms that drive its development remain poorly understood. Here, we generated high-resolution cellular and spatial maps of human skin using single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, immunohistochemistry, and in vitro assays, profiling lesional biopsies from patients with PE ( n = 8 donors), alongside healthy control, psoriasis, and AD skin ( n = 4 donors per group). In PE, we identified distinct transcriptional changes characterized by myeloid and T cell expansion and an altered keratinocyte phenotype shaped by TNF-like weak inducer of apoptosis (TWEAK; encoded by TNFSF12 ) signaling through its receptor TNFRSF12A , confirmed at the protein level by immunohistochemistry. To define the underlying mechanism, we stimulated immortalized (N-TERT) and primary human keratinocytes and found that TWEAK acted together with IL-13 to drive a T helper 2– and type I interferon–polarized epithelial program that partially recapitulated the keratinocyte signature of PE lesions. We validated key target genes by quantitative polymerase chain reaction in primary keratinocytes. In THP-1 cells and primary human CD14 + monocytes, anti-TNF treatment induced TWEAK expression, suggesting a compensatory inflammatory circuit. Together, these findings identify the TWEAK–IL-13 axis as a key driver of PE and suggest how cytokine blockade may reshape cutaneous immune responses.

works.title: Cancer-specific T cell receptor discovery using 150,000 clinical genomics samples
works.abstract: T cell receptors (TCRs) can enable detection and elimination of cancer cells via recognition of cancer-specific peptides presented on human leukocyte antigen (HLA). We speculated that shared cancer antigens could be recognized by recurrent ("public") TCRs, which might be identifiable using statistical methods. Here, we identified public TCRs against therapeutically relevant targets via computational analysis of large-scale bulk RNA sequencing data obtained from routine clinical genomics testing. Using data from ∼150,000 patient tumor samples, we identified TCR chains that were associated with well-known cancer antigens, including human papillomavirus, mutated KRAS, and CT83. We devised methods for pairing enriched TCR-α and TCR-β chain sequences and validated 44 TCRs across nine peptide-HLA targets for antigen recognition, including potent cytotoxic TCRs. Our results suggest that public anticancer TCRs are common and may represent a new source for the development of cancer therapeutics.

works.title: Longitudinal remodeling of the tumor-immune microenvironment during regorafenib, nivolumab, and chemotherapy in advanced gastric cancer
works.abstract: Previous studies combining the multikinase inhibitor regorafenib with a PD-1 inhibitor showed promising activity in gastric cancer. We conducted a phase 1b/2 trial (NCT05394740) of first-line regorafenib, nivolumab, and chemotherapy in 30 patients with mismatch repair–proficient gastric cancer and investigated its impact on the tumor microenvironment. The primary end point was met; 22 of 30 patients showed objective tumor response (73%; 80% confidence interval, 60.3 to 83.8). Single-cell RNA and T cell receptor sequencing were performed on biopsy samples at baseline, during treatment, and at disease progression. The combination treatment increased tumor antigen–reactive CD8 + T cells and M1-like proinflammatory macrophages and decreased immunosuppressive and tumor-promoting populations, including activated CCR8 + regulatory T cells, LRRC15 + cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs), RGS5 + pericytes, and APLN + tip cells. At progression, LRRC15 + CAFs and APLN + tip cells remained reduced, activated CCR8 + regulatory T cells reexpanded, and additional treatment-resistant subsets emerged, including APOC1 + lipid-associated macrophages. In murine models of acquired resistance, therapeutic targeting of these suppressive immune cell populations with antibodies against CCR8 or TREM2 in combination with PD-1 blockade restored antitumor immunity. These findings demonstrate dynamic remodeling of the tumor microenvironment and suggest potential therapeutic targets.

works.title: A synthetic heparin oligosaccharide decouples anticoagulation from heparin-induced thrombocytopenia risk
works.abstract: Low–molecular weight heparin (LMWH) remains clinically indispensable for the prevention and treatment of thrombosis in cardiovascular surgery, hemodialysis, and other critical care settings. However, LMWH is constrained by heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT) and supply chain vulnerabilities of animal-derived sources. This study used chemoenzymatic synthesis to engineer homogeneous dodecasaccharide 12G-2, decoupling anticoagulant efficacy from HIT risk via dual structural modulation. Substitution with 2- O -sulfated glucuronic acid conferred conformational rigidity, and engineered sulfation attenuated platelet factor 4 (PF4) binding, whereas the antithrombin-binding domain remained intact. 12G-2 exhibited nanomolar anti–Factor Xa (FXa) activity in vitro, enoxaparin-equivalent venous antithrombotic efficacy, and superior arterial antithrombotic activity in murine thrombosis models, and it showed diminished PF4 binding, attenuated pathological β sheet formation, and minimal recognition by HIT-related antibodies in vitro. Both in vitro and in a murine tail-bleeding model, 12G-2 demonstrated high protamine reversibility, exceeding standard LMWH enoxaparin neutralization efficiency. In washed human platelets, 12G-2–PF4 complexes with the HIT-mimicking antibody KKO failed to induce integrin αIIbβ3 activation or P-selectin release and elicited minimal platelet spreading comparable to resting controls. Safety assessments in mice showed no hepatotoxicity at tested doses and low immunogenicity in a murine PF4-heparin immunization model. In PF4-heparin antibody–positive mice, 12G-2 attenuated platelet activation while exerting stronger FXa inhibition than enoxaparin. These findings established 12G-2 as an alternative to LMWH.

works.title: Translational resilience in intravaginal HIV prevention and multipurpose prevention technologies: formulation, exposure, and implementation barriers
works.abstract: Intravaginal HIV prevention has progressed from early nonspecific microbicides to antiretroviral gels, films, inserts, and intravaginal rings, alongside emerging biologic agents and multipurpose prevention technologies (MPTs). Despite substantial advances in antiviral potency and formulation technology, translation from pharmaceutical development to consistent clinical protection has remained uneven, indicating that API activity or dosage-form performance alone is insufficient to explain clinical outcomes. This review critically examines the development of intravaginal HIV prevention and MPT products through a mechanistic pharmaceutical perspective, focusing on the relationships between controllable product attributes, drug release and transport, the cervicovaginal environment, compartment-specific pharmacokinetics/pharmacodynamics (PK/PD), and product use. Historical microbicide and antiretroviral programs are examined as translational case studies to identify how mucosal safety, local exposure and use-dependent drug delivery contributed to divergent clinical outcomes. The review further evaluates how cervicovaginal fluid, semen, mucus, epithelial barriers, hormonal state, microbiome composition, and inflammation can modify formulation behavior and drug transport; how API physicochemistry, solid state, drug loading, drug-polymer partitioning, and diffusivity constrain formulation architecture and release; and how these relationships differ among gels, films, inserts, sustained-release devices, MPTs, and biologic delivery systems. Particular attention is given to the distinction between drug incorporation, release, tissue transport, and pharmacologically relevant exposure, and to the additional challenges created when multiple APIs require different release rates, biological compartments, or durations of action. Platform characteristics are further considered in relation to the exposure patterns and product-use conditions they are intended to support. By integrating formulation science with cervicovaginal physiology, PK/PD, and clinical experience, this review provides a mechanistic basis for identifying where intravaginal prevention systems lose translational performance and which formulation-transport-exposure relationships require stronger evidence to support more reproducible clinical protection.

Impact of Gastrointestinal Proteolytic Stability on Macrocyclic Peptide Absorption with Sodium Decanoate as a Membrane Permeation Enhancer in the Rat
works.abstract: Abstract The two major barriers to effective oral peptide delivery are proteolytic degradation in the gastrointestinal environment and low membrane permeability. In this work, we aimed to evaluate the minimum level of intrinsic proteolytic stability in the upper small intestinal environment required to achieve maximal peptide absorption when dosed with permeation enhancers (PEs). We used sodium decanoate (C10) as a representative PE and studied its effect on two chemically distinct series of macrocyclic peptides (MCPs) in vitro and in vivo. The MCPs (within each series) were selected based on their closely related amino acid sequences and physicochemical properties but differing levels of intrinsic proteolytic stability towards pancreatic enzymes. The MCPs were formulated with and without C10 and dosed intrajejunally to rats to determine absolute bioavailability, and the effect of different concentrations of C10 on MCP proteolytic stability was evaluated in the in vitro pancreatin stability assay. C10 protected all MCPs from proteolytic degradation by pancreatic enzymes in a concentration-dependent manner in vitro and increased the absolute bioavailability of all MCPs in vivo. The findings described herein demonstrate that an MCP half-life of approximately 60 min in the in vitro pancreatin stability assay (without C10) is sufficient to enable maximal in vivo absorption in rats when C10 is used as a PE.

works.title: Correction to “Novel Nonsecosteroidal Vitamin D Receptor Modulator Combined with Gemcitabine Enhances Pancreatic Cancer Therapy through Remodeling of the Tumor Microenvironment”
Discovery and Identification of a Novel Class of Aminopyrimidine Derivatives Specifically Blocking the Interaction between the M and N Structural Proteins of the Coronavirus HCoV-OC43
works.abstract: Abstract The pyrimidine nucleus serves as a key structural motif in drug discovery. Using compound 1 as the lead, we synthesized a series of new aminopyrimidine analogues and assessed their antiviral activity against HCoV-OC43. Among them, compound 13h showed exceptional potency, with an EC50 of 0.12 μM, an SI over 800, and a good safety profile. Systematic mechanistic studies revealed that compound 13h specifically binds to the V201 residue of the M structural protein, disrupting the critical M−N protein interaction required for viral assembly. The V201 site is located precisely at the M−N interaction interface, which accounts for the high potency and safety of 13h. Conclusively, we discovered the first small-molecule inhibitor targeting the M−N binding interface. This novel mechanism of action distinguishes it from existing anti-coronavirus drugs and establishes a promising new antiviral strategy.

works.title: Stakeholder-informed use cases and target product characteristics for vaccines and therapeutics for Nipah virus disease
authors: On behalf of the Nipah Countermeasure Use Case Working Group
works.abstract: Nipah virus (NiV) is a deadly zoonotic pathogen with potential for severe outbreaks. We convened a multi-stakeholder expert consultation to define potential implementation strategies and use cases for NiV countermeasures across hypothetical outbreak scenarios and conditions. Participants identified distinct roles for vaccines, monoclonal antibodies (mAbs), and small-molecule therapeutics (SMTs) for prevention, post-exposure protection, and treatment. These stakeholder-informed outputs are intended to inform product development, target product profiles, and equitable access during future outbreaks.

works.title: Clonal tree frequency analysis reveals affinity determinants and enables antibody lead optimization
works.abstract: Understanding the sequence determinants of antibody affinity within a clonal family is a central challenge in therapeutic antibody discovery. Here, we applied amino acid frequency analysis to a large phylogenetic clonal tree of anti-ST2 monoclonal antibodies, where V(D)J recombination is constant and only somatic hypermutations vary. We identified M33I and L100I in the heavy chain as key affinity-governing mutations, corroborated by AlphaFold2 structural modeling and molecular dynamics free‑energy decomposition. The I33/I100 genotype predicted significantly improved functional neutralization of IL-33-induced IL-6 release and was associated with a higher transcriptomic affinity score (Hiscore). Prospective mutagenesis of three low-affinity parent antibodies achieved up to 10-fold affinity improvement, establishing a workflow integrating sequence statistics, structural modeling, transcriptomics and MD simulation for rational lead optimization.

works.title: FDA approves plasmid DNA-based immunotherapy for rare viral disease
Heterogeneity of microbiome responses to menopausal hormone therapy among perimenopausal women
works.abstract: Menopausal hormone therapy (MHT) alleviates climacteric symptoms, yet its microbiome-wide effects and efficacy determinants remain unclear. Here we show that oral estradiol/dydrogesterone, given for 6 months to 356 perimenopausal women, improved neuroendocrine, metabolic and symptom outcomes and induced site-specific microbial remodeling. Vaginocervical and urinary niches showed the most pronounced restructuring, with moderate oral and minimal gut changes. MHT increased vaginocervical Lactobacillus crispatus and reduced Gardnerella vaginalis. Higher baseline vaginocervical L. crispatus predicted greater postintervention vaginocervical and urinary colonization and superior Female Sexual Function Index improvement. Baseline vaginocervical community types determined differential outcomes: G. vaginalis-dominated individuals shifted most toward healthier communities, whereas diversified individuals improved least. MHT efficacy also varied according to baseline gut community type: Phocaeicola vulgatus-dominated women exhibited greater hormonal responsiveness, superior clinical outcomes and were more likely to achieve 4-week rapid clinical remission than Prevotella copri-dominated women. These findings support a precision MHT framework integrating gut and vaginocervical community typing for personalized care. Chictr.org.cn ID: ChiCTR2100049768 .

works.title: A live biotherapeutic product for adult allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation recipients: a partially randomized, placebo-controlled phase 1b trial
works.abstract: Gastrointestinal (GI) microbiome disruption and impaired GI barrier integrity increase the risk of bloodstream infection (BSI) following allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplant. Here we report results from a two-cohort (open-label, n = 15; randomized, placebo-controlled, n = 45) phase 1b study of SER-155, an investigational, cultivated, multi-strain, oral live biotherapeutic designed to address GI microbiome disruption GI epithelial barrier integrity in allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplant recipients. In cohort 2, 34 of 45 participants received either SER-155 treatment (n = 20, SER-155 following microbiome conditioning with oral vancomycin), or placebo (n = 14), and subsequently received transplant. For the primary safety endpoint, SER-155 was well tolerated, with a safety profile comparable to placebo, no treatment-related serious adverse events and no infections with SER-155 species; the most common adverse events were diarrhea and nausea. Four participants in cohort 1 and four participants in cohort 2 (two participants in the SER-155 arm and two in the placebo arm) died during the study; none was attributable to SER-155. For the primary pharmacokinetic endpoint, engraftment was detected for 16 of 16 SER-155 strains, with a median of 11.5 strains detected after the first treatment course. The key secondary efficacy endpoint revealed a significantly lower incidence of BSI with SER-155 versus placebo (10.0% versus 43%; OR 0.15; 95% CI 0.01–1.13; P = 0.0423; 77% relative risk reduction). Other secondary efficacy endpoints (GI infection, acute graft-versus-host disease ≥grade 2, febrile neutropenia and a composite endpoint of BSI, GI infection or acute graft-versus-host disease) were not statistically significant. The secondary pharmacodynamic endpoint of GI domination by Enterococcus and Enterobacteriaceae spp. was not achieved. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT04995653 . In a phase 1b study that included an open-label and randomized-controlled cohorts of allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation recipients, treatment with the investigational, cultivated, multi-strain bacterial oral live biotherapeutic product, SER-155, was found to have a similar safety profile to placebo and resulted in fewer bloodstream infections, indicating further clinical investigation of this therapeutic is warranted.

works.title: Regulatable membrane-bound IL-15 engineered TIL cell therapy for immune checkpoint inhibitor-resistant advanced melanoma: pooled analysis of phase 1 and 1/2 trials
works.abstract: Amsokigene autoleucel (amsoki-cel, OBX-115) is a tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte (TIL) cell therapy engineered to express acetazolamide (ACZ)-regulatable membrane-bound interleukin-15, abrogating the need for interleukin-2. In two single-arm trials (completed phase 1 single-center first-in-human (FIH) and ongoing phase 1/2 multicenter Agni-01), patients with immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-resistant advanced melanoma received lymphodepletion and varying doses and schedules of amsoki-cel and ACZ. The primary objective of FIH and Agni-01 phase 1 was safety, tolerability and recommended phase 2 dose (RP2D); the primary objective of Agni-01 phase 2 was objective response rate (ORR) at the RP2D. The first patient treated experienced rapid lymphocyte expansion and vasogenic edema of a previously irradiated brain metastasis, prompting protocol modifications and dose deescalation in FIH, including 80% reduction in maximum amsoki-cel dose and 75% reduction in ACZ dose. After preliminary demonstration of safety at the lower dose, doses were increased in FIH, and reescalation was initiated in Agni-01. Across studies, 37 patients were treated (FIH, n = 17; Agni-01, n = 20). Post hoc pooled analysis demonstrated no dose-limiting toxicities, ICU care or treatment-related mortality. Most common grade 3 or higher treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) included neutropenia (64.9% (24/37)), leukopenia/lymphopenia (56.8% (21/37) each) and anemia/thrombocytopenia (37.8% (14/37) each). Serious TEAEs were reported for 10 patients, including eight patients with grade 3 or higher events (non-hematologic, 13.5% (5/37); hematologic, 13.5% (5/37)). RP2D was selected based on overall safety and tolerability as well as preliminary anti-tumor activity in Agni-01 phase 1. The phase 2 preliminary ORR was 66.7% (6/9). In total, 15 patients were treated at RP2D and comprise the Key Efficacy Set (Agni-01: phase 1, n = 6; phase 2, n = 9), of which 10 patients (66.7%; 95% confidence interval 38-88%) achieved objective responses (including two complete responses). Amsoki-cel demonstrated favorable safety and promising early clinical activity in patients with ICI-resistant melanoma. A separate phase 2 pivotal Agni-01 cohort is ongoing. ClinicalTrials.gov identifiers: NCT05470283 and NCT06060613 .

works.title: Editor’s Pick: Wild Bioscience
Validation of senescence as a therapeutic target in metabolic dysfunction–associated steatohepatitis (MASH) through navitoclax delivery
works.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) is a chronic liver disease characterized by steatosis, inflammation, and progressive fibrosis. Increasing evidence suggests that cellular senescence contributes to MASH progression by promoting lipid accumulation, inflammatory signaling, and fibrogenic responses, highlighting hepatic senescent cells as a potential therapeutic target. Senolytics selectively eliminate senescent cells, but their application in MASH remains insufficiently explored. In this study, we developed in vitro models integrating hepatic lipid accumulation and hepatocyte-macrophage inflammatory crosstalk to facilitate investigation of the contribution of cellular senescence to MASH pathology and to evaluate senescence-targeted interventions. Senescent hepatic cells showed enhanced lipid accumulation and amplified inflammatory signaling with macrophages. Natural Extracellular Vesicles (EVs) derived from adipocytes reduced senescence-associated phenotypes but exhibited context-dependent biological effects, highlighting the limited control over their intrinsic bioactivity. Navitoclax, a senolytic targeting anti-apoptotic BCL-2 family proteins, reduced senescence-associated phenotypes, but its clinical use is limited by its dose-dependent toxicity. Hence, we conceived nano-Cell Vesicle Technology Systems (nCVTs), a biohybrid-based platform combining cell-derived membranes with synthetic lipids for controlled delivery of navitoclax. Navitoclax-loaded nCVTs retained senolytic activity and reduced inflammatory signaling and fibrotic activation in vitro. Importantly, in a Western diet- and fructose-induced (WDF) MASH mouse model, navitoclax-loaded AML-12-derived nCVTs alleviated hepatic lipid accumulation while reducing histopathological activity score and fibrotic profiles. Neither navitoclax formulation reduced platelet counts or hemoglobin concentrations at the tested dose. Collectively, these findings support cellular senescence as a therapeutically relevant target for MASH and identify nCVTs as a promising engineered platform for controlled senolytic delivery.

works.title: Topical drug delivery for androgenetic alopecia: from hair follicle targeting to clinical translation
Aluminum-Based Metal−Organic Framework Nanoplatform Combines Chemo-Nanotherapy in an Intrahepatic Walker 256 Rat Tumor Model: Association with Glycerophospholipid Metabolic Changes
works.abstract: Abstract Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) treatment is severely limited by the low efficacy and drug resistance of current monotherapies. While nanocarriers for sorafenib (Sor) delivery have been explored, platforms that combine multimodal therapy and elucidate deep-seated anti-tumor mechanisms remain lacking. To address this, we engineered a nanosystem by loading Sor onto an aluminum-based metal−organic framework (Sor@Al-MOF), which combines chemotherapy with the intrinsic bioactivity of the nanocarrier. Sor@Al-MOF nanoparticles exhibited a well-defined lamellar structure, with a zeta potential of 10.10 ± 0.69 mV. Sor@Al-MOF achieved a high drug loading content (56.43% ± 0.36%) and encapsulation efficiency (77.38% ± 4.20%), and exhibited a cumulative release of 65.74 ± 0.55% at pH 5.3 after 72 h. In vitro, Sor@Al-MOF showed potent cytotoxicity against human HCC HepG2 cells (IC50 = 88.40 ± 0.12 μg/mL). In an intrahepatic Walker 256 rat tumor model, Sor@Al-MOF demonstrated enhanced therapeutic efficacy. Integrated metabolomics provided preliminary insights into potential metabolic changes in this model, including changes in choline kinase α (CHKα)-related glycerophospholipid metabolism. This study presents Sor@Al-MOF as a promising combinatorial nanotherapeutic candidate and offers a foundational basis for exploring metabolism-targeting strategies in liver cancer treatment.

works.title: End-to-End Prediction of Subcutaneous Peptide Absorption Rates from Amino Acid Sequences Using Physics-Informed Machine Learning
works.abstract: Abstract The subcutaneous (SC) absorption rate constant (ka) dictates critical pharmacokinetic and dosing parameters of injectable peptide therapeutics, yet currently, it cannot be predicted prior to clinical testing, forcing empirical decisions at the discovery and formulation stages. We address this important gap by constructing the first end-to-end machine learning framework that predicts SC ka, both point predictions and prediction intervals, purely from the amino acid sequence and conjugate chemistry. For developing the model, we first curated a comprehensive database of 41 human clinical ka values (0.0077−7.61 h−1), covering unmodified, fatty-acid-acylated, and protein-conjugated peptides. These data were subsequently encoded into a combination of protein language model (ESM-2) embeddings, chemical language model (ChemBERTa) embeddings, and 30 physics-informed molecular descriptors designed to capture the physical variables governing SC transport. Seven machine learning (ML) architectures and ensembles thereof were trained, with the best model (NGBoost) achieving R2 = 0.850 under leave-one-out cross-validation, a markedly high accuracy given the large variance in the clinically reported ka values. Notably, models trained on the physics-informed molecular descriptors or combinations thereof substantially outperformed models trained purely on learned embeddings (ESM-2, ChemBERTa)a direct consequence of the small scale of our training dataset. SHAP interpretability analysis indicates that predictions are consistent with established SC absorption physics, with properties including molecular weight, net charge, hydrophobicity, and acyl chain molecular characteristics dictating model predictions. Leveraging Jackknife+, the developed framework also reports ka prediction uncertainties (prediction intervals). Overall, this framework enables high-throughput sequence-level candidate ranking before in vivo data become available, supporting the rational early-stage development of peptide therapeutics.

works.title: Identifying Short Half-Life Compounds from Structure Information Using Multi-Task Graph Neural Networks
works.abstract: Abstract Accurate prediction of terminal half-life (t1/2) is paramount for prioritizing drug candidates during the lead optimization stage, as it minimizes the risk of clinical trial failure while optimizing resource allocation. Drugs characterized by suboptimal t1/2 profileseither excessively short or prolongedpresent significant challenges in dosage design and are frequently associated with increased risks of adverse effects. Traditionally, the determination of t1/2 has necessitated in vivo experiments to derive total clearance (CLT) and volume of distribution (Vss). In this study, we curated a comprehensive dataset of over 1400 compounds and developed deep learning-based regression models to predict t1/2 directly from molecular structures using Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs). We implemented both single-task and multi-task learning architectures; the latter integrated CLT, Vss, and other related pharmacokinetic parameters to leverage their inherent physiological correlations. Our results indicate that a multi-task model achieved higher predictive performance than the single-task counterpart, with notably high precision in identifying compounds with short t1/2. By enabling the structural-based identification of unfavorable t1/2 profiles without the need for experimental data, this approach provides a robust and efficient tool for streamlining candidate selection in the early stages of drug development. This methodology is expected to accelerate the discovery of compounds with favorable pharmacokinetic properties, reducing the reliance on late-stage experimental validation.

works.title: Non-invasive oral magnetoelectric vagus nerve neuromodulation for Parkinson’s disease therapy
Issue Information
Crossing subfamily borders: Mechanosensitive TREK‐1 and alkaline‐activated TASK‐4 form heterodimers with unique functional and pharmacological properties
works.abstract: Background and Purpose The tandem of two‐pore‐domain potassium (K 2P ) channels TREK‐1 and TASK‐4 are expressed in the heart and pancreatic beta‐cells. As TREK‐1 and TASK‐4 belong to distinct subfamilies with different functional hallmarks, heteromerization of these two channels was highly unexpected. However, due to their shared expression in these tissues and their involvement in congenital cardiac arrhythmias, the aim of this study was to probe for a possible formation of TREK‐1/TASK‐4 heterodimers. Experimental Approach Two‐electrode voltage‐clamp and inside‐out macropatch clamp recordings, together with immunohistochemistry and chemiluminescence‐based ELISA assays, were utilized to describe heteromerization of TREK‐1 and TASK‐4 channels and elucidate the characteristics of this heteromeric channel complex. Key Results Here, we show that the mechanosensitive TREK‐1 forms heteromeric channel complexes with the alkaline‐activated TASK‐4. The resulting heterodimers of these only remotely related channels have an enhanced temperature sensitivity, an altered pH dependence and regulation by extracellular sodium. Unlike TREK‐1, heteromeric TREK‐1/TASK‐4 channels are not inhibited via G s ‐coupled receptor activation, as the heterodimeric channels are not PKA sensitive. Strikingly, these novel heterodimeric channel complexes are characterized by a unique pharmacology. Conclusions and Implications The newly described heterodimerization across different K 2P channel families is of major relevance for drugs targeting TASK‐4 or TREK‐1. Their functional co‐expression in different tissues raises the possibility of developing drugs against cardiac arrhythmias and Type 2 diabetes by specifically targeting these unique heterodimeric channel complexes.

Povorcitinib for nonsegmental vitiligo: two randomized, controlled, phase 3 STOP-V trials
works.abstract: There is an unmet need for repigmentation therapies for patients with nonsegmental vitiligo (NSV) who are candidates for systemic therapy. Here, 52-week primary results are reported from two parallel phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials of once-daily povorcitinib (oral, highly selective JAK1 inhibitor) 30 mg in adults with moderate-to-severe NSV (STOP-V1 and STOP-V2). STOP-V1 and STOP-V2 enrolled 467 and 449 patients, respectively. In both studies, the primary endpoint of ≥75% improvement in the facial Vitiligo Area Scoring Index (F-VASI75) at week 52 was met, demonstrating statistically significant and clinically meaningful repigmentation with povorcitinib versus placebo (STOP-V1: 18.9% versus 6.8%; odds ratio, 3.1; 95% confidence interval 1.6-5.9; P = 0.0003; STOP-V2: 18.9% versus 3.1%; odds ratio, 7.5; 95% confidence interval 3.0-18.6; P < 0.0001). Povorcitinib was well tolerated; the percentage of patients with any treatment-emergent adverse event (TEAE) was similar between the povorcitinib and placebo groups in both studies (STOP-V1/STOP-V2, 68.7%/66.7% versus 63.7%/62.7%). The most common TEAEs with povorcitinib were nasopharyngitis (STOP-V1/STOP-V2, 11.2%/11.3% versus placebo, 9.8%/11.1%), acne (10.7%/10.8% versus 3.0%/2.2%) and upper respiratory tract infection (6.9%/14.0% versus 9.0%/10.7%). Serious TEAEs were generally single events, and Janus kinase inhibitor class-specific TEAEs were absent or rare. These results support once-daily povorcitinib as an effective and well-tolerated systemic treatment for adults with moderate-to-severe NSV. works.title: Neoadjuvant botensilimab with or without balstilimab in pMMR and dMMR colon cancer: the phase 2 UNICORN trial
works.abstract: Preoperative immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) are active in patients with deficient mismatch repair (dMMR) colon cancer (CC), whereas proficient mismatch repair (pMMR) CC has been consistently considered resistant to first-generation ICIs. In the phase 2 UNICORN trial, we evaluated short-course preoperative botensilimab (BOT; multifunctional Fc-enhanced anti-CTLA-4 monoclonal antibody) alone or in combination with the anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibody balstilimab (BOT + BAL) in 56 patients with resectable, locally advanced CC. Twenty-eight patients with pMMR CC were sequentially enrolled in BOT (n = 14) and BOT + BAL (n = 14) cohorts. Twenty-eight patients with dMMR CC followed the same sequential allocation strategy. The primary endpoint of centrally assessed pathological major response (pMR) rate (≤10% of residual viable tumor) was met in all cohorts, except pMMR BOT. Specifically, the pMR rate was 0% (95% confidence interval (CI): 0-23.2%) in pMMR BOT, 36% (95% CI: 12.8-64.9%) in pMMR BOT + BAL, 36% (95% CI: 12.8-64.9%) in dMMR BOT and 100% (95% CI: 76.8-100%) in dMMR BOT + BAL. Secondary endpoints included safety, quality of life, describing treatment-induced transcriptional dynamics, peripheral blood mononuclear cell dynamics, radiomics and radiogenomics features, fecal microbiota composition and circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) dynamics. Eight (29%) and 15 (54%) patients treated with BOT and BOT + BAL, respectively, experienced immune-related adverse events, most commonly flu-like syndrome and diarrhea. Single-cell spatial transcriptomic analysis of matched baseline and post-treatment samples highlighted high baseline PD-L1 stromal expression and low post-treatment regulatory T cell signatures in pMMR responders, whereas dMMR responders displayed high baseline FCGR2A and FCGR3A expression on intratumoral macrophages. Clearance of ctDNA before surgery correlated with pathological response and lack of recurrence at data cutoff. Preoperative BOT + BAL elicits pathological responses in patients with pMMR or dMMR CC, supporting the combination as a promising strategy to expand ICI benefits to the early-stage setting. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05845450 .

The role of neurogenic inflammation and CGRP in migraine headache
works.abstract: The last 40 years have witnessed a thorough change in our understanding of the mechanisms underlying migraine, initiated by the discovery of calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP). A century ago, William Bayliss, Thomas Lewis and other pioneers introduced a visionary neurophysiological mechanism, brought about by peripheral terminals of a specialized subset of primary sensory neurons, which was named 'neurogenic inflammation'; in both mammal and human skin, action potentials generated by injured nerve terminals of primary sensory neurons can invade collateral fibres via antidromic conduction and release a mediator that 'produces the flare and enhances sensitivity of other sensory axons responsible for pain'. This mediator, much later identified as CGRP, provides the missing link between these early observations and modern therapeutic targets. Multiple monoclonal antibodies against CGRP or its receptor along with orally available small molecule antagonists of the CGRP receptor have revolutionized the prevention and acute treatment of migraine. The pharmacokinetic features of anti-CGRP drugs and the paracrine actions of CGRP suggest the proposal that the mechanism underlying migraine headache occurs in a spatially limited microenvironment located outside the blood-brain barrier. According to this hypothesis, the migraine headache milieu comprises CGRP-containing peripheral sensory nerve endings (C-fibre nociceptors) and neighbouring cells, including other nerve fibres (Aδ-fibres), vascular smooth muscle cells and Schwann cells wrapping these nerve fibres.

works.abstract: The development of pulmonary immunomodulators that prime anti-tumor immune responses is hindered by poor lung delivery, as current strategies show limited lung targeting beyond the liver following intravenous administration. Inspired by the natural process of virus spread to the lungs via red blood cell (RBC) carriage, we developed a biomimetic immunomodulatory platform (M-RBC) integrating silica nanoparticles with RBC-hitchhiking. Rather than relying on static encapsulation, this platform is engineered as a topography-governed, shear-responsive controlled release system. It exploits tunable surface roughness to ensure that the nanoparticles remain securely bound to RBC during normal venous circulation but rapidly dissociate upon encountering the high capillary shear stress transitions in the lungs. Among the variations tested, medium-spiked silica nanoparticles (MNPs) optimally balance macrophage activation, biocompatibility, and shear-dependent RBC detachment. Upon intravenous dosing, the M-RBC platform at an optimal nanoparticle-to-erythrocyte ratio of 150:1 exhibits the highest accumulation within pulmonary metastatic nodules and the lowest liver entrapment, remarkably alleviating the local tumor immunosuppressive microenvironment. When surface-loaded with GM-CSF or administered in combination with an anti-PD1 antibody, the platform not only significantly reduces metastatic burden but also elicits a systemic immune memory that suppresses distant tumor growth. Collectively, our findings decipher how engineering nanoscale topographies can finely govern erythrocyte hijacking and capillary shear-responsive controlled release preferentially within pulmonary metastatic niches, establishing a highly translatable paradigm to engineer next-generation site-specific immunotherapeutics.

works.abstract: Chimeric Antigen Receptor (CAR) T cells are commonly generated using gamma-retroviral or lentiviral vectors given their efficiency and stable integration, but vector supply constraints have created bottlenecks to wider access. Using a combination of lentiviral transduction and genome editing, ‘universal' donor CAR-T cells devoid of endogenous TCRαβ and suitable for multiple recipients are also under investigation as ‘off-the-shelf' therapies. In addition, nuclease mediated insertion by homology-directed repair (HDR) of CAR genes delivered by Adeno Associated Virus into the TRAC locus has been reported to mediate superior tumour clearance. We investigated alternative entirely virus-free procedures to insert synthetic DNA encoding CAR genes at either TRAC or CD3ζ loci in direct comparison to lentiviral generated universal 41BB-CD3ζ-CAR T cells. While non-viral manufacture was successful and in vitro cytotoxic function was comparable, in vivo inhibition of human leukemia in xenograft murine models was not superior to lentiviral products. Non-viral approaches offer attractive prospects for sophisticated editing and precise CAR insertion and may offer valuable therapeutic options, but careful preclinical evaluation and well-designed clinical trials benchmarked against existing lentiviral approaches are recommended.
