works.abstract: Pemphigus vulgaris (PV) is a life-threatening autoimmune blistering disease primarily driven by autoantibodies targeting desmoglein 3 (Dsg3), resulting in loss of keratinocyte cohesion and clinically manifesting blisters and erosions of surface-close mucosal tissues. Current therapies suppress autoantibody production but fail to directly restore desmosomal adhesion. Here, we established an adult mouse model of PV through repeated injections of AK47ch, a recombinant monospecific anti-Dsg3 IgG1 antibody, into C57BL/6J mice. Within 12 days, AK47ch-treated mice reproducibly developed hallmark features of PV, including oral lesions, patchy alopecia, suprabasal acantholysis confined to mucosal tissues, and intercellular IgG deposition. Prophylactic and quasi-therapeutic intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg), an established therapy for refractory PV, significantly reduced disease progression. The selective MEK1/2 inhibitor selumetinib, previously shown to block anti-Dsg3 IgG-induced keratinocyte dissociation in vitro, attenuated disease severity in clinically affected mice and reduced MEK1/2 phosphorylation in lesional mucosa. MEK1/2 inhibition was associated with reduced expression of transcripts linked to inflammatory, chemokine, cytokine, and interferon responses, and increased expression of transcripts related to cellular homeostasis, as shown by targeted NanoString nCounter analysis of buccal mucosa biopsies. This model provides a platform for preclinical evaluation of desmosome-stabilizing therapies and identifies the MEK/ERK signaling axis as a pharmacologically actionable target in PV.

works.abstract: Chronic granulomatous disease is a primary immunodeficiency caused by mutations in the genes encoding subunits of the nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate oxidase complex, resulting in impaired antimicrobial activity of phagocytes. Patients suffer from recurrent infections and inflammation with life-threatening long-term complications. We developed a self-inactivating lentiviral vector for ex vivo gene therapy of p47phox-deficient chronic granulomatous disease, expressing p47phox under control of the myeloid-specific miR223 promoter. Our preclinical studies using the p47phox-deficient mouse model of the disease showed that transduced hematopoietic stem cells engrafted well and led to sustained p47phox expression and NADPH oxidase function in myeloid cells, demonstrating myeloid-specific long-term efficacy. An average of 2 vector integrations per cell were sufficient to restore p47phox expression and NADPH oxidase activity in ∼80% of blood granulocytes. Physiological biodistribution of transduced cells and absence of transgene-related toxicity confirmed the safety of the vector. Transduction of human healthy donor and patient hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells showed that an average of 2 integrations per cell were sufficient to restore NADPH oxidase activity in a clinically relevant 40% of in vitro generated phagocytes. Overall, our preclinical results confirmed the efficacy and safety of this lentiviral vector, supporting translation into a first-in-human clinical trial.

works.abstract: NeuroD1 is a master transcription factor governing neuronal differentiation and subtype specification, yet its potential to restore striatal identity in Huntington's disease (HD) remains unresolved. In HD, striosomal D2 striatal projection neurons (SPNs) represent the earliest and most selectively vulnerable population, leading to early collapse of striatal compartmental organization. Here, we show that astrocyte-targeted expression of NeuroD1, via AAV9-mediated delivery of NeuroD1 under the GFAP promoter in a transgenic murine model of HD, reinstates hallmarks of inhibitory neuronal maturation, synaptic proteins, and chloride homeostasis in the striatum. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing further revealed selective recovery of striosomal D2 transcriptional programs and compartment-specific molecular signatures. NeuroD1 treatment promoted the partial reorganization of striosome-matrix compartmental distinctions, including the restoration of MOR1-defined striosomal domains. These cellular and circuit-level restorations were accompanied by significant amelioration of functional deficits in motor coordination and clasping behaviors. Together, these findings establish astroglial NeuroD1-mediated identity reinforcement as a potential strategy to counter subtype- and compartment-specific circuit disintegration in HD.

works.title: Mosaic Hemagglutinin-Based Influenza B mRNA-LNP Vaccine Induces Strong Humoral Immune Response in Non-Human Primates
works.abstract: Developing broadly protective influenza vaccines remains a major challenge for global public health. Influenza B viruses cause about one-third of all annual influenza virus infections and current vaccines only show moderate effectiveness against matched virus strains, therefore, development of more effective and broadly protective vaccines against them is important. Chimeric and mosaic hemagglutinin (cHA and mHA) immunogens are under investigation as broadly protective influenza B vaccine candidates. The lipid nanoparticle (LNP)-encapsulated nucleoside-modified mRNA technology has recently revolutionized vaccination and gained widespread interest due to its successful use in the coronavirus disease 2019 pandemic. Here, we evaluated influenza B cHA and mHA mRNA-LNP vaccines in non-human primates and compared their immunogenicity to a quadrivalent seasonal influenza virus vaccine. mHA mRNA-LNPs induced high binding antibody titers against antigenically distant influenza B virus strains, with significant hemagglutination inhibition and antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity activity and provided protection in mice in a serum transfer challenge experiment. This approach shows great promise for developing broadly protective influenza B vaccines.

works.title: Development of an Efficient and Precise TadA-based C-to-G Base Editor Mi-zCGBE
works.abstract: C-to-G base editors (CGBEs) offer the potential to correct 11% of pathogenic single-nucleotide variants. While APOBEC-based CGBEs are highly efficient, they are limited by high indel rates and off-target activity. In contrast, TadA-based CGBEs offer greater precision but currently suffer from suboptimal editing efficiency. In this study, we first developed zCGBE, a TadA-based variant that achieves editing efficiency comparable to APOBEC-based editors while maintaining low Cas-independent off-target activity. To further reduce residual on-target indels, we engineered mi-zCGBE by fusing Brex27, a 36-amino-acid-long RAD51-recruiting peptide, to zCGBE. Mi-zCGBE preserves high C-to-G editing capacity and low Cas9-independent off-target activity while significantly reducing both on-target indels and guide-RNA-dependent off-target effects. We demonstrated the potential utility of mi-zCGBE by correcting the CFTR-N1303K mutation in Cystic Fibrosis patient-derived bronchial epithelial cells, achieving high rates of base correction and minimal indels or off-target edits, leading to restored CFTR protein expression and functional chloride channel activity. These results establish mi-zCGBE as an efficient and precise tool for gene editing research and future therapeutic applications.

works.abstract: Modern drug discovery attrition is often attributed to biological complexity or target invalidation. However, a core obstacle may lie in the industry's asymmetric focus on maximizing binding affinity at the expense of holistic molecular quality, driven by a pervasive potency bias. This produces overengineered leads that collide with an 'Activity Wall', defined here as the multifactorial barrier that prevents chemical analogs from being optimized indefinitely, in which further affinity gains cease to translate into therapeutic success. By exploring chemical space through scaffold-based constellation plots and ligand lipophilic efficiency, we show how structural modifications improve potency primarily via lipophilicity inflation within established scaffolds. This is illustrated by analyzing small-molecule inhibitors of two key Alzheimer's targets: beta-site APP cleaving enzyme 1 and the Tau protein.

works.abstract: • The Clinical Global Impression Scale (CGIS) is an important assessment as a regulatory endpoint and anchor for symptom scales. • Psychometric issues, leading to low sensitivity in the CGIS, have given rise to numerous disease-specific scales. • In the Alzheimer’s disease field, use of the CGIS has transitioned to activities of daily living and functional scales. • Future use of the CGIS will need to examine its purpose in therapeutic evaluation. The Clinical Global Impression (CGI) Scale was developed as an efficient means to capture drug effect in the burgeoning field of psychopharmacology during the 1960s and 1970s. It has also served as an anchor for scaling symptom scale results and as a regulatory endpoint. For reasons largely related to its lack of definition, disease-specific versions have been developed. The overlap between these CGIs and symptom scales raises a question as to the utility of a global scale. Future direction in this issue could be directed by increased use of the Activity of Daily Living or Functionality Scales to describe clinical meaningfulness.

works.abstract: Conventional ex vivo chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy is limited by cumbersome manufacturing workflows, prohibitive costs and various treatment-related risks. In vivo CAR-T technology directly generates engineered cells within patients, conferring distinct advantages in operational simplicity, biosafety and clinical accessibility. This review systematically evaluates existing delivery platforms and classifies in vivo CAR-T into two core paradigms: persistent engineering and transient reprogramming, each featuring distinct properties tailored to different clinical indications. It further summarizes preclinical advances and clinical data covering hematological malignancies, solid tumors, autoimmune disorders and organ fibrosis, in which numerous investigational candidates have exhibited encouraging efficacy. Ultimately, five translational barriers summarized as the 5S challenges (specificity, stability, safety, suppression and scalability) and their matched optimization tactics are comprehensively discussed. This review provides a clinician-oriented decision matrix that links carriers selection to disease biology, and a 5S optimization framework to guide next-generation vector design. Collectively, these insights establish a translational roadmap for customizing in vivo CAR-T design to specific clinical indications and take a critical step toward realizing the full therapeutic potential of this disruptive modality.

works.title: Overcoming technological and biological barriers to pulmonary mRNA delivery with lipid-polymer hybrid nanoparticles
works.abstract: Delivering mRNA to the lungs promises treatment of genetic, infectious and non-communicable lung diseases. Yet, conventional lipid nanoparticle formulations lack the stability needed to endure the harsh mechanical stress during nebulization. Additionally, once deposited in the respiratory tract, gene delivery systems may first have to overcome the mucus barrier, before actually transfecting the target cells. To overcome these challenges, we utilize lipid-polymer hybrid nanoparticles (LPH), merging the stability of pharmaceutical polymers with the transfection efficiency of cationic and ionizable lipids. LPH are produced in a robust microfluidic process, accomplish near-complete encapsulation efficiency, even after nebulization, and confer high transfection efficiency in A549 cells. To provide colloidal stability after aerosolization, we developed a coating strategy with hyaluronic acid (HA) and poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA), ensuring ideal nebulization stability by steric shielding. This formulation showed good transfection efficiency of air-liquid interface grown Calu-3 cells, producing and covered by mucus. The potential of LPH to deliver mRNA to mammalian cells was first shown in primary human lung fibroblasts in vitro and could also be confirmed after intratracheal administration to mice in vivo. Together, these findings validate LPH as a versatile and aerosolizable mRNA delivery platform, overcoming the key technological and biological barriers in pulmonary gene delivery.

Machine Learning Modeling for Solubility Prediction in Pharmaceutical-Ionic Liquid Systems with Deep Feature Search
works.abstract: Abstract Drug solubility is a critical determinant of bioavailability and therapeutic efficacy in pharmaceutical development, with poorly soluble compounds presenting significant formulation challenges. Ionic liquids (ILs) have emerged as promising solubilizing agents due to their tunable physicochemical properties and ability to enhance drug dissolution. While machine learning (ML) has shown promise in predicting various IL properties, its application to pharmaceutical solubility prediction in IL media remains underexplored, largely due to the fragmented experimental data reported, the inherent complexity of binary (or multi-component) pharmaceutical−IL systems, and the susceptibility of conventional feature selection methods to overfitting on small datasets. This study addresses this gap by developing a data-driven quantitative structure−property relationship (QSPR) model for solubility prediction in pharmaceutical−IL systems. We curated a comprehensive experimental dataset comprising 234 solubility measurements spanning diverse pharmaceuticals and ILs (including binary IL mixtures, where IL1 and IL2 denote the two constituent ionic liquids) across varying temperatures. From SMILES representations of molecular structures, we computed 155 molecular descriptors using RDKit, followed by rigorous preprocessing including variance thresholding and Yeo-Johnson transformation. Two complementary feature selection strategies, deep feature selection (DFS) and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), were employed to identify the most predictive descriptors. Four regression models, including random forest (RF), extreme gradient boosting (XGB), decision tree (DT), and multilayer perceptron (MLP), were evaluated on the selected features. Under the adopted validation framework, DFS-selected features produced more consistent out-of-sample performance than SHAP-selected features, with XGB achieving the highest test performance (R2 = 0.84). While DFS prioritized structural descriptors (e.g., bicyclic rings and aromatic systems), SHAP analysis revealed that temperature and IL composition ratios exert the strongest influence on final predictions. This work establishes a reliable ML framework for solubility prediction in pharmaceutical−IL systems, providing valuable guidance for the rational design of IL-based drug delivery formulations.

works.abstract: PHERGain was a randomized, non-comparative phase 2 trial evaluating a positron 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose-positron emission tomography (18F-FDG-PET)-guided, pathological complete response (pCR)-adapted strategy to omit chemotherapy in HER2-positive early breast cancer. Female patients with HER2-positive stages I–IIIA operable breast cancer (tumor size ≥ 1.5 cm) were randomized to receive chemotherapy plus trastuzumab and pertuzumab (HP; group A) or HP ± endocrine therapy (group B). In group B, treatment was adapted according to 18F-FDG-PET response after two cycles and pCR, with chemotherapy administered to nonresponders or patients without pCR. We previously reported that this de-escalation approach revealed a 3-year invasive disease-free survival (iDFS) of 94.3% (95% confidence interval (CI): 90.9 to 96.8) in group B. Here we report the prespecified secondary endpoint, 5-year iDFS and exploratory circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) findings. After a median follow-up of 5.6 years, the 5-year iDFS was 89.5% (95% CI: 85.7 to 93.4) in group B (n = 267) and 92.4% (95% CI: 86.7 to 98.5) among 18F-FDG-PET responders achieving pCR without chemotherapy (n = 86), with one distant recurrence. The latter estimate describes a long-term outcome in a post-randomization subgroup defined by 18F-FDG-PET response and pCR and should be interpreted as descriptive rather than as causal effects of omitting chemotherapy. Detectable ctDNA at baseline or during treatment was associated with inferior iDFS, whereas ctDNA clearance correlated with higher pCR rates and improved long-term outcomes. These findings continue to support the clinical validity of an 18F-FDG-PET-guided, pCR-adapted approach and suggest a potential role for ctDNA in refining treatment individualization. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03161353 . A 5-year secondary analysis of the phase 2 PHERGain trial supports the clinical utility of a PET-guided adaptive strategy for treatment de-escalation in HER2-positive early breast cancer and provides circulating tumor DNA insights that could inform further treatment approaches.

works.title: A clinical multimodal vision language foundation model with fine-grain explainability
works.abstract: Despite their considerable promise, many current medical foundation models remain modality specific and lack transparent reasoning, limiting clinical adoption. To address this gap, we introduce Explainable Vision Language Foundation Model for Medicine (EVLF-FM), a multimodal vision language foundation model that combines broad diagnostic capabilities with fine-grained explainability. The development and testing of EVLF-FM encompassed more than 1.3 million total samples from 18 global datasets across 10 imaging modalities related to six clinical specialties: dermatology, hepatology, ophthalmology, pathology, pulmonology and radiology. External validation employed 13,443 independent test samples from 17 additional datasets across 10 imaging modalities. EVLF-FM supports disease diagnosis, visual question answering and pixel-level visual grounding with reasoning capabilities. In internal validation for disease diagnostics, EVLF-FM achieved the highest average accuracy, 0.895, outperforming leading generalist and specialist models. In medical visual grounding, EVLF-FM also achieved reasonable performance across nine modalities with average accuracy at 0.5 intersection over union (Acc@0.5) of 0.842. External testing further confirmed consistent zero-shot and few-shot performance, with competitive F1 scores despite a smaller model size. A hybrid training strategy combining supervised and visual reinforcement fine-tuning enables EVLF-FM to generate clinically interpretable explanations aligned with visual evidence. Human evaluation of these reasoning outputs using the S.C.O.R.E. framework yielded a high overall mean score of 4.25/5, supporting their clinical interpretability. Current limitations include the need for additional validation across diverse healthcare settings. Prospective clinical studies are required to evaluate the safety, effectiveness and clinical utility of EVLF-FM before routine clinical deployment.

works.title: Applying digital twins to prevent preterm births
A small-molecule TREM2 agonist for Alzheimer’s disease
Insights into early-onset colorectal cancer from a single-nucleus RNA-seq atlas of colorectal cancer across the age continuum
works.abstract: The incidence of early-onset colorectal cancer (EO-CRC; diagnosed before age 50 years) is increasing worldwide. Although current data indicate that EO-CRC may be biologically distinct from average-onset CRC (AO-CRC; diagnosed at age ≥50 years), molecular differences remain poorly defined. To address this knowledge gap, we generated a single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) atlas from 189 primary CRC tumors (54 EO-CRC, 135 AO-CRC) spanning eight decades of life, with at least 20 tumors in most age decades. Our analyses stratified tumors by microsatellite status and accounted for tumor sidedness, stage, patient sex and neoadjuvant treatment history, modeling age continuously or categorically (EO-CRC versus AO-CRC). Among microsatellite-stable (MSS) tumors, those from younger patients were characterized by increased stromal and decreased epithelial proportions, which we confirmed using multispectral immunofluorescence and machine learning in an external cohort of 712 MSS CRC tumors (18 EO-CRC, 694 AO-CRC). Tumor epithelial cells from young patients exhibited increased expression of long noncoding RNAs and FN1, with a trend toward increased heterogeneity in copy number alterations. MSS left-sided EO-CRC tumors had more cell-cell interactions, with epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition-related signaling pathways (FN1/GDF/ACTIVIN) showing increased, cell type-specific interactions. Our large high-resolution snRNA-seq atlas uncovers age-associated features of CRC and provides a resource for the community to understand EO-CRC biology.

works.title: Letter to Editor: Clarifying the classification of normal organ biodistribution in a meta-analysis of polymeric Micelle Tumour delivery
Tetrahedral DNA engineered Janus nanoplatform for potentiated Zn2+ interference therapy and cGAS-STING activation via efficient delivery of exogenous DNA
Dissolving Polymeric Microneedles for Enhanced Transdermal Drug Delivery: Formulation Optimization, Characterization, and Permeation Studies
works.abstract: Abstract This investigation aimed to fabricate and optimize dissolving microneedle patches composed of hydroxypropyl methylcellulose and polyvinylpyrrolidone for transdermal delivery of two model drugs: berberine chloride (BBR) and salmon calcitonin (sCT). Dissolving microneedles were prepared using the micromolding technique. The effects of polymer type, concentration, polymer blending ratios, and vacuum-assisted air bubble removal duration on microneedle morphology, mechanical strength, and rheological behavior were investigated. In vitro drug permeation and skin retention were evaluated using vertical diffusion cells with excised mouse skin. A vacuum duration of 15 min × 2 cycles was optimal for complete air removal from the polymeric solution. Among the four polymers screened, HPMC E3 and PVP K10 yielded microneedles with superior morphology, greater needle lengths, and lower percentage length reduction upon compression. All polymer solutions displayed pseudoplastic flow behavior, and viscosity decreased with increasing temperature. Two optimized formulations were selected: MN6.3 (HPMC E3 10%/PVP K10 30%) and MN7.2 (HPMC E3 20%/PVP K10 20%). In vitro permeation studies revealed that MN7.2 released 49.45 ± 3.82% of BBR and 16.16 ± 0.48% of sCT through mouse skin over 24 h, substantially higher than the corresponding control patches (39.80 ± 4.70% and 9.26 ± 0.55%, respectively, n = 4, p < 0.05). Drug loading, transdermal permeation, percentage of drug released, lag time, steady-state flux, and drug quantity in skin were reported and compared among the groups. Conclusively, HPMC E3/PVP K10 dissolving microneedles represent a promising platform for enhancing transdermal delivery of drugs spanning a wide molecular weight range, from small hydrophilic alkaloids to large peptides.

works.title: Closing the loop on blood flow control in spinal cord injury
Optimal closed-loop feedback control of blood flow after spinal cord injury with norepinephrine
works.abstract: After spinal cord injury, clinical management aims to support tissue perfusion, but current methods rely on the indirect control of arterial blood pressure without direct measurement of the local blood flow. This limits the ability to tailor drug delivery to the injured tissue. Here, we show that spinal cord blood flow can be regulated using a closed-loop controller that adjusts vasopressor infusion on the basis of real-time ultrasound flow measurement. We characterize the dynamic relationship between drug infusion, arterial pressure and spinal cord blood flow, and we use these data to design a feedback controller that targets a predefined flow level. We validate the system in simulations, implement the controller in real time in rodents and translate it to pigs. We show that the controller reduced blood flow deviations and variability compared with constant dosing and supported functional recovery in a rodent survival model. These results show a closed-loop spinal cord perfusion control strategy that leverages clinically available measurements and pharmacological interventions, supporting its translation to clinical settings for the management of acute spinal cord injury.

works.title: SprintX: mitigating data scarcity in antibody design via synthetic structural prior knowledge dataset
works.abstract: Structure-based artificial intelligence (AI)-driven antibody design is increasingly important for therapeutic development, yet progress has been hindered by the scarcity of high-quality antibody-antigen complex structures for model training. To alleviate this bottleneck, we introduce SprintX (Structural Prior for Antibody-Antigen CompleXes), a large-scale AlphaFold3-derived synthetic dataset designed to provide structural prior knowledge for antibody-antigen modeling. Unlike conventional docking-based synthesis pipelines, SprintX uses AlphaFold3 to generate antigen-conditioned candidate complex-structure predictions from sampled antibody sequences paired with selected antigens, without imposing predefined binding-site or pose constraints. Candidate structures were ranked to select one representative structure per antibody-antigen pair before terminal trimming and multistage quality control. To improve reliability and learning stability, we applied a multi-stage quality-control pipeline integrating global confidence metrics, stereochemical validation, and interface-level contact analysis. SprintX recapitulated key geometric characteristics and physicochemical regularities of experimentally resolved antibody-antigen complexes while filtering out structurally unstable or implausible synthetic outputs. Across downstream tasks including antibody generation, computational binding-affinity prediction, and binding-interface prediction, models pretrained with SprintX showed meaningful improvements in structural plausibility and competitive performance on computational binding-affinity and binding-interface prediction benchmarks. These results support SprintX not as a substitute for experimentally resolved complexes, but as a complementary source of structural prior knowledge for structure-aware antibody modeling. Finally, we release SprintX as an openly accessible resource to facilitate data-efficient learning for AI-driven antibody design.

works.title: Editorial Expression of Concern: MicroRNA-133 controls cardiac hypertrophy
An mRNA–lipid nanoparticle vaccine against H5N1 influenza virus protects lactating dairy cows from infection
works.abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 virus has recently emerged in dairy cattle in the USA, leading to mastitis and sharp reductions in milk production. The main site of H5N1 viral replication is the mammary tissue rather than the respiratory tract and viral transmission between animals is thought to occur through viral shedding in milk. Here, we generate an mRNA-lipid nanoparticle (mRNA-LNP) vaccine encoding the hemagglutinin (HA) of A/dairy cattle/Texas/24-008749-002/2024, representative of circulating bovine H5N1 viruses, and assess its immunogenicity and efficacy in lactating dairy cows. Eight cows were divided into vaccinated and control groups, receiving two intramuscular doses of the vaccine or saline, followed by intramammary viral challenge. Vaccination elicited HA-reactive and neutralizing antibodies in serum and HA-reactive antibodies in milk. Following viral challenge, vaccinated cows had ~1,000-fold lower peak viral RNA in milk and a lower occurrence of mastitis and mammary fibrosis.

works.title: An engineered, compact Cas12m variant for multiplexed gene activation in vivo
Dengue virus controlled human challenge reveals that preexisting immunity shapes viral replication and broadly protective responses
works.abstract: Dengue is the canonical viral disease for which immune history is a determinant of protective versus pathogenic responses and immunogenicity. Yet, because of limitations in animal models and clinical presentation after peak viremia, how preinfection and early immune responses affect dengue outcome is not confirmed. We conducted a phase 1 clinical trial with 45 healthy adults to test whether secondary infection challenge with a heterotypic, full-length, attenuated virus increases viremia and immunogenicity compared with primary and tertiary infection. Viremia was associated with more, but still mild, clinical signs and symptoms, and secondary infection resulted in greater viremia, neutralizing antibodies, and protective T cell responses. However, those whose baseline antibodies most efficiently increased dengue virus replication in an in vitro assay experienced delayed inflammatory and adaptive immune activation, the highest viremia, strong acute immune responses, and waning of potent CD8 + T cells and antibodies. In contrast, higher baseline antibodies against the nonstructural protein 1 of multiple serotypes predicted early interferon and balanced immune activation, viremia control, and development of enduring, potent B and T cells, revealing how vaccines can induce broad, long-lasting protection. Last, individuals with potent and neutralizing antibodies and IFN-γ + T cells at baseline experienced minimal viral replication. Together, these findings demonstrate that controlled human challenge with dengue virus can delineate coordinated versus dysregulated acute immune responses and their effects on immunogenicity, informing therapeutic and vaccine strategies for dengue and other viral diseases.

works.title: Brain-sensing synNotch–CAR T cells enable precise targeting and clearance of diffuse midline glioma in multiple preclinical models
works.abstract: Diffuse midline glioma (DMG) is a lethal pediatric brain tumor with limited therapeutic options and a poor prognosis. The success of chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy requires both improving T cell tumor infiltration and persistence and reducing the risk of on-target/off-tumor toxicity. Here, we adapted and advanced a brain-restricted CAR T cell platform previously validated in glioblastoma to address the anatomical and biological challenges of DMG. We engineered a T cell circuit in which a brain-specific synthetic Notch (synNotch) receptor recognizing brevican (BCAN) induced CAR expression against EphA2 or IL-13Rα2 ("B-SYNC"), thereby restricting CAR expression to the central nervous system (CNS). In immunodeficient DMG models, a single infusion of intravenous (iv) or intracerebroventricular (icv) B-SYNC circuit T cells led to tumor infiltration, sustained persistence, antitumor activity, and extended survival. An alternative BCAN-primed CAR targeting B7-H3 or IL-13Rα2 ("B-SYNC-B/I") similarly improved therapeutic efficacy when delivered intravenously. However, icv administration triggered fatal neurotoxicity because of low-level B7-H3 expression in nontumor CNS regions, indicating that rapid CNS exposure via icv delivery can amplify off-tumor toxicity. In contrast, in an immunocompetent syngeneic DMG model, both iv and icv delivery of a murinized BCAN-gated B7-H3 CAR (mB-SYNC-B7-H3) achieved durable tumor clearance and resistance to rechallenge without any detectable neurotoxicity. Mechanistically, synNotch-primed CAR T cells exhibited reduced exhaustion, enhanced activation, and enrichment of naïve and stem cell memory-like subsets. These findings demonstrate that brain-sensing synNotch CAR T circuits represent a generalizable and translatable strategy for targeting multiple CNS malignancies, including DMG.

works.title: Acute kidney injury as a systemic disease
works.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) affects ∼20% of hospitalized patients and is traditionally viewed as a transient complication of acute illness. Evidence suggests that AKI can initiate long-term renal and cardiovascular disease, even when kidney function appears to recover. Survivors of AKI face increased risks of CKD, heart failure, myocardial infarction, and premature mortality, yet post-AKI care remains poorly defined. We synthesize emerging mechanistic and clinical evidence linking AKI to systemic cardiorenal disease and discuss how biomarkers, imaging, and clinical risk prediction may enable identification of high-risk patients and support translational strategies to prevent progression to chronic disease.

works.title: Keratinocyte-derived CHI3L2 reprograms phospholipid metabolism to promote skin inflammation in psoriasis
works.abstract: Psoriasis is a chronic inflammatory skin disorder characterized by hyperproliferative keratinocytes and a dysregulated cytokine milieu, perpetuating a self-reinforcing inflammatory cycle. Despite the key involvement of keratinocytes in this pathogenic loop, the molecular pathogenesis remains incompletely understood. Here, we identify chitinase-like protein CHI3L2 as a key mediator. Elevated CHI3L2 levels were detected in serum and lesional skin from patients with psoriasis, predominantly in keratinocytes, as also verified by single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomic analyses. In vitro stimulation of keratinocytes with M5 cytokine cocktail (IL-17A, IL-22, oncostatin M, IL-1α, and TNF-α) increased CHI3L2 expression, demonstrating that CHI3L2 is inducible under inflammatory conditions. Transgenic mice expressing human CHI3L2 exhibited aggravated psoriasis-like phenotypes in both imiquimod- and mannan-induced psoriasis models, characterized by epidermal hyperplasia and scaling. To dissect the role of CHI3L2, we used recombinant protein injection, parabiosis, and bone marrow transplantation, identifying keratinocytes as the primary source of pathogenic CHI3L2. This was further confirmed by keratinocyte-specific CHI3L2 knockin mice. CHI3L2 functions in the HaCaT cell line and primary keratinocytes were investigated by recombinant CHI3L2 administration or CHI3L2 knockout. CHI3L2 disrupted phospholipid homeostasis, leading to altered inflammatory responses, proliferation, and differentiation of keratinocytes. CHI3L2 activated secretory phospholipase A2, elevating lysophosphatidylcholine, thereby establishing an autocrine loop perpetuating keratinocyte inflammation and reshaping the immune microenvironment. Therapeutic neutralization of CHI3L2 with antibodies or intervention of phospholipid pathway ameliorated skin inflammation in mouse psoriasis models. Our findings reveal CHI3L2 as an important regulator of keratinocyte-driven lipid remodeling and inflammation in psoriasis, highlighting potential as a therapeutic target.

works.title: T cell–mediated depletion of intratumoral regulatory T cells using a CCR8xCD3 T cell–engaging bispecific antibody (TCB) promotes antitumor immunity in preclinical mouse models
works.abstract: T cell–engaging bispecific antibodies (TCBs) have seen notable successes in hematologic malignancies, and emerging data demonstrate their potential for the treatment of solid tumors. Most oncology applications of TCBs have focused on targeting tumor cells via tumor-specific antigens; however, TCBs have been underutilized for strategic depletion of immunosuppressive cells in the TME. Regulatory T cells (T reg cells) play a crucial role in suppressing antitumor immune responses, making them an attractive target for immune-based therapies. T reg cells express several surface markers that can serve as potential targets for antibody-mediated depletion, including C-C chemokine receptor type 8 (CCR8), which is highly enriched on tumor-infiltrating T reg cells. Monoclonal antibody (mAb)–mediated T reg cell depletion relies on natural killer (NK) cells, which can be scarce in some solid tumors, whereas TCBs can broadly engage the T cell compartment by overwriting antigen specificity and redirecting potent T cell cytotoxicity against target cells. Here, we have developed a CCR8xCD3 TCB and show that it effectively depletes CCR8-expressing T reg cells in a T cell–mediated manner. CCR8xCD3 TCB led to the selective depletion of intratumoral T reg cells from human solid tumor samples in vitro and mediated inhibition of tumor growth in multiple syngeneic tumor models with variable levels of T cell infiltration alone or in combination with anti–PD-L1. In cynomolgus monkeys, CCR8xCD3 TCB was well tolerated without evidence of acute phase inflammation or cytokine release syndrome and led to effective and durable depletion of the CCR8-expressing subset of T reg cells.

works.title: MIF-CD74 orchestrates synovial macrophage metabolic-inflammatory reprogramming by ENO2 interaction to drive osteoarthritis pathogenesis
works.abstract: Synovitis is a central driver of osteoarthritis (OA) progression, yet the cellular and molecular mechanisms sustaining inflammatory circuits in the synovium remain incompletely understood. Through integrative analysis of time-resolved single-cell RNA sequencing in murine synovium and spatial transcriptomics of human OA tissues, we identified a pathogenic CD74 + macrophage subset that expands in OA and localizes at the synovial-cartilage interface. This subset exhibits a proinflammatory, nonclassical polarization and displays a metabolic dependency on glycolysis. Multiomics and mechanistic studies revealed that CD74 interacts with the glycolytic enzyme enolase 2 (ENO2). This interaction orchestrates a feed-forward signaling axis wherein CD74/ENO2 facilitates the nuclear translocation of hypoxia-inducible factor 1-α (HIF-1α)/β-catenin dimers, which coactivate glycolytic and inflammatory gene programs, thereby sustaining a metabolically driven inflammatory state. Genetic ablation of CD74 in myeloid cells or its pharmacological blockade mitigated synovitis and cartilage degradation in murine OA models. To translate this axis therapeutically, we developed synovium-targeted cationic lipid nanoparticles decorated with MIF-mimetic peptides (PcLNPs) for the delivery of CD74 siRNA. Intra-articular administration of PcLNPs efficiently targeted CD74 + macrophages, attenuated their inflammatory and glycolytic phenotypes, and ameliorated murine OA progression in vivo. Our findings establish the CD74/ENO2/HIF-1α/β-catenin axis as a critical integrator of metabolic reprogramming and inflammation in OA synovitis and present a potential targeted nanotherapeutic strategy for disease modification.

works.title: B cell subsets are associated with durable responses in distinct cancer types after immune checkpoint inhibition
works.abstract: B cells are a critical arm of the adaptive immune system. However, the impact of B cells and antibody responses on overall cancer survival remains understudied. Here, we report results from a prospective randomized phase 2 trial of 106 patients treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) and identify that B cell antibody responses are associated with exceptional complete responses to ICI in certain cancer types. To further dissect the impact of B cell subtypes, we generated a comprehensive single-cell RNA sequencing database of intratumoral B cells in 12 tumor types from 152 patients. We found a context-dependent role for B cells, in which they are beneficial in certain cancer types and potentially unfavorable in others, with germinal center and memory B cells enriched in favorable prognosis cohorts and immunoglobulin A-positive plasma cells enriched in unfavorable prognosis cohorts. Depletion of B cells using rituximab in patients before surgery affected intratumoral T cell frequency and diversity. Furthermore, we show that B cells improve long-term overall survival even when T cell infiltrates are already high, indicating that a coordinated dual-arm T cell and B cell adaptive immune response is key to long-term tumor control. Overall, these results demonstrate that B cells and antibody responses in the proper context play an important role in durable complete responses in multiple tumor types.

works.title: Nanoarchitectonics via emulsion interfacial in situ polymerization for enhanced cross-presentation and antitumor immunity
Additive manufacturing as a unifying platform across drug discovery, drug delivery, and theranostics

Engineering human brain microphysiological systems for alzheimer’s disease (AD) and chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE) modeling and drug testing: translational promise, limitations, and future directions
works.abstract: This review examines the emerging role of human brain microphysiological systems (HBMPS) in recapitulating diseases and evaluating their translational potential and limitations for Alzheimer's disease (AD) and chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE). Both disorders differ in underlying cause, but converge on shared downstream pathophysiology such as tau pathology, neuroinflammation, and blood-brain barrier (BBB) dysfunction. We review the critical pathophysiological features relevant to modeling AD and CTE and introduce HBMPS platforms/validation strategies as potential tools for evaluating therapeutic compounds as well as drug-delivery approaches. We also provide a systematic comparison of the relative advantages and disadvantages of 2D, HBMPS, Xenograft, and animal models and discuss the future potential of HBMPS's drug-testing platform. We further discuss current challenges of HBMPS related to drug testing, engineering extracellular matrix for tissue chips, and BBB penetration in AD and CTE. We suggest future integration of organoid xenografts and AI-assisted frameworks to enhance pathophysiological fidelity/drug predictive capability and to bridge the gap between HBMPS and animal models. In summary, this paper reviews HBMPS technologies as future translation platforms' direction for drug screening and delivery, while providing current limitations and challenges including model validation, reproducibility, and standardized regulatory bases required for preclinical success for HBMPS use. Rather than comparing biological complexity with translational validity, this review applies a decision-oriented framework that distinguishes mechanistic fidelity, comparative candidate ranking, predictive validation, investigational new drug (IND)-supporting use, and replacement of a defined animal test. For each use, we identify quantitative transport, exposure-response, pharmacodynamic, safety, and reproducibility evidence required to support an advance, redesign, or go/stop decision.

works.title: Correction to “Predicting First-in-Human Pharmacokinetics: Comparative Evaluation of Standard PBPK, High-Throughput PBPK, and Machine Learning”
Fluoxetine attenuates asthma symptoms in a murine model through modulation of innate and adaptive immune components, and regulation of ROR γ t signalling axis in a pathogenic Th17 cell population
works.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Asthma is a heterogeneous chronic inflammatory airway disease, characterised by dysregulated interactions between innate and adaptive immune cells. Although Th2-mediated inflammation predominates, persistent Th17-associated immune responses contribute to chronic airway inflammation implicated in the corticosteroid-insensitive disease state. Fluoxetine, a SSRI with immunomodulatory properties, was investigated to determine its effects on inflammation and Th17 response in experimental allergic airway disease. EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: Immunomodulatory effects of fluoxetine evaluated in exploratory in vitro assays. In vivo studies were performed in an ovalbumin (OVA)-induced murine model of allergic asthma using oral fluoxetine at clinically relevant doses. Airway pathology, immunophenotypes, cytokine production, gene and protein expression were evaluated by histology, flow cytometry, quantitative reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR), confocal microscopy and ex vivo functional assays. Public transcriptomic datasets were integrated with target enrichment analyses, molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations used to explore potential molecular interactions. KEY RESULTS: Fluoxetine reduced the inflammatory response in activated macrophages without noticeable cytotoxicity. In an allergic asthma model, fluoxetine attenuated inflammatory cell infiltration, eosinophilia, IgE production and pulmonary macrophage activation, whilst reducing the accumulation of the phenotypically granulocytic myeloid-derived suppressor like cell population along with diminished T-cell activation and reduced Th17 responses, reduced IL-17 production together with decreased expression and nuclear localisation of RORγt. Ex vivo studies confirmed inhibition of RORγt expression and IL-17 production in Th17 cells. Transcriptomic integration identified significant enrichment of Th17-associated inflammatory pathways, whereas molecular docking and molecular dynamics analyses supported RORγt as a plausible molecular target. CONCLUSION AND IMPLICATIONS: Fluoxetine attenuates experimental allergic airway inflammation through coordinated modulation of innate and adaptive immune responses, with suppression of the RORγt-IL-17 signalling axis emerging as a key mechanistic feature. These findings expand the immunopharmacological profile of fluoxetine and provide an experimental rationale for further investigating its therapeutic potential in Th17-associated airway inflammatory diseases and in experimental models that more closely recapitulate corticosteroid-resistant asthma.

works.title: GLP‐1 receptor activation attenuates chronic migraine‐like behaviour: Sex‐specific modulation of opioid‐ and endocannabinoid‐related pathways
works.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Chronic migraine (CM) is a highly disabling condition that remains suboptimally treated. Metabolic disturbances may trigger migraine chronification, whereas impaired endogenous pain inhibition contributes to CM development. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs), used for type 2 diabetes and obesity, show efficacy in chronic pain models. We evaluated the prophylactic effects of liraglutide, semaglutide and dulaglutide compared with propranolol (reference drug), potential opioidergic/endocannabinoid involvement and sex differences in a CM model. EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: Chronic migraine-like hypersensitivity was induced by repeated nitroglycerin administration in male and female mice. The prophylactic effects of GLP-1RAs and propranolol were examined using von Frey, acetone and orofacial glutamate tests. Body weight and glucose tolerance were monitored to evaluate metabolic safety. Potential opioidergic/endocannabinoid involvement in semaglutide-induced antinociception (selected GLP-1RA class representative) was assessed by pharmacological blockade and/or quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) analysis of pain-related neurobiomarker mRNA expression in brainstem and trigeminal ganglia. KEY RESULTS: Liraglutide, semaglutide and dulaglutide dose-dependently attenuated CM-like hypersensitivity in both sexes, with efficacy comparable to propranolol. GLP-1RAs did not affect metabolic parameters, whereas propranolol induced male-specific hyperglycaemia. Semaglutide-induced antinociception was partially sensitive to naloxone and was associated with sex-dimorphic, brainstem-specific transcriptional changes in opioid- and endocannabinoid-related pathways. Semaglutide increased Glp1r, Cnr1, Pomc, Pcsk1 and Pcsk2 mRNA expression in males, whereas it up-regulated Glp1r and down-regulated Faah and Mgll in females. CONCLUSIONS AND IMPLICATIONS: GLP-1RAs exert class-wide antinociceptive effects in a preclinical CM model, with semaglutide-based analyses suggesting sex-specific modulation of central opioid- and endocannabinoid-related pathways. These findings support further investigation of GLP-1RAs as prophylactic strategies for migraine, particularly in individuals with metabolic comorbidities.

works.title: Metabolic heterogeneity of obesity
Persistent and compartmentalized T cell immunity in ALS
works.abstract: Abstract Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis is a fatal neurodegenerative disease increasingly linked to T cell responses, although the mechanisms driving T cell activation and disease progression remain unclear. Here we used single-cell RNA and T cell receptor sequencing, longitudinal immune profiling and imaging flow cytometry to identify long-lived intrathecal clonotypes and antigen-presenting cell–T cell complexes displaying features of immunological synapse formation, consistent with intrathecal antigen presentation. Higher frequencies of CD4 + effector, CD4 + regulatory and CD8 + T cells in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) were associated with slower disease progression, whereas increased circulating CD4 + effector and regulatory T cells were associated with faster progression. T cell clonotypes shared between blood and CSF exhibited distinct transcriptional states. Finally, frequencies of cytomegalovirus-specific T cells in CSF and anticytomegalovirus serum antibodies were correlated with faster progression and shorter survival in sporadic amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. These findings reveal compartmentalized immune dynamics, largely contrasting protective intrathecal responses with harmful systemic activation.

works.title: Author Correction: Toripalimab or placebo plus chemotherapy as first-line treatment in advanced nasopharyngeal carcinoma: a multicenter randomized phase 3 trial
Uncovering the lymphatic uptake, pharmacokinetics, and biodistribution of mRNA-lipid nanoparticles after intravenous and subcutaneous injection
works.abstract: Lipid nanoparticle (LNP) formulations have enabled the in vivo delivery of messenger ribonucleic acid (mRNA) vaccines and therapeutics yet the delivery of RNA remains relatively inefficient. In order to improve LNP design there is a need to better understand how current mRNA-LNP formulations are trafficked and expressed in vivo. Importantly, no prior work has quantified mRNA-LNP transport through lymphatics. In the current study we profile the thoracic lymph uptake, plasma pharmacokinetics (PK), and tissue protein expression after intravenous (IV) and subcutaneous (SC) administration in rats of three common LNP formulations (ALC-0315, SM-102 and MC3 ionizable lipids) containing muGFP-P2A-nLuc reporter mRNA. After IV administration, the SM-102 and MC3 LNP formulations provided the most effective protection of mRNA in plasma. Despite this, tissue NanoLuc® Luciferase (nLuc) expression at 32 h post-dosing was relatively similar across formulations with highest expression seen in the liver and spleen. After SC injection, all formulations supported relatively low bioavailability of mRNA (0.42-0.87% dose) and slightly higher bioavailability of ionizable and PEG lipid (<5% dose) with PK profiles of the ionizable lipid and PEG lipid not completely matching the mRNA PK profiles. There was also greater lymphatic recovery of all ionizable lipids (3.1-4.3% dose) compared to mRNA (0.62-1.4% dose) and PEG lipid (1.9-2.0% dose). Together these data suggest that mRNA is lost prior to or during lymphatic transport. Importantly, concentrations of all mRNA-LNP components were 10-1000 fold higher in thoracic lymph compared to plasma after SC injection. At 32 h after SC injection, highest nLuc expression was seen in lymph nodes and tissues near the dosing site and in the liver and spleen. These findings demonstrating that mRNA-LNPs predominantly traffic from tissue injection sites via lymphatics, mRNA-LNP components may traffic separately from each other in both lymph and blood, and tissue protein expression reflects the PK of mRNA-LNPs at early timepoints.

works.title: Ritlecitinib lipid microsphere development and model-facilitated determination of regional gastrointestinal delivery in healthy volunteers
works.abstract: Colonic drug delivery has the potential to provide therapeutic benefit for diseases like Ulcerative Colitis (UC) and Crohn's disease (CD) by elevating local drug concentrations while minimizing adverse effects associated with systemic exposure. Achieving colonic drug delivery requires deliberate formulation development optimally supported by Physiologically Based Biopharmaceutics Models (PBBMs) that may predict colonocyte exposure and drug concentration in the colon lumen. In this study, ritlecitinib (Litfulo™), a covalent inhibitor of JAK3 and TEC family kinases, was incorporated into modified release (MR) lipid microsphere formulations to achieve colonic delivery. To assess in vivo performance, two ritlecitinib MR formulations were administered to healthy human volunteers, pre- and post-prandially, and a ritlecitinib oral solution was administered as a control. Using a combination of the resulting pharmacokinetic dataset, ritlecitinib physicochemical properties, in vitro release profiles of the administered formulations, and formulation-specific gastrointestinal transit profiles, a PBBM was established to predict the ritlecitinib dose fraction absorbed in each gastrointestinal compartment, pre- and post-prandially. In the fasted state, the ritlecitinib dose fraction absorbed in the colon (Fa colon ) was enhanced for both the faster-releasing (Fa colon : 0.38 ± 0.07) and slower-releasing (Fa colon : 0.40 ± 0.08) MR formulations relative to the oral solution (Fa colon : 0.01 ± 0.01). In the fed state, Fa colon was consistent for the slower-releasing formulation (Fa colon : 0.38 ± 0.07), whereas Fa colon for the faster-releasing formulation was notably reduced (Fa colon : 0.27 ± 0.09), indicating that consistent colonic delivery across prandial states depends on release rate optimization. Clinical Trial Records: ClinicalTrials.gov ID NCT06172348; EU CTR number 2023-505603-23-00

works.title: Sustained Tobramycin (Antibiotic) Release from Poly(lactic- co -glycolic Acid)-Polymethyl Methacrylate (PLGA-PMMA) and PLGA−PLGA Core−Shell Electrospun Nanofiber Mats for Ophthalmic Drug Delivery
works.abstract: Abstract Postoperative ophthalmic therapy requires sustained local antibiotic delivery, whereas conventional eye drops suffer from rapid clearance and limited patient compliance. Here, electrospun nanofiber mats were developed for sustained tobramycin (antibiotic) release, with emphasis on the transition from monolithic poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA)-based fibers to poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid)-polymethyl methacrylate (PLGA-PMMA) core−shell architectures. Monolithic PLGA/polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) and PLGA fibers exhibited burst-dominated release, with rapid drug accessibility within minutes to hours despite changes in polymer composition and molecular weight. In contrast, coaxially electrospun PLGA-PMMA core−shell nanofibers remained structurally stable in phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) environment and substantially suppressed early release. The PMMA shell−PLGA core system released approximately 9% of the loaded tobramycin within the first 6 h and approximately 34% over 60 days, demonstrating sustained delivery from a stable nanofiber architecture. The measured release profiles were described using a single-stage desorption-limited model, and the extracted parameters revealed a clear transition from a burst-dominated monolithic release to a shell-regulated transport, with reduced accessible drug fraction, longer characteristic release time, lower effective diffusivity, and higher tobramycin desorption activation energy for the core−shell systems. These results demonstrate that architectural control, rather than polymer selection alone, is critical for suppressing burst release. The architectural control enables long-term ophthalmic drug delivery and the developed PLGA-PMMA core−shell nanofibers provide a promising platform for postoperative sustained antibiotic release.

works.title: Exploration and Evaluation of PEGylation and Aromatic Substitution of Covalent FAP-Targeted Radiopharmaceuticals: Preclinical and Preliminary Clinical Studies
works.abstract: Abstract Fibroblast activation protein (FAP) is an attractive target for cancer theranostics; however, currently available FAP-targeted radiopharmaceuticals often exhibit rapid clearance and insufficient tumor retention. In this study, we designed two covalently modified FAP-targeted radiotracers, [68Ga]Ga-T1 and [68Ga]Ga-T2, by incorporating a sulfonyl fluoride (SuFEx) covalent warhead together with PEGylation and naphthalene substitution strategies. Both tracers were synthesized successfully and radiolabeled with 68Ga at high radiochemical purity (>98%). Molecular docking demonstrated favorable binding to FAP, with docking scores of −7.9 kcal/mol for T1 and −7.1 kcal/mol for T2, and both tracers showed high binding affinity in U87MG cells (IC50 = 4.46 nM and 6.63 nM, respectively). In U87MG tumor-bearing mice, both tracers showed specific tumor targeting and prolonged tumor retention, achieving a tumor uptake of 9.21 ± 0.26 %ID/g and 10.48 ± 1.80 %ID/g at 1 h post injection for [68Ga]Ga-T1 and [68Ga]Ga-T2, respectively, and FAP expression in the xenografts was confirmed by immunohistochemistry. No treatment-related toxicity was observed at doses up to 37 MBq. Preliminary clinical PET imaging further confirmed effective tumor visualization with [68Ga]Ga-T1 in two patients with lung cancer. Notably, increased uptake in glandular tissues, particularly the thyroid and pancreas, was observed in humans but was not predicted by preclinical biodistribution studies. Collectively, these findings demonstrate the feasibility of applying a covalent targeting strategy to FAP-directed molecular imaging and provide initial insights into the pharmacokinetic and biodistribution characteristics of covalent FAP-targeted radiopharmaceuticals. The results further suggest that optimization principles established for noncovalent FAP inhibitors may not be directly transferable to covalent systems, offering considerations for a future probe design.

works.title: Incretin and nutrient-sensing GPCR therapeutics in type 2 diabetes: What target–modality–formulation matching explains
works.abstract: Receptor-directed therapeutics now dominate type 2 diabetes, yet their clinical value depends on more than target biology. This review proposes a pharmaceutics-centered framework spanning the receptors for glucagon-like peptide-1, glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide and glucagon, amylin co-agonism and selected nutrient-sensing receptors, it then tests against a defined cohort of 49 programs that reached Phase II in type 2 diabetes. Among arrests with a disclosed scientific cause, modality predominates; two-thirds of arrests were unexplained or attributed to portfolio decisions. Deliverability discriminates among comparable mechanisms, cannot raise a low receptor ceiling and is poorly served by the public record.

works.title: Neoadjuvant durvalumab plus chemotherapy in resectable or borderline resectable non-small-cell lung cancer: the phase 2 MDT-BRIDGE trial
works.abstract: The phase 2 MDT-BRIDGE study is investigating perioperative durvalumab plus neoadjuvant chemotherapy (AEGEAN regimen) in resectable and borderline resectable non-small-cell lung cancer and chemoradiotherapy (CRT) followed by consolidation durvalumab (PACIFIC regimen) in patients who become unresectable after neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy guided by multidisciplinary team assessments during the neoadjuvant period. The primary endpoint was the overall resection rate (descriptive with no formal hypothesis testing). Secondary endpoints included event-free survival, progression-free survival, pathological complete response rate (resectable patients cohort), circulating tumor DNA clearance between baseline and presurgery/pre-CRT and safety. Overall, 142 patients received neoadjuvant treatment; 64.8% and 35.2% were deemed resectable and borderline resectable at baseline, respectively. The overall resection rate (95% confidence interval) was 74.6% (66.7‒81.6) in a population that included more than one-third of patients with borderline resectable disease. R0 resection rate was 96.2% (90.6‒99.0) in those who underwent surgery. Overall, 131 (92.3%) patients had surgery (n = 106) or CRT (n = 25) after neoadjuvant treatment, and 117 (82.4%) patients received adjuvant (n = 94) or consolidation (n = 23) durvalumab. During adjuvant or consolidation durvalumab, maximum grade 3/4 adverse events occurred in 7.4% of resected patients and 17.4% of CRT-treated patients, with 8.5% and 13.0% discontinuing treatment due to adverse events. This multidisciplinary team-guided approach was feasible and enabled delivery of curative-intent treatment (surgery or CRT), followed by durvalumab in most patients, and demonstrated encouraging preliminary efficacy with a manageable adjuvant or consolidation safety profile that was consistent with prior studies. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05925530 . As presented at the ESMO Congress 2026: In the global phase 2 MDT-BRIDGE trial, neoadjuvant durvalumab plus chemotherapy in patients with resectable and borderline resectable non-small-cell lung cancer, followed by multidisciplinary reassessment, enabled surgery in most patients, leading to encouraging pathological complete response rates, and no additional safety concerns were reported when patients with unresectable tumors continued with chemoradiotherapy and consolidative durvalumab.

Nanoparticles for cardiovascular diseases: identifying and overcoming barriers in translating preclinical success to clinical applications
works.abstract: Nanoparticles (NPs) have emerged as versatile platforms for drug delivery in cardiovascular diseases (CVDs), demonstrating robust efficacy in preclinical models by stabilizing atherosclerotic plaques, promoting safe and efficient thrombolysis, and mitigating ischemia-reperfusion injury. These advances highlight the maturation of cardiovascular nanomedicine; however, translation to clinical practice remains limited. This gap between laboratory success and clinical adoption reflects broader challenges in nanomedicine design, including suboptimal delivery to diseased tissues, limited efficacy of single therapeutic payload-based strategies in addressing the multifaceted inflammatory pathways driving CVDs, NPs' immunogenicity, and scale-up feasibility. Addressing these barriers is particularly critical in CVDs, where therapeutic success depends on precise engagement with multiple molecular and cellular drivers of disease. This review discusses the evolving landscape of cardiovascular nanomedicine, focusing on four aspects. First, we highlight advances in NPs bioengineering strategies, such as refined targeting moieties, optimized physicochemical properties, and responsiveness to endogenous and external stimuli that enhance organ- and cell-specific delivery in atherosclerosis, myocardial infarction, and stroke. Second, we discuss analytical innovations that improve characterization and control of NPs' biodistribution, enabling more rational targeting. Third, we evaluate therapeutic payloads, emphasizing how RNA-based and immunomodulatory agents represent a meaningful step toward clinical translation. Fourth, we outline approaches to addressing persistent challenges in safety and scalable manufacturing. Together, these developments establish a foundation for translating NP design principles into practical cardiovascular therapies. With continued progress in targeted delivery, clinical safety, and production scalability, cardiovascular nanomedicine is increasingly well-positioned to translate preclinical advances to transformative patient outcomes.

works.title: Emerging insights into amino acid metabolism in the heart: implications for cardiovascular diseases and therapeutic targeting
works.abstract: As a metabolically versatile organ, the heart is capable of generating energy from a wide range of substrates. Although fatty acid and glucose metabolism in the heart have been extensively studied, the contribution of amino acid metabolism to cardiac physiology and disease is gaining increasing attention. A range of amino acids, including branched-chain amino acids, glutamine and glutamate, asparagine, glycine, tryptophan and alanine, play integral roles in signalling pathways that orchestrate key adaptive and maladaptive changes in the myocardium, under both physiological and pathological stress. Dysregulation of these pathways is associated with cardiovascular disease such as heart failure, hypertension, myocardial infarction and atherosclerosis, via mechanisms involving impaired mitochondrial function, oxidative stress and inflammation. This review provides a comprehensive overview of amino acid metabolism in the heart, including sulphur amino acids, their role in relation to cardiovascular disease and emerging therapeutic strategies targeting amino acid metabolism in the heart. Finally, this review also discusses current and ongoing clinical trials targeting amino acid metabolism with the aim of finding potential therapeutic targets in cardiovascular disease.

works.title: The fight of innate immunity and abnormal cannabinoids against Candida infection
works.abstract: Candida species represent the most clinically significant fungal pathogens in humans, with invasive candidiasis carrying a mortality of 30%–40% in critically ill patients despite modern antifungal therapy. The innate immune system – through the coordinated and specific activities of neutrophils, macrophages, NK cells, mast cells and eosinophils – constitute the primary and most consequential biological defence against Candida invasion. Abnormal cannabinoids (Abn‐CBDs), a structurally distinctive class of synthetic lipid compounds with non‐psychoactive properties and regioisomeric configurations, critically distinct from classical cannabinoids in their independence from CB 1 and CB 2 receptor signalling, have emerged as a novel and pharmacologically compelling class of antifungal compounds. This review integrates the current understanding of innate immune cell antifungal mechanisms with the emerging pharmacology of abnormal cannabinoids, examines the direct antifungal and immunomodulatory properties of Abn‐CBDs, and critically addresses the tripartite contest between innate immunity, abnormal cannabinoids and Candida 's formidable evasion repertoire.

Neoadjuvant nivolumab with or without visugromab in muscle-invasive bladder cancer: the phase 2a GDFATHER-NEO trial
works.abstract: Growth differentiation factor-15 (GDF-15) is overexpressed in muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) and was recently identified as a potential therapeutic target to overcome resistance to programmed cell death protein 1/programmed death ligand 1 (PDL1) blockade. We investigated the safety and efficacy of GDF-15 blockade in an exploratory, stratified, placebo-controlled, single-blinded, nonrandomized phase 2a trial (GDFATHER-NEO). Thirty-one cisplatin-ineligible or cisplatin-refusing patients with newly diagnosed MIBC (clinical T2–T4aN0M0) were stratified by tumor stage and PDL1 combined positive score (CPS) and allocated sequentially to receive three cycles of neoadjuvant nivolumab (N, 480 mg 4-weekly) plus the GDF-15-neutralizing antibody visugromab (V, 20 mg kg−1 4-weekly; n = 16) or placebo (P, n = 15), followed by radical cystectomy or repeat transurethral resection of the bladder tumor. Locally assessed pathologic complete response (pCR, ypT0N0/x) and Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors v1.1-based radiographic response served as dual primary endpoints. pCR was 33% (5 of 15, 95% confidence interval (CI) 12–62%) in patients receiving N + V versus 8% (1 of 13, 95% CI 0–36%) for N + P; major pathologic response was 60% (95% CI 32–84%) versus 23% (95% CI 5–54%), and radiographic overall response rate was 60% (95% CI 32–84%) versus 15% (95% CI 2–45%), respectively. Responses to N + V were associated with higher baseline densities of total and proliferating (Ki-67+) CD8+ T cells, but independent of CPS and baseline GDF-15 levels in serum and tumor. There were no treatment-related discontinuations or treatment-related delays to surgery; grade 3–4 treatment-related adverse events occurred in two (13%) and three (20%) patients treated with N + V or N + P, respectively. These findings support further evaluation of visugromab in MIBC. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT06059547 . As presented at the ESMO Congress 2026: In this exploratory, nonrandomized phase 2a trial, treatment of patients with immune checkpoint inhibitor-naive muscle-invasive bladder cancer with the GDF-15-neutralizing antibody visugromab and nivolumab produced encouraging pathological complete response and radiographic response rates with no new safety signals, supporting further evaluation in larger randomized studies.

works.title: Relatlimab plus nivolumab versus nivolumab for advanced melanoma: 5-year survival and biomarker analyses of the phase 3 RELATIVITY-047 trial
works.abstract: Nivolumab plus relatlimab is approved for advanced melanoma based on the RELATIVITY-047 trial; however, long-term data are needed. Here, we report data from RELATIVITY-047 with the longest follow-up at present. In this phase 2–3, double-blind trial, patients with metastatic/unresectable melanoma were randomized 1:1 to nivolumab 480 mg plus relatlimab 160 mg (n = 355) or nivolumab 480 mg (n = 359) intravenously every 4 weeks. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS) by blinded independent central review. Secondary endpoints were overall survival (OS), response, and safety. Additional post-hoc analyses such as melanoma-specific survival (MSS), and exploratory biomarker analyses are also reported. This analysis shows clear separation in survival curves with the largest absolute differences to date in PFS, OS, and MSS. In this prespecified 5-year analysis, with a minimum follow-up of 57.3 months, nivolumab plus relatlimab demonstrated continued clinically significant benefit versus nivolumab for PFS (hazard ratio = 0.77; 95% confidence interval: 0.65–0.92), OS (hazard ratio = 0.78; 95% confidence interval: 0.64–0.95), and MSS (hazard ratio = 0.71; 95% confidence interval: 0.57–0.88). The safety profile remained consistent with prior reports. Among biomarker-evaluable patients in the programmed death ligand 1 ≥1% subgroup, analyses revealed an association between worse outcomes with nivolumab and high peripheral or tumor lymphocyte activation gene 3 (LAG-3)+ CD8 cell levels. The addition of relatlimab to nivolumab was associated with a lower prevalence of primary resistance than nivolumab alone. These data support the hypothesis that relatlimab can overcome LAG-3–mediated resistance to nivolumab and provides evidence for differential efficacy patterns observed across biomarker subgroups linked to primary versus acquired resistance states. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03470922. As presented at the ESMO Congress 2026: In a 5 year follow-up of survival and correlative data from the pivotal phase 3 RELATIVITY-047 trial comparing relatlimab plus nivolumab versus nivolumab alone in patients with metastatic or unresectable melanoma, statistically significant differences in progression-free survival, overall survival and melanoma-specific survival were seen with high baseline levels of LAG3 high CD8+ T cells associated with improved response in the combination arm.

Biodegradable radiopaque polymeric particles for computed tomography-guided intraperitoneal drug delivery
works.abstract: An iodinated hydrophobic oil containing the 2,3,5-triiodobenzoate moiety was encapsulated in biodegradable poly(lactic acid)-based polymer particles using a solvent emulsion-evaporation technique that provided control over particle size. The hydrophobic iodinated oil served a dual function as radiopaque contrast agent for particle quantification using dual-energy x-ray computed tomography (DECT) imaging and furthermore as solvent for the chemotherapeutic drug paclitaxel (PTX), establishing a novel theranostic system. Release kinetics of PTX was studied in fetal bovine serum over seven days demonstrating sustainable drug release over the entire period, with cumulative release mainly depending on particle diameter. Intraperitoneal administration of a therapeutic dosage of radiopaque spheres in mice provided sufficient iodine contrast to track biodistribution and clearance over 18 days. Importantly, imaging showed unexpected particle aggregation in vivo with about 50% clearance over 18 days, emphasizing the value of real-time distribution assessment as a complementary method to conventional ex vivo histology. A proof of concept of longitudinal dual imaging using single-photon emission CT (SPECT)/DECT was demonstrated in a mouse model of colorectal cancer with intraperitoneal metastases following a single intraperitoneal dose of PTX or PTX-loaded particles. Treatment response was monitored using SPECT, while particle distribution was tracked by DECT. This theranostic approach integrates controlled intraperitoneal drug delivery with non-invasive quantitative DECT-based imaging and may improve treatment precision and therapeutic outcomes.
