Dual-Targeting Liposomes Based on Ginsenoside Rg3 for Intercepting the Metastatic Cascade in Breast Cancer
works.abstract: Abstract Metastatic progression remains the primary cause of mortality in triple-negative breast cancer. However, unmodified cholesterol-based liposomes displayed inherent limitations, such as pharmacological inertness and sole reliance on passive targeting, that preclude the selective elimination of residual tumor lesions or circulating tumor cells after surgery, thereby failing to interrupt the multi-step metastatic cascade. Herein, we present a dual-targeting cRGD-Rg3@DOX liposomal designed to overcome these limitations for post-TNBC surgical therapy. This smart liposome was fabricated via a single-step microfluidic synthesis, wherein ginsenoside Rg3 strategically replaces cholesterol as both a structural stabilizer and a bioactive therapeutic targeting component. This novel design achieves dual active targeting via Rg3-mediated GLUT1 recognition and cRGD binding to ανβ3 integrin, resulting in superior cellular specificity and uptake. A fourfold increase in targeting efficiency to lung metastatic sites in vivo is critical for eradicating both postoperative residual tumor cells and circulating tumor cells. In a murine 4T1 metastasis model, the cRGD-Rg3@DOX liposome exerts a multi-stage intervention on the metastatic cascade, significantly inhibiting epithelial−mesenchymal transition and concurrently downregulating key prometastatic factors to eliminate postoperative residual lesions. This synergistic multi-targeted action suppresses the formation of pulmonary metastatic colonies, reduces colony numbers from 139 to 31, extends median survival time from 22 to 43 days, and markedly reduces doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity. This cRGD-Rg3@DOX liposome presents a robust, dual-targeted nanotherapeutic strategy that effectively suppresses lung metastases and mitigates pro-metastatic factors, offering a promising paradigm for intercepting metastatic progression in the preclinical TNBC mice model.

works.title: Development of a 18F-Radiolabeled CD38 Probe for Targeted PET Imaging of NSCLC Xenografts with Different EGFR-Mutant Status
works.abstract: Abstract Non-invasive identification of epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) mutation status remains a critical unmet clinical need for personalized therapy of non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Given that CD38 is markedly downregulated in EGFR-mutant NSCLC while remaining highly expressed in EGFR-wild-type tumors, CD38 can serve as a surrogate imaging biomarker for the indirect stratification of EGFR molecular phenotypes. Herein, we report the preclinical development and comprehensive characterization of 18F-NOTA-78c, a novel 18F-radiolabeled small-molecule PET imaging probe targeting CD38. 18F-NOTA-78c was synthesized under mild aqueous conditions with high radiochemical purity (>95%). The tracer exhibited favorable in vitro and in vivo stability, high hydrophilicity (logD7.4 = −1.76 ± 0.02), and specific CD38-mediated cellular binding, with the cold precursor showing an IC50 value of 38.27 nM. In vivo micro-PET/CT and biodistribution studies in NSCLC xenograft-bearing mice demonstrated higher tracer accumulation in EGFR wild-type A549 tumors (SUVmax = 1.28, T/M = 4.74), whereas low uptake was observed in EGFR-mutant HCC827 and H1975 tumors. Our findings validate the proof-of-concept application of CD38-targeted PET for indirect EGFR status differentiation in NSCLC.

works.title: Rational Design, Synthesis, and Evaluation of a Novel PET Tracer Targeting Programmed Death-Ligand 1: From Bench to Bedside
works.abstract: Abstract Programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) is a critical immune checkpoint and an important PET/CT imaging target. Current PD-L1-targeted PET/CT tracers have the disadvantage of suboptimal pharmacokinetics and low tumor-to-background contrast. Based on the PD-L1-binding peptide RK-10, we rationally introduced different hydrophilic linkers containing aspartic acid and polyethylene glycol to design a series of novel precursors. Among them, NOTA-AP-PDL1p was selected with the best predicted binding affinity. [68Ga]Ga-AP-PDL1p was subsequently developed. The binding affinity, in vitro and in vivo properties, micro-PET/CT imaging, and first-in-human PET/CT imaging of [68Ga]Ga-AP-PDL1p were conducted. [68Ga]Ga-AP-PDL1p exhibited high affinity to human PD-L1, good in vitro and in vivo characteristics, as well as favorable in vivo pharmacokinetics. Moreover, [68Ga]Ga-AP-PDL1p administration also upregulates the PD-L1 expression in tumor xenografts. Pilot clinical studies showed good in vivo distribution of [68Ga]Ga-AP-PDL1p, and the uptake of [68Ga]Ga-AP-PDL1p in tumor lesions correlates with its PD-L1 expression. These promising results highlight the potential of [68Ga]Ga-AP-PDL1p as a novel tracer for PET imaging of the PD-L1 expression.

works.title: Investigating the TASK1 potassium channel in equine atrial myocardium as a potential treatment target for atrial fibrillation
works.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common clinically relevant arrhythmia in horses, with limited pharmacological treatment options in both veterinary and human medicine. TASK1 potassium channels represent a promising atrial-selective antiarrhythmic target, but their relevance in horses has not been established. To characterize equine TASK1 (eqTASK1) channels regarding structural conservation, electrophysiological function, pharmacological sensitivity, cardiac expression pattern and in vivo electrophysiological effects of TASK1 inhibition. EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: Sixteen horses killed for non-cardiovascular reasons, of which 10 horses used for tissue harvesting and six horses for in vivo testing. Functional and pharmacological properties of eq TASK1 and human (hTASK1) channels were assessed in Xenopus laevis oocytes using two-electrode voltage clamp recordings. Cardiac expression of eqTASK1 was analysed by qRT-PCR and immunoblotting, while in vivo electrophysiological studies were performed in anaesthetized horses before and after intravenous ketodoxapram administration. KEY RESULTS: EqTASK1 and h TASK1 channels demonstrated high structural conservation, comparable potassium-selective background currents and preserved pharmacological sensitivity with species-dependent differences in potency. EqTASK1 expression was strongly enriched in atrial and nodal tissue, whereas ventricular expression was minimal. In vivo administration of ketodoxapram significantly prolonged atrial effective refractory periods from 275 ± 54 to 418 ± 94 ms without significant changes in heart rate or atrioventricular conduction parameters. CONCLUSION AND IMPLICATIONS: EqTASK1 channels are highly conserved with human orthologs and display pronounced atrial-predominant cardiac expression. In vivo TASK1 inhibition prolongs atrial refractoriness in horses, supporting TASK1 as a translational atrial-selective antiarrhythmic target in both human and veterinary medicine.

works.title: RTS,S-induced off-target antibody responses in malaria-naïve adults associated with protection against controlled human malaria infection
works.abstract: RTS,S, a WHO-recommended malaria vaccine, targets the circumsporozoite protein (CSP) on the Plasmodium falciparum sporozoite surface. Emerging data suggest off-target (non-CSP) antibody responses are associated with RTS,S-induced protection, but vaccine-derived responses are challenging to differentiate from boosting of naturally acquired immunity in endemic areas. We probed pre-challenge sera from RTS,S-vaccinated malaria-naïve adults who were either protected ( n = 18) or unprotected ( n = 17) against controlled human malaria infection on a custom peptide array with 1747 total variants from 130 non-CSP proteins from across the parasite lifecycle to assess off-target antibody responses with amino acid-level precision. Compared with the unprotected group, the protected group had increased IgG and/or IgA responses to 124 proteins (95%) studied. Using ssearch36, we found that 22 protein regions associated with protection had sequence similarities to CSP epitopes, including regions not found in RTS,S. The finding that off-target antibody responses are induced by RTS,S and are associated with protection in this and other studies suggests that they could be a marker of improved avidity, improved effector functions, or could be mediating improved protection by binding CSP or other proteins. Differentially reactive epitopes without linear sequence homology with CSP could represent conformational epitopes. Further study of these off-target antibody responses could help identify improved strategies for next-generation malaria vaccines.

works.title: Lymph node-targeted, mKRAS-specific amphiphile vaccine in pancreatic cancer: the randomized phase 2 AMPLIFY-7P trial
works.abstract: Camupepimut (ELI-002 7P) drives mutated KRAS (mKRAS)-specific T cell responses that correlated with disease-free survival (DFS) and overall survival (OS) in patients with mKRAS pancreatic adenocarcinoma (PDAC) in the phase 1 AMPLIFY-201 trial. In the phase 2 AMPLIFY-7P trial, patients with stage I-III KRAS-mutated PDAC without recurrence within 6 months of standard therapy were randomized 2:1 to camupepimut (n = 96) or standard-of-care/observation (n = 48). Stratification balanced nodal status. The primary DFS endpoint was not met (median 23.8 versus 21.2 months; HR 0.85, P = 0.5329). However, prespecified and exploratory analyses were informative. A numerical DFS advantage at 6 months of 14.0% (75.7% versus 61.7%; HR 0.55, P = 0.0557) corresponded to camupepimut dosing. Post hoc multivariate Cox regression analysis of DFS indicated an improved outcome for camupepimut (adjusted HR 0.47, P = 0.0086), a worse outcome for stage III disease (adjusted HR 2.29, P = 0.0127), an elevated baseline CA19-9 (adjusted HR 3.16, P < 0.0001) and baseline circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) positivity (adjusted HR 5.99, P < 0.0001). Prespecified subgroup analyses addressing prognostic and predictive factors suggested DFS benefit for camupepimut (ctDNA negative: HR 0.51, P = 0.0280; no prior radiation: HR 0.59, P = 0.0221). Exploratory analysis demonstrated that ex vivo mKRAS-specific T cell responses were robust (98.9%, 89/90) and associated with antigen spreading (86.7%, 13/15). In camupepimut-treated patients, mKRAS-specific T cell response >9.17-fold over baseline (82.2%, 74/90) correlated with improved DFS (HR 0.22, P < 0.0001), with the median DFS not reached versus 6.08 months for above and below 9.17-fold, respectively. Camupepimut safety was similar to observation, with grade ≥3 adverse events in 10.4% (10/96) versus 14.6% (7/48), and few serious AEs (6.3%, 6/96 versus 8.3%, 4/48; reflecting progression/surgical complication). These efficacy and immunogenicity signals will inform a refined strategy for a confirmatory phase 3 trial. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05726864 .

Determinants of response to CAR T cell therapy in a multicenter, multi-trial cohort analysis of patients with lymphoma
works.abstract: Abstract In patients with non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL) treated with chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy, factors associated with efficacy overlap with prognostic biomarkers. Currently, there is no consensus on optimal product characteristics. We analyzed the phenotypic attributes of the anti-CD19 CAR T therapy axicabtagene ciloleucel (axi-cel) from 580 patients with NHL across multiple clinical trials with long-term follow-up (median, 41.9 months). A high proportion of naive-like (CCR7 + CD45RA + ) T cells was the most significant feature associated with prolonged progression-free survival (PFS; hazard ratio = 0.46, 95% confidence interval: 0.31−0.68, P = 9.8 × 10 −5 , high versus low naive-like T cell groups) without impacting safety. The relationship between naive-like T cells and efficacy was independent of tumor microenvironment characteristics (assessed in 112 patients). In multivariate models, the naive-like phenotype outperformed clinicopathologic features such as inflammatory markers and tumor burden, remaining significant after adjusting for product expansion. An inverse correlation was observed between prior lines of therapy and the proportion of naive-like T cells in both product and matched apheresis samples, suggesting a benefit of earlier intervention. The key findings were validated in an independent cohort of 203 patients treated with axi-cel-based therapy or brexucabtagene autoleucel. Mass cytometry by time-of-flight analysis of products from a subgroup of 116 patients confirmed an association between a CD8 naive-like T cell phenotype lacking expression of exhaustion markers, such as TIGIT, LAG-3 and PD-1, and PFS. The evidence generated by this study has the potential to advance the development of more effective cellular therapies.

works.title: Peroxidase-mimicking Nanozymes for Redox Monitoring and Regulation in Cancer Theranostics
works.abstract: Cancer progression is closely associated with dysregulated redox homeostasis, including altered hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂) metabolism and adaptive antioxidant responses within the tumour microenvironment (TME). These biochemical changes provide opportunities for redox-responsive cancer diagnosis and therapeutic intervention. Peroxidase-mimicking nanozymes have emerged as engineered catalytic materials capable of exploiting H₂O₂-dependent reactions for signal amplification and modulation of oxidative stress. This review critically examines their catalytic mechanisms, structural determinants, and applications in cancer theranostics, with particular emphasis on the relationship between interfacial redox chemistry and biological function. Unlike natural peroxidases with structurally defined catalytic sites, many nanozymes mediate peroxide-dependent reactions through surface-associated redox centres involving electron transfer and reactive intermediate formation. Their tunable composition, morphology, and surface chemistry offer opportunities to tailor catalytic performance for diagnostic and therapeutic applications. By exploiting tumour-associated H₂O₂ availability and local acidity, appropriately designed nanozyme systems may facilitate preferential catalytic activation and amplified diagnostic signals. Therapeutically, peroxidase-like activity can promote oxidative damage in cancer cells, while multifunctional nanozyme platforms may incorporate complementary mechanisms to modulate hypoxia, antioxidant defences, and tumour-associated immune responses. However, catalytic performance and tumour selectivity are strongly influenced by biological matrix effects, tumour heterogeneity, catalyst stability, and potential contributions from dissolved metal species. Distinguishing sustained heterogeneous catalysis from consumptive redox reactions, together with establishing in vivo efficacy, safety, and reproducibility, remains essential for clinical translation. Future developments should therefore prioritise mechanistically validated nanozyme platforms that integrate reliable redox monitoring with controllable therapeutic activity, supporting the development of more effective cancer theranostic strategies.

works.title: Biophysics of Monoclonal Antibody Solutions And Scattering Methods as Probes: A Review
works.abstract: Abstract Monoclonal antibody solutions represent a unique class of protein solutions whose microscopic structure and dynamics govern key pharmaceutical properties, including viscosity, stability, self-association, and aggregation. These phenomena become crucial in highly concentrated formulations required for subcutaneous administration, where anisotropic molecular shape, conformational flexibility, and highly specific protein−protein interactions give rise to complex collective behavior that cannot be fully understood from macroscopic measurements alone. Many aspects of mAb solution behavior can be interpreted within the broader framework of colloid physics. This theoretical tool is useful to predict the diffusion of proteins in a crowded environment. However, the molecular architecture of antibodies challenges classical descriptions of crowded protein solutions. Experimental methods capable of probing molecular dynamics over multiple time and length scales are therefore essential for establishing quantitative relationships between intermolecular interactions and formulation properties. Among these, scattering techniques provide label-free access to both structural and dynamical correlations in solution. Recent advances in neutron and X-ray scattering, complemented by light scattering, molecular simulations, and theoretical modeling, have considerably expanded our understanding of antibody diffusion, transient clustering, reversible self-association, and the microscopic origins of high solution viscosity. This review places recent advances in the biophysics of monoclonal antibody solutions within the broader context of protein and colloidal systems, with particular emphasis on scattering methodsand especially neutron spectroscopyas probes of molecular dynamics. By combining concepts from colloid physics with modern scattering approaches, we discuss how microscopic structural and dynamical information can be linked to the macroscopic behavior of antibody formulations, providing a physical framework for the rational design, optimization and development of next-generation biopharmaceuticals.

Plasma EC 90 multiples are drug, target site and species specific—A physiologically based pharmacokinetic modelling example of nirmatrelvir central nervous system distribution
works.abstract: Abstract Background and Purpose Achieving minimum unbound drug concentration in plasma above in vitro EC 90 is a common antiviral pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) target. However, it often overlooks restricted distribution into target sites like the central nervous system (CNS), where a trough concentration above 1 × EC 90 is needed. Currently, the required EC 90 multiplier ( n ) is defined empirically without mechanistic evidence. This study utilizes physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) modelling of nirmatrelvir in rats to bridge the gap between plasma and target‐site exposure, providing a mechanistic basis for the minimal EC 90 multiplier in antiviral dose selection. Experimental Approach A nirmatrelvir population PK (popPK) model developed from rat plasma data was integrated into the LeiCNS PBPK platform. Evaluated against rat cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) concentration, the PBPK model was used to simulate drug distribution across various CNS compartments, to assess the plasma‐to‐periphery relationship of antivirals with varying blood–brain barrier (BBB) permeability. Key Results The simulation results highlight how both unbound fraction in plasma ( f u ) and unbound tissue‐to‐plasma partition coefficient ( K p,uu ) are the primary determinants of the minimal EC 90 multiplier. We demonstrated that aiming to reach plasma C min above an arbitrary multiple of the EC 90 without accounting for drug and species‐dependent parameters, and related body distribution, can lead to insufficient drug exposure at peripheral target sites. Conclusion and Implications Target‐site concentration, rather than total plasma concentration, is the mechanistically correct effect site for linking to in vitro EC 90 . By incorporating both f u and K p,uu , a more mechanistically informed EC 90 multiplier can be predicted a priori.

works.title: SARS-CoV-2 breakthrough infections imprint signatures of enhanced immunity against COVID-19
works.abstract: SARS-CoV-2-specific immunity has been shaped in recent years by a combination of natural infection, complicated by ongoing viral evolution, and vaccination. However, it has remained unclear to what extent combined antigen challenge, which elicits so-called hybrid immunity, impacts clinical outcomes and subsequent protection against COVID-19. In this study, we evaluated spike-specific humoral and cellular immune responses elicited by hybrid antigen exposure versus vaccination alone, considering the order of challenge and disease severity after infection with SARS-CoV-2. Hybrid antigen exposure was characterized by enhanced humoral and cellular immune responses compared with vaccination alone. CD8 + T cell responses were also more cross-reactive and displayed skewed epitope targeting hierarchies in the context of hybrid immunity. These features were maintained in older adults, who typically exhibit age-related deficits in de novo immunity, especially after breakthrough infections (BTIs). BTIs were further associated with more coordinated adaptive immune responses compared with those elicited by vaccination after infection with SARS-CoV-2. We also found that humoral immune responses, specifically IgG antibody titers targeting the spike protein receptor-binding domain, were better maintained after mRNA vaccination and that cellular immune responses were better maintained after vectored vaccination in the wake of BTIs. Moreover, vaccination was associated with mild disease after subsequent infection, especially among individuals who had received a booster dose. These results suggest that vaccine-induced memory responses, which generally wane over time, can be reactivated and reshaped by BTIs, amplifying features associated with enhanced immunity against SARS-CoV-2.

works.title: Linear cap-independent mRNA vaccines as an emerging vaccine platform
works.abstract: Linear cap-independent mRNA (LciRNA) is an emerging vaccine platform enabling cap-independent translation while retaining a linear RNA architecture. This review summarizes LciRNA design principles, including IRES-mediated initiation, stability engineering, and immune regulation, and compares LciRNA with major mRNA vaccine platforms. We discuss current preclinical progress, particularly in cancer vaccines, and analyze challenges in potency, manufacturability, application scope, and clinical translation.

A Pan-KRAS-Targeted PET Probe for Noninvasive Quantitative Imaging of KRAS Expression
works.abstract: Abstract Kirsten rat sarcoma viral oncogene homolog (KRAS) mutations are key drivers of the initiation and progression of multiple solid tumors. Precise assessment of KRAS mutation status and expression levels is critical for molecular subtyping and targeted therapeutic decision-making. However, pan-KRAS molecular imaging probes capable of noninvasively identifying multiple clinically relevant KRAS mutant subtypes while quantitatively assessing KRAS expressions remain unavailable. In this study, we developed a pan-KRAS-targeted positron emission tomography (PET) probe, [68Ga]Ga-DOTA-pKRASi, based on the pan-KRAS small-molecule inhibitor BI-2493. [68Ga]Ga-DOTA-pKRASi was efficiently prepared with a radiochemical purity exceeding 99%. In vitro cellular uptake studies and micro-PET/CT imaging in tumor-bearing mice demonstrated that the probe specifically targeted multiple clinically relevant KRAS mutant subtypes, including KRAS-G12C, KRAS-G12D, and KRAS-G12V. Compared with the corresponding xenograft models harboring endogenous KRAS mutations, the KRAS-overexpressing models consistently exhibited higher tracer uptake, with the highest tumor uptake observed in the BxPC-3KRAS−G12V model (4.65 ± 0.22 % ID/mL). Competitive blocking reduced tumor uptake by 61.11−68.82%, confirming the excellent in vivo targeting specificity of this probe. Furthermore, the tracer uptake was significantly positively correlated with the mutated KRAS protein content determined by immunohistochemistry in tumor tissues, demonstrating its potential for the quantitative assessment of KRAS expression. Overall, these findings provide a proof-of-concept for pan-KRAS-targeted PET molecular imaging. This imaging strategy enables the noninvasive visualization of multiple clinically relevant KRAS mutant subtypes while allowing quantitative assessment of KRAS expression. This work lays the experimental foundation for the development of companion diagnostics for pan-KRAS-targeted therapies.

Checkpoint kinase 1 (Chk1) inhibition promotes motor function recovery through suppressing pyroptosis signalling and attenuating microglial polarization shift to M1 phenotype in spinal cord injury mice
works.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Microglial polarization shifts that induce inflammatory responses play a role in the occurrence and progression of spinal cord injury (SCI). We reported that checkpoint kinase 1 (Chk1) was involved in regulating SCI-induced motor dysfunction. We aim now to determine whether the microglial polarization shift is involved in the action of Chk1 on SCI-induced motor dysfunction. EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: The pathological SCI in vivo model was induced in mice through spinal cord contusion injury, while the in vitro model was established by exposing cultured murine BV2 cells to lipopolysaccharide (LPS). To analyse the expression levels of associated genes and proteins, we utilized quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction, western blotting and immunofluorescence staining. We employed the cell counting kit-8, EdU assay and comet assay to evaluate microglia proliferation and DNA damage. KEY RESULTS: Chk1 down-regulation reversed the shift in microglial polarization and pyroptosis induced by SCI in vivo, improving motor dysfunction. Up-regulation of Chk1 worsened the microglial polarization shift and pyroptosis, causing deterioration in motor function following SCI. In vitro, both γ-H2AX and Chk1 activation increased in BV2 cells in a dose- and time-dependent manner in response to LPS. The selective Chk1 inhibitor SCH900776 or the DNA damage repair agonist AV-153 showed that LPS-induced microglial polarization shifted from M2 to M1 and this shift was linked to the suppression of pyroptosis signalling. CONCLUSIONS AND IMPLICATIONS: Our results demonstrate that the Chk1-regulated shift in microglial polarization through pyroptosis signalling may be a promising drug target for future therapies for SCI-induced motor dysfunction.

works.title: Coordinated serum interferon gamma and IL-15 responses to PfRAS vaccination are associated with protection from malaria
works.abstract: Abstract Immunization with radiation-attenuated sporozoites (PfRAS) is highly protective against Plasmodium falciparum malaria, but our understanding of protective correlates is incomplete. The IMRAS study used a PfRAS dose aimed at 50% efficacy to enable discovery of protective correlates. We performed serum proteomics, assaying 2925 serum proteins at five IMRAS study timepoints for 6 protected and 5 non-protected donors, to identify secreted proteins that correlate with immunization and/or protection. We next integrated this serum proteomics dataset with whole blood transcriptomic responses and proportions of circulating immune cells to identify involved signaling pathways and cell subsets. We identified 21 vaccine-induced proteins, including IFNG and IL15. IFNG-stimulated PBMCs from protected IMRAS participants showed increased CXCL9 and CXCL10 responses vs. non-protected participants. IFNG levels in protected individuals correlated with IL15, as well as interferon response gene expression levels in whole blood, and circulating activated CD14+ monocytes. Altogether, this analysis showed that PfRAS can prevent blood-stage malaria infection via coordinated IFNG and IL15 production, activation of CD14+ monocytes, and subsequent production of CXCL9, CXCL10, and CXCL11.

Deep dynamical models of single-cell multiomic velocities predict loss-of-function and rescue perturbations in B cells
works.abstract: Abstract Here we present DynaVelo, a generative neural ordinary differential equation model that learns the joint dynamics of gene expression and transcription factor (TF) motif activity from single-cell multiome data. DynaVelo learns a functional form of the vector field, such that the model can be perturbed in silico and not only used to draw trajectories. We show that DynaVelo recovers the bifurcating in vivo dynamics of wild-type murine germinal center (GC) B cells and reveals how these dynamics change under heterozygous loss of epigenetic regulators Arid1a and Ctcf . In silico perturbation yields dynamic and cell-state-specific gene regulatory networks (GRNs) that recover known TF-to-gene edges in the wild-type GC GRN and predicts those that are disrupted in mutants. Perturbing Arid1aHet GCs in silico identified Ctcf , Stat3 and Bcl6 as rescue targets for Arid1a loss. In vivo experiments in double-heterozygous mice confirmed rescue of the Arid1aHet dark-zone phenotype in all three cases, and multiome profiling of Arid1aHet ; CtcfHet GCs validated the predicted shift toward wild-type dynamics.

works.title: Recordanelles for transcriptome-wide single-cell RNA recording in human cells
works.abstract: Transcriptomic measurement technologies provide powerful approaches to understand biology but are limited to providing either a high-resolution snapshot at a moment in time or a low-resolution history of transcription constrained to a few genes over a narrow time range. Here, we introduce the 'recordanelle', a single-component synthetic organelle capable of recording the transcriptome in human cells. Recordanelles are composed of a mitochondrial membrane anchor, a condensate assembler and a poly(A)-binding protein. We demonstrate that the recordanelle can be engineered to recruit engineered RNAs or a sampling of up to 90% of all endogenous mRNAs and protect them over several days. We further show that transient and dynamic transcriptional responses resulting from inducible promoters or interferon signaling are preserved throughout time within the recordanelle at the single-cell level. This work provides a nondisruptive and unbiased transcriptome-wide single-cell RNA recording technology to enable a deeper understanding of biology.

works.title: The kinase inhibitor dabrafenib halts progression of cerebral cavernous malformations in a BRAF-independent manner
works.abstract: genes, forming fragile mulberry-like malformed blood vessel structures that are prone to leak and break. Treatment is limited to surgical removal of solitary cavernomas, and because patients often present with multiple lesions, pharmacological alternatives to surgery are needed. We performed a high-throughput screen of 5200 bioactive molecules in programmed cell death 10 (PDCD10 or CCM3)-deficient mouse endothelial cells, coupled to automated image analysis. This screen identified dabrafenib, a clinically approved BRAF inhibitor, as a compound that restored cell-cell junctions and vascular barrier properties of CCM3-deficient endothelial cells. The potential translatability of dabrafenib was tested in acute and chronic CCM mouse models, where it reduced cerebral lesion burden and suppressed lesion permeability. Dabrafenib also rescued abnormal structural defects present in the developing retina vasculature in an acute CCM mouse model. Mechanistically, dabrafenib targeted extracellular regulated kinase (ERK)5-Krüppel-like factor (KLF)2/4 signaling and suppressed F-actin stress fiber formation in human brain endothelial cells, two potentially independent and central molecular processes involved in CCM pathology. Silencing BRAF did not prevent dabrafenib-induced KLF2/4 inhibition or restoration of cell-cell junctions, suggesting that its dual therapeutic outcome is independent of BRAF pathway inhibition. In conclusion, dabrafenib is a low-molecular weight compound that inhibits cavernoma pathogenesis, suggesting that CCMs could be treated with dabrafenib to block cavernoma growth and vascular leakage.

works.title: Targeting ZIP12-mediated Zn 2+ signaling as a treatment for pulmonary hypertension
works.abstract: ZIP12, a membrane-bound zinc importer, is up-regulated in the remodeled pulmonary arterioles of patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). Genetic deletion of its encoding gene, Slc39a12 , ameliorates the disease in rodent models. Here, we show that ZIP12 overexpression in human pulmonary artery smooth muscle cells (PASMCs) increased intracellular labile Zn 2+ and promoted proliferation. ZIP12 siRNA knockdown attenuated pulmonary hypertension in rodent models. We developed a humanized anti-ZIP12 monoclonal antibody, APL-9796, that normalized intracellular Zn 2+ concentration, suppressed proliferation in fibroblasts derived from patients with PAH and PDGF-stimulated PASMCs, and reduced PDGF-induced cytoskeletal remodeling in PASMCs and contractility in PASMCs and engineered pulmonary artery tissues. APL-9796 showed dose-dependent efficacy in humanized Slc39a12 rats, improving cardiopulmonary parameters after induction of pulmonary hypertension and was well tolerated in phase 1 clinical studies. Transcriptomic profiling revealed modulation of several molecular pathways, including those involving AMPK, PPAR, and PI3K-Akt. ZIP12-driven labile Zn 2+ signaling underpins the pathogenesis of PAH. Targeting ZIP12 with APL-9796 offers a promising therapeutic strategy.

works.title: A 5 + 1 polyene scaffold that selectively recognizes ergosterol’s conjugated diene uncouples antifungal potency from host toxicity
works.abstract: Amphotericin B remains the gold-standard therapy for invasive fungal infections, but its clinical utility is limited by toxicity arising from poor selectivity for fungal ergosterol over mammalian cholesterol, a challenge that decades of medicinal chemistry have failed to fully overcome. Here, we report mandimycin M16, a polyene macrolide engineered from a unique 5 + 1 polyene scaffold that uncouples antifungal potency from host toxicity. Mandimycin M16 exhibited potent, broad-spectrum activity against 11 tested World Health Organization (WHO) priority fungal pathogens. Unlike amphotericin B, which binds cholesterol, M16 exhibited no detectable cholesterol binding and showed no detectable hemolysis, cytotoxicity, or nephrotoxicity at concentrations up to 128 micrograms per milliliter in vitro and after up to seven daily intravenous doses in mice. Mechanistic studies revealed that mandimycin M16 exerted rapid fungicidal activity through selective recognition of the conjugated C5-C8 diene system present in ergosterol but absent in cholesterol, a mode of sterol discrimination fundamentally different from classical polyenes. In multiple disseminated murine infection models, M16 outperformed liposomal amphotericin B at equivalent doses, achieving up to 3.4 log reduction in fungal burden and 100% survival without detectable renal injury by biomarkers or histopathology. These findings establish that the 5 + 1 polyene architecture enables complete sterol selectivity and molecularly uncouples antifungal potency from host toxicity, providing a next-generation antifungal candidate for the treatment of invasive fungal infections.

works.title: Single-nucleotide polymorphism–directed design of allele-specific antisense oligonucleotides for spinocerebellar ataxia type 3
works.abstract: Spinocerebellar ataxia type 3 (SCA3), also called Machado-Joseph disease, the most common form of autosomal dominant cerebellar ataxia, is caused by a CAG repeat expansion in ATXN3 . The mutant protein is prone to aggregation and exerts toxic gain-of-function effects, whereas the wild-type protein has important neuroprotective roles as a deubiquitinase. Current treatment strategies for SCA3 lack specificity for the mutant allele. Identifying genetic variants such as single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in linkage with the pathogenic CAG expansion offers a promising avenue to develop allele-specific therapeutic interventions, like antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs). To address this, we conducted allele-specific, targeted, multiplexed nanopore sequencing on 79 patients with SCA3 from Germany, UK, and Portugal. We identified almost 200 polymorphisms and grouped them into three haplotype blocks on the basis of linkage disequilibrium. These SNPs were strongly associated with the CAG expansion. Genotypic modeling of our subcohorts indicated that targeting only two SNPs from different blocks could enable allele-specific treatment of the majority of European patients with SCA3. We evaluated 17 candidate ASOs targeting SNPs from different haplotype blocks. Seven of these ASOs caused allele-preferential reduction of more than 65%. A single ASO application in two SCA3 iPSC-derived cortical neurons (AX1, AX2) achieved up to 90% reduction of mutant ATXN3. Toxicity assessments together with RNA sequencing analyses in AX1 did not indicate evidence of toxicity or widespread transcriptional perturbations. These findings highlight that characterizing heterozygosity rates offers valuable opportunities for selective ASO therapies. Our proof-of-principle targeting with ASOs demonstrates the feasibility of haplotype-informed allele-specific silencing in ATXN3 .

works.title: Cas9 nickase–mediated contraction of CAG/CTG repeats is associated with phenotypic improvements in a Huntington’s disease mouse model
works.abstract: Expanded CAG/CTG repeats cause more than 15 different diseases that all remain without a disease-modifying treatment. Because repeat length accounts for most of the variation in disease severity, contracting CAG/CTG repeats presents an attractive therapeutic avenue. Here, we show that the CRISPR-Cas9 nickase targeted to CAG/CTG repeats leads to efficient repeat contractions in Huntington's disease (HD) patient-derived neurons and astrocytes and in myotonic dystrophy type 1 patient-derived neurons. The approach was allele selective and free of detectable off-target mutations. Injection of the Cas9 nickase into the striatum of the R6/1 mouse model of HD using adeno-associated viral vectors led to repeat contractions in more than half of striatal neurons. Upon injection, we observed a reduction in the number of inclusion bodies, an improved gene expression profile, and amelioration of locomotion deficits in the open field test. The effects were greater than expected from the contractions induced, suggesting that non-cell autonomous mechanisms may be involved. Our results provide the proof of concept that correction of CAG/CTG repeats can improve HD phenotypes in a mouse disease model.

works.title: Graft-versus-host disease prophylaxis shapes T cell biology and immune reconstitution after hematopoietic cell transplant
works.abstract: Successful hematopoietic cell transplant requires immunosuppression to prevent graft-versus-host disease (GVHD), a lethal, T cell-mediated complication. The phase 3 BMT CTN 1703 trial demonstrated superior GVHD-free/relapse-free survival for posttransplant cyclophosphamide (PT-Cy)-based GVHD prophylaxis versus tacrolimus/methotrexate (Tac/MTX), but the T cell biology underpinning these outcomes remains unknown. To determine this, 324 patients were coenrolled onto BMT CTN 1801 to investigate the distinct T cell immune reconstitution pathways of these regimens, including extensive evaluation of T cell receptor (TCR) repertoire, via sequencing of 2359 longitudinal samples and 180,432,350 T cells. Multimodal T cell analysis revealed that PT-Cy was associated with pan-T cell deletion followed by delayed T cell expansion from a smaller founder population compared with Tac/MTX. This created a T cell diversity bottleneck, leading to reduced TCR repertoire diversity for 2 years posttransplant. Reduced TCR diversity, more common in patients receiving PT-Cy, was linked to protection against chronic GVHD when patients were analyzed without regard to study arm. Leveraging donor- and host-specific TCR clonal analysis, we determined that PT-Cy-mediated T cell depletion also depleted pathogen-specific TCRs, rendering PT-Cy patients more likely to lack detectable graft-derived pathogen-specific TCRs early after transplant, which was associated with an increased risk of severe infection. This study reveals how distinct immunosuppression strategies uniquely remodel T cell immunity and shape divergent transplant outcomes.

works.title: A fluorescent choline kinase alpha inhibitor for intraoperative molecular imaging during resection of canine NSCLC tumors
works.abstract: Choline kinase α (ChoKα) is a biomarker of lung cancer, is overexpressed in 60% of human pulmonary malignancies, and is associated with an aggressive phenotype and poor clinical outcome. Patients with lung cancer who undergo surgery have a recurrence rate of 30 to 50%, indicating a potential need for better tumor detection modalities. A near-infrared fluorescent ChoKα-targeting imaging agent, JAS239 (λ ex , λ em : 745, 775 nanometers), was developed for intraoperative identification of tumors, their margins, and local metastases. In lung cancer cells, JAS239 inhibited phosphocholine production, reduced viability in a dose-dependent manner, and accumulated in the cytoplasm where ChoKα is active. JAS239 had favorable pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics for imaging metastatic lung lesions in mice. In situ and ex vivo fluorescence imaging of primary lung tumors in a canine clinical trial showed distinct tumor identification and margin delineation with a tumor-to-background ratio of 5.0 ± 0.6 and a contrast-to-variance ratio of 2.0 ± 0.2 at 0.5 milligram/kilogram. Fluorescence imaging identified a clinically significant event where an occult lesion was found after primary tumor resection. Fluorescence imaging also identified a close surgical margin, which prompted further investigation. Immunohistochemistry for ChoKα showed overexpression in canine lung tumors proportional to tumor fluorescence. Ex vivo human tumor painting demonstrated preferential JAS239 localization with a tumor-to-background ratio of 1.5 ± 0.1 and a contrast-to-variance ratio of 0.9 ± 0.1. These studies establish JAS239 as a safe and effective imaging agent for intraoperative lung tumor detection, warranting further evaluation for human patients with lung cancer.

Beyond the Ice Interface: Assessment of Sugar-Modulated Intermolecular Correlations in Ice-Free Freeze-Concentrated Matrix Analogues of Monoclonal Antibodies Using SAXS
works.abstract: Abstract This study investigates sugar-mediated modulation of intermolecular positional correlations in monoclonal antibody (mAb) formulations upon freeze-concentration using small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS). While previous studies have focused on solutions or dried states, experimental data on freeze-concentrated matrices (FCMs) for mAbs are still scarce, representing a key knowledge gap. Understanding the mAb FCM is key for the formulation of frozen drug substance, frozen drug product, and lyophilizates. To address this gap, we combined complementary systems: a solution concentration series of constant composition but varying total solid content, ice-free reconstituted FCM analogues, and genuine in situ frozen FCMs with varying sucrose/mAb ratios, measured within the ice-containing, non-equilibrium state. The concentration series reproduces the compositional upconcentration of all solutes that occurs upon freezing and enables tracking how protein−protein correlation features evolve with increasing crowding. A controlled cooling ramp from 20 to −40 °C probed the effect of temperature on intermolecular organization in FCM analogues and their response to cooling across Tg′. Structure factor features indicated a progressive transition from whole-molecule spacing to shorter-range, domain-level correlations with increasing concentration, converging on the distances observed in the FCM analogues and, as confirmed by cross-comparison, in the genuine in situ frozen FCM. A complementary, geometry-based coarse-grained 12-bead modelserving as an interpretive geometric frameworkreproduced the experimental correlation lengths, supporting their interpretation as sub-molecular proximity between neighboring subunits or domains. In the FCM analogues and in situ frozen FCMs, the sucrose-to-mAb ratio was a primary factor modulating intermolecular spacing, while buffer conditions had no measurable impact. Together, the FCM analogues and in situ frozen measurements provide mechanistic insight into protein packing in freeze-concentrated environments relevant for formulation stability.

works.title: Engineered human Argonaute 2 for targeted C-to-U RNA base editing
works.abstract: Tools for manipulating RNA that rely on nonhuman proteins, such as ISC-based and Cas-based scaffolds, can lead to unintended and little-understood effects on human cells and present challenges in therapeutic translation. Replacing them with human proteins engineered for expanded, programmable functions could bypass the limitations of these foreign proteins. Here we demonstrate that human Argonaute 2 (AGO2) can be repurposed as a modular RNA targeting domain. AGO2 fused to a C-to-U deaminase enables AGO-led targeted editing of RNA (ALTER). Using guide RNAs that remodel target RNA structure for selective editing and reduced nuclease activity, we show that ALTER achieves, on average, 1.9-fold higher C-to-U editing on mRNA targets in HEK293T cells compared with Cas13 editors CURE and RESCUE. Transcriptome-wide RNA-seq revealed similar or lower levels of off-target editing compared to the same Cas13-based editors. Machine learning models predict that far fewer immunogenic peptides will result from ALTER and we show that ALTER is amenable to a validated workflow for artificial intelligence-directed deimmunization. Human Argonaute is repurposed for RNA editing.

works.title: Genetic code expansion enables plant-directed control of bacterial activity
works.abstract: Microorganisms have the potential to deliver growth-promoting benefits to plants and crops; however, to be useful in a field setting, their gene expression should be programmable and restricted to specific plant hosts and conditions. Here, using O-methyl-L-tyrosine (OMY) as a model compound, we establish noncanonical amino acids (ncAAs) as a tool for plant-based control of associated microbial activity. We use genetic code expansion to engineer OMY-dependent control of protein synthesis in the soil bacterium Bacillus subtilis. Engineered B. subtilis strains express an orthogonal aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase and tRNA pair that, upon provision of OMY, results in suppression of in-frame amber stop codons in target transcripts. We engineer Arabidopsis, tomato and poplar to biosynthesize OMY, showing that plant-derived OMY can stimulate gene expression in both model and wild soil bacteria. This demonstrates that inducible and tissue-specific expression of a single biosynthetic enzyme by the plant enables on-demand control over microbial activity, establishing ncAAs as a tool for programming plant-microorganism partnerships.

works.title: Poloxamer 188 Promotes Severe Aggregation of Insulin under Shaking Conditions
works.abstract: Insulin is an indispensable cornerstone in the management of diabetes mellitus, yet its extreme susceptibility to aggregation under mechanical stress remains a formidable challenge for long-term formulation stability. This study investigates the potential of Poloxamer 188 (P188) as a chemically stable alternative to the industry-standard Polysorbate 20 (PS20) for stabilizing insulin. Formulations containing graded concentrations of P188 (0.005%-0.15%, w/v), 0.05% (w/v) PS20, or no surfactant were subjected to 24 h shaking stress at 300 rpm. Our results reveal a striking concentration-dependent profile for P188, where 0.05% PS20 consistently maintains robust protection, whereas low-to-moderate concentrations of P188 (0.005%-0.05%) fail to stabilize insulin and instead exert a pronounced "pro-aggregatory" effect. At 0.05% P188, this pro-aggregatory behavior leads to severe macroscopic turbidity, a massive surge in particle concentration (≥2 μm), and the near-total disappearance of detectable insulin monomers in the supernatant. Crucially, elevating the P188 concentration to 0.15% effectively prevents macroscopic turbidity and preserves high soluble protein recovery. Mechanistically, the instability observed at low-to-moderate P188 concentrations stems from its sluggish interfacial adsorption kinetics compared to PS20, leaving nascent air-liquid interfaces temporarily unprotected. Under such conditions, P188 functions as a macromolecular scaffold and nucleation core, cross-linking interface-denatured proteins with native molecules to drive rapid co-assembly. These findings serve as a critical warning for the biopharmaceutical industry that the use of P188 in insulin-based products must be approached with extreme caution to avoid inadvertent protein aggregation.

works.title: Saponin extract from Astragalus membranaceus (Fisch.) Bunge regulates gut–brain axis through intestinal Escherichia coli to reduce cerebral oxidative stress to treat vascular dementia in rodents
works.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Vascular dementia (VD) is a cognitive dysfunction syndrome caused by cerebrovascular diseases. Astragalus membranaceus (Fisch.) Bunge (AS) has antioxidative, gut microbiota-regulating, and cognitive-improving effects. Escherichia coli (E. coli) abundance is associated with cognitive dysfunction. This study explored the mechanism by which AS improves VD by regulating E. coli along the gut-brain axis, providing a basis for VD drug research and development. EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: VD models were established by permanent ligation of the common carotid artery. Morris water maze, Doppler cerebral blood flow measurement, blood lipid assays, pathological staining, Western blot, and ELISA were used to evaluate AS's protective effects on the brain. 16S rRNA sequencing analyzed gut microbiota to screen differential strains. Metabolomics screened endogenous differential metabolites. Oxygen-glucose deprivation (OGD) was established to evaluate 5-aminovaleric acid effects on neuronal mitochondrial function and oxidative stress. KEY RESULTS: AS significantly improved cognitive dysfunction, restored cerebral blood flow, and attenuated abnormal protein accumulation and oxidative stress in VD rat brains. Microbiota analysis revealed that AS inhibited E. coli proliferation and mitigated associated pathological damage. Furthermore, endogenous metabolite 5-aminovaleric acid alleviated OGD-induced neuronal damage and oxidative stress. CONCLUSION AND IMPLICATIONS: AS can treat cognitive dysfunction and brain injury in rodents, regulate gut microbiota balance, and reduce the contribution of E. coli. Meanwhile, AS-regulated endogenous metabolite 5-aminovaleric acid can also treat OGD-induced nerve cell injury. These findings suggest that AS may be a promising candidate for VD treatment and provide mechanistic insight into gut-brain axis regulation.

works.title: Repurposed catechol‐O‐methyltransferase inhibitors tolcapone and entacapone preferentially suppress aggregation and seeding of P301 mutant tau in human neuronal models
works.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Pathogenic aggregation and propagation of seed-competent TAU assemblies drive tauopathies. MAPT P301 mutations accelerate aggregation and enhance seed competence, yet pharmacological strategies selectively targeting these pathogenic species remain limited. We investigated whether the clinically approved catechol-O-methyltransferase inhibitors tolcapone (TOL) and entacapone (ENT) preferentially modulate mutant TAU aggregation and seeding. EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: TOL and ENT effects on TAU aggregation were evaluated via cell-free assays, surface plasmon resonance (SPR), and in silico docking. Functional consequences of compound-modified fibrils were assessed in mutant TAU-expressing SH-SY5Y cells. Translational relevance was examined in human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC)-derived neurons exposed to pathogenic K18 fibrils, followed by post-seeding compound treatment. KEY RESULTS: Both compounds dose-dependently inhibited TAU aggregation, exhibiting greater potency, stronger SPR binding affinities, and more favourable computed interaction energies for P301S mutant versus wild-type TAU. Fibrils formed with TOL or ENT induced less downstream TAU oligomerization and phosphorylation in SH-SY5Y cells, with TOL showing superior protection. In hiPSC-derived neurons, post-seeding treatment with either compound decreased fibril-induced, sarkosyl-insoluble, TAU aggregation and phosphorylation without overt cytotoxicity. CONCLUSION AND IMPLICATIONS: TOL and ENT preferentially reduced the aggregation and seeding of pathogenic P301 mutant TAU in the experimental models examined. These findings provide proof-of-concept support for mutation-focused pharmacological approaches and identify catechol scaffolds as starting points for developing more potent and safer TAU-directed compounds. Further studies are required to define the relevant molecular interactions, confirm the neuronal findings across additional hiPSC lines and determine whether effective CNS exposure can be achieved in vivo.

works.title: Editor’s pick: Bioptimus
Bioorthogonal chemistry conjugates: ADCs and beyond
works.abstract: Bioorthogonal click chemistry has played a transformative role in developing advanced hybrid conjugates. These molecular constructs are formed by chemically linking a targeting component to a functional moiety through a suitable linker. Therapeutic conjugates are designed to deliver a biologically active agent to a specific target to treat, prevent, or modify a disease process. By directing the payload to a defined site of action, these conjugates can improve efficacy while reducing off-target effects and systemic toxicity. Among these, antibody-drug conjugates stand out as the most clinically successful compounds. Where various chemical strategies, such as thiol-maleimide additions and site-selective glycan engineering, are employed to attach toxic payloads to antibodies with high precision and reduced sample heterogeneity. Beyond delivery of potent therapeutic payloads, click chemistry approaches have expanded into radioimmunoconjugates for diagnostics, oligonucleotide conjugates for gene silencing, and the creation of bispecific antibodies that can target multiple disease pathways simultaneously. These modular approaches often utilize combinations of ligation and chemical conjugation to preserve the structural integrity and immune functions of the original proteins. These techniques are now being applied to modulate living systems, including cell surface engineering, where metabolic machinery is exploited to install chemical handles on living cells for therapeutic tracking and "click-to-release" drug activation in vivo. Ultimately, current and emerging molecular "click" technologies emphasize a shift toward homogeneous, site-specific methods that expand the functionality and improve the stability, efficacy, and clinical potential of diverse bioconjugates to enhance the precision of modern medicine.

works.title: Molecular Insights into the Wet Granulation Mechanisms of Drugs with Different Solubilities
works.abstract: Wet granulation is an interfacial reconstruction process mediated by liquid binders. However, the mechanisms underlying the distinct granulation behaviors of drugs with different solubilities remain poorly understood due to a lack of molecular-level insight. Here, we elucidate these mechanisms using density functional theory (DFT) calculations and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. Three model drugs with distinct solubilitiesaminophylline (AMI), metformin hydrochloride (MET), and diclofenac sodium (SD)were selected. The results show that differences in granulation behavior cannot be attributed solely to solubility; rather, they arise from variations in interfacial interactions may be governed by crystal structure. Molecular simulations further reveal that crystal structure contributes to macroscopic granulation outcomes by regulating the dynamics of interfacial water molecules.

works.title: An interpretable AI model decodes the rules of cell recruitment to specific destinations
Interaction with NEGR1 affects mGlu 5 cell signalling and the neuroprotection induced by the positive allosteric modulator VU0409551
works.abstract: Abstract Background and Purpose The metabotropic glutamate receptor mGlu 5 plays an important role in neuronal survival and synaptic plasticity. We and others have shown that mGlu 5 positive allosteric modulators (PAMs) are biased agonists, triggering the activation of neuroprotective pathways and promoting neuronal survival. As mGlu 5 biased pharmacology arises from drug‐induced interactions with different protein partners, in this study, we analysed the mGlu 5 interactome to identify novel binding partners capable of modulating receptor cell signalling. Experimental Approach To identify new mGlu 5 partners, we employed mass spectrometry, followed by co‐immunoprecipitation experiments, which confirmed the interaction between mGlu 5 and the neuronal growth regulator 1 (NEGR1), a cell adhesion molecule. We next evaluated how NEGR1 affects mGlu 5 cell signalling and cellular distribution using lentivirus transduction on primary neuronal cultures to knockdown NEGR1 expression. We also assessed whether NEGR1 plays a role in the neuroprotective effects of the mGlu5 PAM, VU0409551, by evaluating apoptotic cell death and neurite degeneration. Key Results The interaction between NEGR1 and mGlu 5 is important for mGlu 5 synaptic localization and for its coupling with Homer, thereby modulating cell signalling pathways activated by mGlu 5 receptors. For instance, NEGR1 knockdown led to decreased mGlu 5 ‐dependent activation of ERK1/2 and reduced expression of ARC/ARG3.1 and BDNF. Importantly, NEGR1 knockdown affected mGlu 5 pharmacology, as the neuroprotective effect of VU0409551 was not observed in neurons expressing low levels of NEGR1. Conclusions and Implications These results indicate that NEGR1 is essential for mGlu 5 ‐biased activation of neuroprotective cell signalling pathways and for the neuroprotective effects triggered by VU0409551.

works.title: Issue Information
Preparation quality and epitranscriptomic modification influence circular RNA vaccine performance
works.abstract: Circular RNA (circRNA) is an emerging vaccine modality that is proposed to improve stability, reduce reactogenicity and extend antigen expression compared with linear mRNA. However, the relative contributions to vaccine performance of its covalently closed structure, its preparation quality and nucleotide modifications remain poorly described. Here, we systematically dissected these parameters in vivo across two antigen systems. We identified RNA preparation quality as a major contributor to markers of circRNA reactogenicity, with innate immune activation tracking with the abundance of residual low molecular weight RNA species in less refined preparations. High-quality circRNA exhibited markedly reduced innate immune activation compared with linear mRNA, independent of nucleotide modification. Despite these differences, circRNA and mRNA vaccines elicited comparable antibody titres and T cell responses, indicating that reduced innate activation did not translate into enhanced adaptive immune magnitude. Incorporating N 6 -methyladenosine (m 6 A) did not affect markers of reactogenicity or antigen expression but was associated with increased antibody avidity across both antigen systems, with neutralisation trending in the same direction. CircRNA vaccination also altered the anatomical distribution of germinal centre responses, reducing splenic antigen-specific germinal centre B cells at the measured timepoint while preserving lymph node responses. Together, these findings indicate that circRNA vaccine performance is shaped by RNA preparation quality and epitranscriptomic modification, rather than differences in innate immune activation.

works.title: Rational engineering of Omp34 loop-based immunogen enhances protection against Colistin-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii
works.abstract: The surface antigens are promising immunogenic targets for vaccine development and immunotherapies. Here, the loop3 to loop7 (L3-L7) region of the Omp34 from Acinetobacter baumannii was evaluated. A DNA fragment encoding the L3-L7 region was amplified from the Omp34 gene. The structures of ΔL5/5Gly-L3-L7 and ΔL5/Acr-L3-L7 were achieved through the modification of the loop 5 sequence in the L3-L7 of Omp34. Optimization of Omp34 loop epitopes via Acr sequence linkage was performed. Omp34, L3-L7 region, ΔL5/5Gly-L3-L7 and ΔL5/Acr-L3-L7 were recombinantly expressed. Mice immunized with the purified antigens, were infected with the clinical isolate of A. baumannii 58ST. Active immunizations with ΔL5/Acr-L3-L7, L3-L7, Omp34 and ΔL5/5Gly-L3-L7 resulted in 75%, 50%, 37.5% and 37.5% survival rates, respectively. Passive immunization with sera from these antigens in the same order results in survival rates of 62.5%, 37.5%, 25% and 25%, respectively. Anti-ΔL5/Acr-L3-L7 sera mediated the greatest opsonophagocytic killing activity. In addition, active and passive immunizations with ΔL5/Acr-L3-L7 resulted in the highest bacterial clearance in the lung, spleen, and liver. These findings suggest that the L3-L7 region of Omp34 is an appropriate scaffold and antigen against A. baumannii , in which replacing loop 5 with the Acr sequence could enhance its antigenicity and protectivity.

works.title: Theoretical Quantification of Cargo Effective Diffusivity in Affinity-Based Hydrogels
works.abstract: Affinity hydrogels enable precise control of cargo release kinetics through specific, non-covalent interactions between the functionalized polymer network and therapeutic agents. Yet, how these interactions integrate with steric hindrance in the crosslinked network to determine cargo diffusivity, a critical kinetic parameter governing cargo-controlled release, remains poorly quantified. Here, we present a theoretical framework that explicitly bridges microscopic cargo-polymer interactions with macroscopic cargo release kinetics. Specifically, our approach delineates cargo diffusivity into two principal contributions: (i) binding interactions and (ii) steric hindrance, enabling a quantitative understanding of their interplay in defining cargo release performance. Increasing binding interactions, attractively, reduce diffusivity in a reverse sigmoidal fashion, transitioning from a steric- to a binding-controlled regime. Overall, we demonstrate how the interplay of microscopic forces governs cargo diffusivity within affinity hydrogels and, in turn, regulates cumulative cargo release at the macroscopic level, thereby bridging microscopic thermodynamic interactions with macroscopic cargo release kinetics, quantitatively.

works.title: PET Imaging of Dual GLP-1R and GIPR Targeting with [18F]AlF-NOTA-Asp2-Tirzepatide
works.abstract: Tirzepatide is a clinical dual GLP-1R and GIPR agonist for type 2 diabetes and obesity, and non-invasive approaches to assess its in vivo biodistribution and systemic toxicity in living animals remain limited. Both receptors also serve as potential targets for neuroendocrine tumor imaging, and dual-target PET probes for simultaneous GLP-1R and GIPR detection are still lacking. Herein, we developed a novel PET probe [18F]AlF-NOTA-Asp2-tirzepatide via structural modification of tirzepatide. This probe successfully visualized the in vivo distribution of tirzepatide, which was primarily eliminated through the renal system. The C20 fatty diacid moiety caused elevated uptake in the heart, liver and blood due to enhanced albumin binding. In vitro assays verified its reliable GLP-1R and moderate GIPR binding affinity. Persistent tumor accumulation was observed in INS-1 and A549-GIPR xenografts, allowing effective tumor visualization. In summary, [18F]AlF-NOTA-Asp2-tirzepatide features facile radiolabeling and enables the clear visualization of tirzepatide in vivo, along with favorable dual-targeting performance, while excessive non-target uptake still needs to be optimized for further clinical translation.

works.title: Monoclonal Antibody Coformulations Reveal Three Interaction Patterns Governing Stability
works.abstract: Coformulated monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) offer a promising next-generation therapeutic strategy by combining multiple antibodies in a single drug product to enhance efficacy and improve patient compliance. However, ensuring the quality and stability of individual components in combination remains a key challenge. Here, we systematically characterized ten IgG1 mAbs (eight low-viscosity and two high-viscosity mAbs at 150 mg/mL) and all 45 possible 1:1 binary coformulations. Viscosity measurements revealed three distinct cross-interaction patterns: (1) minimal cross-interaction, where coformulation viscosity fell between those of the parental mAbs; (2) attractive cross-interaction, characterized by viscosity above both parental mAbs; and (3) repulsive cross-interaction, characterized by viscosity below both parental mAbs. Among the two high-viscosity mAbs, one exhibited reduced viscosity when coformulated with low-viscosity mAbs, whereas the other exhibited increased viscosity. Diffusion interaction parameter (kD) measurements showed partial correspondence with the observed interaction patterns, although kD did not consistently align with the viscosity trends across all coformulation pairs. In parallel, conformational stability was assessed using thermal unfolding parameters, including onset temperature (Tonset) and the first unfolding transition temperature (Tm1). Most coformulations exhibited thermal unfolding parameters intermediate between those of their parental mAbs, often shifting toward the less conformationally stable parent, indicating that conformational stability was generally retained following coformulation. This study represents one of the most comprehensive investigations of antibody coformulations to date and, to our knowledge, is the first to report repulsive interactions, particularly in the context of high-concentration viscosity. These findings highlight fundamental protein-protein interaction patterns that govern antibody coformulations, expand the knowledge base for the development of stable next-generation antibody combination therapies, and provide a rich experimental dataset to guide future computational modeling of mAb-mAb coformulation behavior.

works.title: Fatty Acids for the Treatment of Ocular Diseases and Ocular Drug Delivery
works.abstract: The intricate anatomical and physiological barriers of the eye severely limit the bioavailability of conventional topical therapies, necessitating innovative strategies. In this review, fatty acids are presented as versatile agents functioning in two distinct roles. As bioactive lipids, specific fatty acids exert disease-modifying effects, offering novel pharmacological interventions for ocular surface and posterior segment disorders, including dry eye syndrome, uveitis, and retinal degeneration. Concurrently, beyond their biological activity, fatty acids serve as structural components in formulation design; their physicochemical properties, particularly varying chain lengths and degrees of unsaturation, enable the construction of advanced ocular drug delivery systems with substantially enhanced ocular bioavailability. Crucially, this review not only summarizes the translational prospects of fatty acid-based therapeutics but also highlights the structure-activity relationships governing the in vivo performance of fatty acid-integrated delivery systems. By delineating these dual functionalities, we provide a clear framework for distinguishing nutritional or pharmacological supplementation from excipient or carrier design, thereby facilitating the rational development of next-generation ophthalmic formulations.

works.title: Engineering monocytes and macrophages for therapeutic control
Cross-protection of wildtype and vaccine-derived chikungunya virus antibodies against chikungunya and Mayaro viruses in mice
works.abstract: Abstract The live-attenuated vaccine IXCHIQ against chikungunya virus (CHIKV) was approved in 2023, with its efficacy evaluated using human neutralizing antibody titers as surrogate effectiveness criterion. Previous in vivo studies assessed its efficacy at high CHIKV-specific antibody titers, whereas its efficacy and antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE) risks at suboptimal levels mimicking long-term immunity remain poorly characterized. Here, we assessed antibody-mediated protection following vaccination or natural infection by passively immunizing transiently immunocompromised mice with graded doses of pooled immune sera before challenge with two CHIKV genotypes or the related Mayaro virus (MAYV). Protection was evaluated using viral loads at 3 days post-infection and clinical parameters. Vaccine- and infection-induced antibodies conferred strong protection against both CHIKV genotypes, even at antibody concentrations nearing ELISA detection limits. In contrast, protection against MAYV required higher titers. We observed no ADE. Our findings align with previous studies supporting durable protection against CHIKV and partial cross-protection against MAYV.
